nodes.title: The Index
nodes.heading: 37.3.2 The Index
nodes.start_phrase: The return of the Alerian ETNs is linked to the performance of the Index.
nodes.summary:
- Defines “holders” as registered owners on the issuer’s or trustee’s books (not beneficial owners in street name) and points to a “Certain Defined Terms” section for capitalized terms.
- Describes the Index to which the Alerian ETNs are linked: a float-adjusted, market-capitalization index of energy-oriented MLPs, calculated by S&P Dow Jones Indices LLC (Index Calculation Agent) in consultation with GKD Index Partners, LLC (Index Sponsor). MLPs are partnerships engaged in exploration, marketing, mining, processing, production, refining, storage, or transportation of minerals/natural resources.
- Sets denominations: U.S. dollar notes with a minimum Principal Amount of $19.03661 per note, equal to the Initial VWAP Level divided by ten.
- Details coupon mechanics: on each Coupon Payment Date, holders receive a cash Coupon Amount equal to the Reference Distribution Amount minus the Accrued Tracking Fee.
- Accrued Tracking Fee: accrues daily at 0.85% per annum on the Daily Note Value as of the Index Business Day preceding the Coupon Valuation Date. Daily Note Value reflects cumulative performance of the Index’s VWAP Level since April 1, 2009 and is published on Bloomberg (AMJIVWAP; AMJIVWAP:IND).
- Explains VWAP Level: weighted VWAPs of Index Components; each component’s VWAP is the volume-weighted average price on its Primary Exchange as determined by the VWAP Calculation Agent.
- Outlines shortfall handling: if the Reference Distribution Amount is less than the Accrued Tracking Fee, no coupon is paid; the difference (Tracking Fee Shortfall) is carried forward and added to the next period’s Accrued Tracking Fee, with continued 0.85% accrual, repeating until distributions exceed fees. Coupons are paid quarterly in arrears on the fifteenth Index Business Day after each Coupon Valuation Date; the final coupon is paid at maturity and included in the Cash Settlement Amount.
- Notes interim accrual publication: the Note Calculation Agent computes and publishes a daily interim accrued Coupon Amount on Bloomberg (AMJEU; AMJEU:IND), though coupons are only paid quarterly.
- Provides early repurchase option: subject to procedures and potential postponements for Market Disruption Events, holders may submit a repurchase request once per week, generally by 11:00 a.m. New York City time on Thursday.

nodes.title: Denominations
nodes.heading: 37.3.3 Denominations
nodes.start_phrase: The Alerian ETNs are denominated in U.S. dollars in minimum denominations equal to the $19.03661 per note (the “Principal Amount”), which is the amount equal to the Initial VWAP Level (defined below), divided by ten.
nodes.summary:
- Defines “holders” as registered owners of the Alerian ETNs on the issuer’s or trustee’s books (not beneficial owners in street name), and points to a “Certain Defined Terms” section for capitalized terms.
- Index linkage: ETN returns track an Index measuring the composite performance of energy-oriented MLPs; calculated by S&P Dow Jones Indices LLC (Index Calculation Agent) in consultation with GKD Index Partners, LLC (Index Sponsor) using a float-adjusted, market capitalization methodology. MLPs span exploration, marketing, mining, processing, production, refining, storage, or transportation of minerals/natural resources.
- Denominations: U.S. dollar notes in minimum denominations equal to the $19.03661 Principal Amount, set as the Initial VWAP Level divided by ten.
- Coupon mechanics: On each Coupon Payment Date, holders receive a Coupon Amount equal to the Reference Distribution Amount minus the Accrued Tracking Fee, both measured as of the corresponding Coupon Valuation Date. Coupons are paid quarterly in arrears on the fifteenth Index Business Day after each Coupon Valuation Date; the final Coupon Amount is paid on the Maturity Date and included in the Cash Settlement Amount.
- Accrued Tracking Fee: Accrues daily at 0.85% per annum on the Daily Note Value as of the Index Business Day immediately preceding the Coupon Valuation Date. The Daily Note Value reflects cumulative performance of the Index’s VWAP Level since the April 1, 2009 Inception Date and is published on Bloomberg (AMJIVWAP; AMJIVWAP:IND).
- VWAP Level: On any Index Business Day, reflects weighted VWAPs of the Index Components; each component’s VWAP is determined by the VWAP Calculation Agent based on its Primary Exchange.
- Shortfall handling: If the Reference Distribution Amount is less than the Accrued Tracking Fee for a period, no coupon is paid; the difference (Tracking Fee Shortfall) is carried forward and added to the next period’s Accrued Tracking Fee, with the 0.85% per annum accrual continuing. This process may repeat across quarters.
- Interim accruals: An interim accrued Coupon Amount is calculated daily (treating the prior Index Business Day as a Coupon Valuation Date) and published on Bloomberg (AMJEU; AMJEU:IND); actual coupons are calculated and paid only quarterly.
- Early repurchase: Holders may submit repurchase requests once a week (generally by 11:00 a.m. New York time on Thursday), subject to specified procedures and potential postponements/adjustments for Market Disruption Events.

nodes.title: Coupon Payments and the Accrued Tracking Fee
nodes.heading: 37.3.4 Coupon Payments and the Accrued Tracking Fee
nodes.start_phrase: For each Alerian ETN a holder holds on the applicable Coupon Record Date, holders will receive on each Coupon Payment Date the “Coupon Amount,” which is an amount in cash equal to the difference between (a) the Reference Distribution Amount (defined below), calculated as of the corresponding Coupon Valuation Date and (b) the Accrued Tracking Fee (defined below), calculated as of the corresponding Coupon Valuation Date.
nodes.summary:
- Defines “holders” as those registered on the issuer’s or Trustee’s books, not beneficial owners in street name.
- Index linkage: ETN returns tied to an index of energy-oriented MLPs; calculated by S&P Dow Jones Indices (Index Calculation Agent) with GKD Index Partners (Index Sponsor), using a float-adjusted market-cap methodology. VWAP Level is based on volume‑weighted average prices on each component’s Primary Exchange.
- Denominations: U.S. dollar notes with a Principal Amount of $19.03661 per note, equal to the Initial VWAP Level divided by 10.
- Coupon mechanics: Quarterly Coupon Amount equals Reference Distribution Amount minus Accrued Tracking Fee. The Tracking Fee accrues daily at 0.85% per annum on the Daily Note Value (which reflects cumulative VWAP performance since April 1, 2009). If Reference Distribution is less than the fee, no coupon is paid and the shortfall carries forward. Final coupon is paid at maturity and included in the Cash Settlement Amount.
- Published data: Daily Note Value and VWAP Level published on Bloomberg (AMJIVWAP / AMJIVWAP:IND). Interim accrued coupon published daily (AMJEU / AMJEU:IND); actual coupons paid quarterly.
- Early repurchase: Holders may request weekly repurchases (minimum 50,000 notes). Repurchase Amount equals Principal Amount adjusted for index return (Initial to Final VWAP Level over a five‑day Repurchase Measurement Period), less Accrued Tracking Fee and a Repurchase Fee, plus adjustments for certain accrued but unpaid coupon-related distributions. Final VWAP Level is the arithmetic mean of the five measurement days.
- Repurchase Fee: 0.125% of Principal Amount, adjusted for index return, Accrued Tracking Fee, and certain distributions during the measurement period; varies accordingly.
- Risk note: Holders may lose some or all of their investment upon early repurchase if index performance does not offset fees.
- Repurchase process and deadlines: Submit Repurchase Notice via email by 11:00 a.m. (NYC time) on the Business Day before the Repurchase Valuation Date (generally Thursday); receive and return signed Repurchase Confirmation by 4:00 p.m. via fax; arrange DTC delivery versus payment at the Repurchase Amount on the Repurchase Valuation Date; complete DTC settlement by 10:00 a.m. (NYC time) on the Repurchase Date. Brokerage firms may impose earlier internal deadlines.

nodes.title: Payment Upon Early Repurchase
nodes.heading: 37.3.5 Payment Upon Early Repurchase
nodes.start_phrase: Subject to a holder's compliance with the procedures and the potential postponements and adjustments as described under “Market Disruption Events” below, that holder may submit a request once a week (generally on or before 11:00 a.m., New York City time, on Thursday) during the term of the Alerian ETNs to have us repurchase that holder's Alerian ETNs, provided that holder requests that we repurchase a minimum of 50,000 Alerian ETNs.
nodes.summary:
- Describes the issuer’s weekly early repurchase feature for Alerian ETNs, subject to a minimum aggregate size of 50,000 ETNs and specific notification/settlement procedures.
- Repurchase Amount: cash paid per ETN on the Repurchase Date; can be $0 if the calculated amount is ≤ $0; not known at the time of request because it depends on a five-day Repurchase Measurement Period that begins after the request.
- Calculation of Repurchase Amount: principal adjusted by (a) the Index return from Initial VWAP Level to Final VWAP Level, (b) deduction of the Accrued Tracking Fee, (c) deduction of the Repurchase Fee, and (d) addition of accrued but unpaid coupon-related amounts, including:
  - The prior Coupon Amount if its ex-date has not occurred by the last Index Business Day in the measurement period,
  - An Adjusted Coupon Amount for certain cash distributions with ex-dates from the prior Coupon Valuation Date through the Repurchase Valuation Date (less Accrued Tracking Fee),
  - Certain cash distributions with ex-dates during the measurement period.
- Final VWAP Level: arithmetic mean of VWAP Levels on each Index Business Day in the five-day Repurchase Measurement Period, determined by the VWAP Calculation Agent.
- Repurchase Fee Amount: equals 0.125% of principal, adjusted for Index return, Accrued Tracking Fee, and certain cash distributions during the measurement period; therefore varies with performance and fees.
- Risk disclosure: holders may lose some or all of their investment upon early repurchase, particularly if the Final VWAP Level is at or below the Initial VWAP Level or does not exceed it enough to offset the Accrued Tracking Fee and Repurchase Fee.
- Repurchase process and deadlines (through the holder’s broker/custodian):
  - Email Repurchase Notice to ETN_Repurchase@jpmorgan.com by 11:00 a.m. New York time on the Business Day immediately preceding the Repurchase Valuation Date (generally Thursday).
  - Issuer sends a Repurchase Confirmation in response.
  - Holder returns a signed Repurchase Confirmation via fax to (917) 456-3471 by 4:00 p.m. New York time the same Business Day; receipt must be acknowledged to be effective.
  - DTC custodian books a delivery-versus-payment trade on the Repurchase Valuation Date at the Repurchase Amount.
  - Settlement via DTC by 10:00 a.m. New York time on the Repurchase Date.
- Notes that brokerage firms may have their own, earlier internal deadlines and reiterates the need to meet the issuer’s 11:00 a.m./4:00 p.m. cutoffs.

nodes.title: Repurchase Requirements
nodes.heading: 37.3.6 Repurchase Requirements
nodes.start_phrase: To exercise the right to have us repurchase a holder's Alerian ETNs on a weekly basis, that holder must instruct that holder's broker or other person through whom that holder holds the Alerian ETNs to take the following steps:
nodes.summary:
- Covers early weekly repurchase mechanics for Alerian ETNs, how the Repurchase Amount and Repurchase Fee are calculated, operational requirements and deadlines, risks of loss, payment at maturity, the roles of calculation agents, VWAP determinations, and handling of market disruptions.
- Minimum early repurchase size: 50,000 ETNs. Holders won’t know the Repurchase Amount when electing repurchase because it depends on a subsequent five-day measurement period.
- Repurchase Amount: Principal Amount adjusted by (a) index return from Initial VWAP Level to Final VWAP Level; (b) minus Accrued Tracking Fee; (c) minus Repurchase Fee; (d) plus coupon-related adjustments, including (i) the prior Coupon Amount if its ex-date has not yet occurred by the last day of the Repurchase Measurement Period, (ii) an Adjusted Coupon Amount reflecting certain cash distributions between the prior Coupon Valuation Date and the Repurchase Valuation Date (less Accrued Tracking Fee), and (iii) certain cash distributions during the Repurchase Measurement Period. Final VWAP Level is the arithmetic mean of VWAP Levels over the five Index Business Day Repurchase Measurement Period.
- Repurchase Fee Amount: 0.125% of Principal Amount, adjusted by index return, Accrued Tracking Fee, and certain cash distributions during the Repurchase Measurement Period; therefore, it varies with index performance and distributions.
- Loss risk on early repurchase: Holders may lose some or all of their investment; if Repurchase Amount is ≤ $0, payment is $0. Loss is likely if the Final VWAP Level does not exceed the Initial VWAP Level by enough to offset the Accrued Tracking Fee and Repurchase Fee.
- Repurchase Requirements (weekly process and deadlines, generally before a Thursday Repurchase Valuation Date): 
  - Email Repurchase Notice to ETN_Repurchase@jpmorgan.com by 11:00 a.m. New York time on the Business Day before the Repurchase Valuation Date.
  - Receive Repurchase Confirmation from issuer, then return signed confirmation via fax to (917) 456-3471 by 4:00 p.m. the same day (receipt must be acknowledged).
  - Instruct DTC custodian to book a DvP trade at the Repurchase Amount on the Repurchase Valuation Date and settle via DTC by 10:00 a.m. New York time on the Repurchase Date.
  - Brokerage firms may have earlier internal cutoffs; late or incomplete submissions are ineffective. The Note Calculation Agent has sole discretion to resolve validity/timing questions. Once given, a Repurchase Notice is irrevocable.
- Expiration of repurchase rights: If the notice (by 11:00 a.m.) or confirmation (by 4:00 p.m.) is not timely on the Business Day before the Repurchase Valuation Date, the repurchase will not occur. Validly confirmed notices are irrevocable.
- Payment at Maturity: Cash Settlement Amount per ETN equals Principal Amount adjusted by (a) index return from Initial to Final VWAP Level; (b) plus final Coupon Amount, if any; (c) minus Accrued Tracking Fee; (d) plus certain cash distributions with ex-dates during the Final Measurement Period. If ≤ $0, payment is $0. Final Measurement Period is five Index Business Days near maturity; Final VWAP Level is the mean VWAP over that period. Initial VWAP Level is the mean VWAP over the three Index Business Days ending on the Inception Date. Holders may lose some or all principal at maturity if index performance does not offset tracking fees.
- Calculation agents: JPMS is the Note Calculation Agent for all necessary calculations other than VWAP determinations. The JPMorgan Global Index Research Group acts as the VWAP Calculation Agent on non-Disrupted Days, determining component VWAPs, the VWAP Level, and the Final VWAP Level.
- Market Disruption Events: If a Disrupted Day affects an Index Component on an Averaging Date, the VWAP and published share weighting for that component are deferred to the next non-Disrupted Day (Deferred Averaging Date) for that component, even if that day was originally scheduled as an Averaging Date; only the affected component is deferred.

nodes.title: Expiration of Repurchase Rights
nodes.heading: 37.3.7 Expiration of Repurchase Rights
nodes.start_phrase: If we do not receive a holder's Repurchase Notice by 11:00 a.m., New York City time (as described under the first bullet point in “Repurchase Requirements” above), or a holder's Repurchase Confirmation by 4:00 p.m., New York City time (as described under the third bullet point in “Repurchase Requirements” above) on the Business Day immediately preceding the applicable Repurchase Valuation Date (generally Thursday), that holder's Repurchase Notice will not be effective and we will not repurchase that holder's Alerian ETNs on the relevant Repurchase Date.
nodes.summary:
- Repurchase process and deadlines: A Repurchase Notice must be received by 11:00 a.m. and a Repurchase Confirmation by 4:00 p.m. (New York City time) on the Business Day immediately preceding the applicable Repurchase Valuation Date (generally Thursday). Missing either deadline renders the notice ineffective and no repurchase will occur on the relevant Repurchase Date. Once submitted, a Repurchase Notice is irrevocable. The Note Calculation Agent has sole discretion to resolve questions about notice validity, timing, and required deliveries.
- Expiration of repurchase rights: If the required notice/confirmation times are not met, repurchase rights for that cycle lapse; any properly confirmed Repurchase Notice is irrevocable.
- Payment at maturity: Unless earlier repurchased, each Alerian ETN pays a Cash Settlement Amount at maturity, which may be zero if the calculated amount is less than or equal to zero.
- Cash Settlement Amount components: Principal Amount adjusted by (a) Index return from Initial VWAP Level to Final VWAP Level, (b) addition of any final Coupon Amount, (c) deduction of the Accrued Tracking Fee, and (d) addition of certain cash distributions on Index Components with ex-dividend dates during the Final Measurement Period.
- Measurement periods and levels: The Final Measurement Period is a five Index Business Day window near maturity. The Final VWAP Level is the arithmetic mean of VWAP Levels across those days. The Initial VWAP Level is the arithmetic mean of VWAP Levels over the three Index Business Days ending on the Inception Date.
- Risk disclosure: Investors may lose some or all of their principal at maturity, particularly if the Final VWAP Level is below the Initial VWAP Level or not sufficiently higher to offset the Accrued Tracking Fee.
- Roles of calculation agents: J.P. Morgan Securities LLC (JPMS) is the Note Calculation Agent responsible for all necessary calculations and determinations other than those assigned to the VWAP Calculation Agent. The JPMorgan Global Index Research Group, an affiliate, is the VWAP Calculation Agent, determining component VWAPs, VWAP Levels, and the Final VWAP Level on non-Disrupted Days.
- Market disruption handling: If a Disrupted Day affects an Index Component on an Averaging Date, its VWAP and published share weighting for that date are deferred to the next Index Business Day that is not disrupted (the Deferred Averaging Date), on a component-by-component basis, even if that day was originally an Averaging Date.

nodes.title: Payment at Maturity
nodes.heading: 37.3.8 Payment at Maturity
nodes.start_phrase: For each Alerian ETN, unless earlier repurchased, holders will receive at maturity a cash payment equal to the Cash Settlement Amount.
nodes.summary:
- Repurchase process and deadlines:
  - A Repurchase Notice must be received by 11:00 a.m. New York City time and the Repurchase Confirmation by 4:00 p.m. New York City time on the Business Day immediately preceding the applicable Repurchase Valuation Date (generally Thursday), or the notice is ineffective and no repurchase will occur on the relevant Repurchase Date.
  - Once submitted, a Repurchase Notice is irrevocable; any notice accompanied by a valid confirmation is irrevocable.
  - The Note Calculation Agent has sole discretion to resolve questions about the validity and timing of Repurchase Notices and required deliveries.

- Payment at maturity:
  - If not earlier repurchased, each Alerian ETN pays a Cash Settlement Amount at maturity; if this amount is $0 or less, the payment is $0.
  - Cash Settlement Amount adjustments include:
    - Index return from the Initial VWAP Level to the Final VWAP Level,
    - Addition of the final coupon, if any,
    - Deduction of the Accrued Tracking Fee,
    - Addition of certain cash distributions on Index Components with ex-dividend dates during the Final Measurement Period.
  - Risk: Because the Accrued Tracking Fee reduces the payout, holders may lose some or all of their investment if the Final VWAP Level is not sufficiently above the Initial VWAP Level.

- VWAP levels and measurement periods:
  - Final Measurement Period: five Index Business Days near maturity.
  - Final VWAP Level: arithmetic mean of daily VWAP Levels over the Final Measurement Period.
  - Initial VWAP Level: arithmetic mean of VWAP Levels over a three-day period ending on the Inception Date.
  - The VWAP Calculation Agent determines VWAPs and VWAP Levels.

- Roles of calculation agents:
  - J.P. Morgan Securities LLC (JPMS) is the Note Calculation Agent responsible for all required calculations and determinations other than those assigned to the VWAP Calculation Agent.
  - The JPMorgan Global Index Research Group acts as the VWAP Calculation Agent on each non-Disrupted Day, determining VWAPs for Index Components, the VWAP Level, and the Final VWAP Level.

- Market disruption handling:
  - If an Index Component experiences a Disrupted Day on an Averaging Date, its VWAP and published share weighting for that date are determined on the next Index Business Day that is not a Disrupted Day (the Deferred Averaging Date), even if this falls on a date originally scheduled as an Averaging Date.
  - This postponement applies for determining VWAP Levels during the Final Measurement Period and the Repurchase Measurement Period.

nodes.title: Note Calculation Agent
nodes.heading: 37.3.9 Note Calculation Agent
nodes.start_phrase: J.P. Morgan Securities LLC, or JPMS (the “Note Calculation Agent”), will make all necessary calculations and determinations in connection with the Alerian ETNs, including calculations and determinations relating to any payments on the Alerian ETNs, other those to be made by the VWAP Calculation Agent described below.
nodes.summary:
- Repurchase process and deadlines: Holders must submit a Repurchase Notice by 11:00 a.m. and a Repurchase Confirmation by 4:00 p.m. (New York City time) on the Business Day immediately preceding the applicable Repurchase Valuation Date (generally Thursday). If either deadline is missed, the notice is ineffective and the ETNs will not be repurchased on the related Repurchase Date. Valid repurchase submissions are irrevocable.
- Calculation agent authority: The Note Calculation Agent (J.P. Morgan Securities LLC) has sole discretion to determine the validity and timing of Repurchase Notices and required deliveries and to make all calculations and determinations for the ETNs other than those assigned to the VWAP Calculation Agent.
- Payment at maturity: Unless repurchased earlier, each ETN pays a Cash Settlement Amount at maturity, which may be $0 if the calculation results are $0 or less.
- Cash Settlement Amount components: Starts with the Principal Amount and is adjusted by (a) the Index’s return from Initial VWAP Level to Final VWAP Level, (b) addition of the final Coupon Amount (if any), (c) deduction of the Accrued Tracking Fee, and (d) addition of certain cash distributions on Index Components with ex-dividend dates during the Final Measurement Period.
- Measurement periods and VWAP levels: The Final Measurement Period is five Index Business Days near maturity. The Final VWAP Level is the arithmetic mean of daily VWAP Levels over that period; the Initial VWAP Level is the arithmetic mean over a three-day period ending on the Inception Date. The VWAP Calculation Agent (JPMorgan Global Index Research Group) determines daily VWAPs, VWAP Levels, and the Final VWAP Level on non-Disrupted Days.
- Risk of loss: Investors may lose some or all of their investment at maturity, especially if the Final VWAP Level is below the Initial VWAP Level or does not exceed it by enough to offset the Accrued Tracking Fee.
- Market disruption handling: If a Disrupted Day occurs for an Index Component on an Averaging Date, the VWAP and share weighting for that component are determined on the next Index Business Day that is not disrupted (the Deferred Averaging Date), even if that falls on a date originally scheduled as an Averaging Date.

nodes.title: VWAP Calculation Agent
nodes.heading: 37.3.10 VWAP Calculation Agent
nodes.start_phrase: The JPMorgan Global Index Research Group (the “VWAP Calculation Agent”), one of our affiliates, will on each day that is not a Disrupted Day (as defined below) act as the VWAP Calculation Agent.
nodes.summary:
- Repurchase process and deadlines:
  - Holders must submit a Repurchase Notice by 11:00 a.m. and a Repurchase Confirmation by 4:00 p.m., New York City time, on the Business Day immediately before the applicable Repurchase Valuation Date (generally Thursday).
  - If either deadline is missed, the notice is ineffective and the ETNs will not be repurchased on the intended Repurchase Date.
  - Once given (with a valid confirmation), a Repurchase Notice is irrevocable.
  - The Note Calculation Agent has sole discretion to determine the validity and timing of Repurchase Notices and required deliveries.

- Expiration of repurchase rights:
  - Restates that failure to meet the specified timing for notice and confirmation voids the repurchase for that cycle.
  - Validly confirmed repurchase instructions cannot be revoked.

- Payment at maturity and Cash Settlement Amount:
  - Unless earlier repurchased, each ETN pays a Cash Settlement Amount at maturity; if this amount is $0 or less, the payment is $0.
  - Cash Settlement Amount adjusts the Principal Amount by:
    a) the Index return from Initial VWAP Level to Final VWAP Level,
    b) adding the final Coupon Amount (if any),
    c) deducting the Accrued Tracking Fee,
    d) adding certain cash distributions on Index Components with ex-dividend dates during the Final Measurement Period.
  - Final Measurement Period: five Index Business Days near maturity used to determine the Final VWAP Level.
  - Final VWAP Level: arithmetic mean of daily VWAP Levels over the Final Measurement Period; Initial VWAP Level: arithmetic mean of daily VWAP Levels over the three Index Business Days ending on the Inception Date.
  - Risk disclosure: holders may lose some or all principal at maturity, particularly if the Final VWAP Level is not sufficiently above the Initial VWAP Level to offset the Accrued Tracking Fee.

- Calculation agents and responsibilities:
  - Note Calculation Agent: J.P. Morgan Securities LLC (JPMS) performs all necessary calculations and determinations for the ETNs other than those assigned to the VWAP Calculation Agent.
  - VWAP Calculation Agent: JPMorgan Global Index Research Group determines daily VWAPs of Index Components, VWAP Levels, and Final VWAP Levels on days that are not Disrupted Days.

- Market disruption events and averaging adjustments:
  - If a Disrupted Day occurs for an Index Component on an Averaging Date, the VWAP and share weighting for that component are determined on the next Index Business Day that is not disrupted (Deferred Averaging Date), even if that date was originally an Averaging Date.
  - Clarifies treatment of postponed calculations for determining VWAP Levels during the Final Measurement Period and the Repurchase Measurement Period.

nodes.title: Market Disruption Events
nodes.heading: 37.3.11 Market Disruption Events
nodes.start_phrase: To the extent a Disrupted Day (as defined below) exists with respect to an Index Component on an Averaging Date (as defined below), the VWAP and published share weighting with respect to such Index Component (and only with respect to such Index Component) for such Averaging Date will be determined by the Note Calculation Agent or one of its affiliates on the first succeeding Index Business Day that is not a Disrupted Day (the “Deferred Averaging Date”) with respect to such Index Component irrespective of whether pursuant to such determination, the Deferred Averaging Date would fall on a date originally scheduled to be an Averaging Date.
nodes.summary:
- Repurchase process and deadlines:
  - Holders must submit a Repurchase Notice by 11:00 a.m. New York City time and a Repurchase Confirmation by 4:00 p.m. New York City time on the Business Day immediately before the applicable Repurchase Valuation Date (generally Thursday), or the notice is ineffective and no repurchase occurs on the related Repurchase Date.
  - Once submitted, a Repurchase Notice is irrevocable. The Note Calculation Agent has sole discretion to determine the validity, timing, and completion of required deliveries.

- Payment at maturity:
  - Unless previously repurchased, each Alerian ETN pays a Cash Settlement Amount at maturity; if this amount is $0 or less, the payment is $0.
  - Cash Settlement Amount adjusts the Principal Amount by: (a) index return from Initial VWAP Level to Final VWAP Level; (b) addition of the final coupon, if any; (c) deduction of the Accrued Tracking Fee; and (d) addition of certain cash distributions on Index Components with ex-dividend dates during the Final Measurement Period.
  - Investors may lose some or all of their investment; losses are likely if the Final VWAP Level does not exceed the Initial VWAP Level by enough to offset the Accrued Tracking Fee.

- VWAP levels and measurement periods:
  - Final Measurement Period: five Index Business Days near maturity during which the Final VWAP Level is determined.
  - Final VWAP Level: arithmetic mean of VWAP Levels on each Index Business Day in the Final Measurement Period.
  - Initial VWAP Level: arithmetic mean of VWAP Levels over a three Index Business Day period ending on the Inception Date.
  - VWAP Calculation Agent determines VWAPs and VWAP Levels on non-Disrupted Days.

- Calculation agents and roles:
  - Note Calculation Agent: J.P. Morgan Securities LLC (JPMS) makes all calculations and determinations related to the ETNs, other than those assigned to the VWAP Calculation Agent.
  - VWAP Calculation Agent: JPMorgan Global Index Research Group (affiliate) determines daily VWAPs, VWAP Levels, and Final VWAP Level.

- Market Disruption framework:
  - Averaging Date: each Index Business Day in the Final Measurement Period or Repurchase Measurement Period.
  - Disrupted Day: an Index Business Day when the Primary or Related Exchange fails to open for its regular session or a Market Disruption Event occurs and materially affects the VWAP Level.
  - Market Disruption Events include: suspensions/limitations of trading in an Index Component on its Primary Exchange; suspensions/limitations on Related Exchanges for futures/options tied to the component; events impairing market participants’ ability to transact or obtain values; or early exchange closures before Scheduled Closing Time, in each case as determined by the Note Calculation Agent. Also includes determinations that such events materially interfered with hedging.
  - Exclusions/clarifications: announced changes to trading hours are not disruptions; circuit-breaker-style limitations (e.g., NYSE Rule 80B, Nasdaq Rule 4120) count as suspensions/limitations. Scheduled Closing Time refers to regular session close, ignoring after-hours.

- Handling Disrupted Days:
  - If a component is disrupted on an Averaging Date, its VWAP and published share weighting are deferred to the next non-disrupted Index Business Day (Deferred Averaging Date) and applied to both the original disruption date and that Averaging Date in calculating VWAP Levels.
  - The final Averaging Date for any component cannot be postponed more than three Index Business Days beyond the originally scheduled final Averaging Date; if still disrupted, the Note Calculation Agent (or affiliate) will use a good-faith estimate of VWAP and share weighting.

nodes.title: Discontinuation of the Index; Alteration of Method of Calculation
nodes.heading: 37.3.12 Discontinuation of the Index; Alteration of Method of Calculation
nodes.start_phrase: If the Index Calculation Agent discontinues publication of or otherwise fails to publish the Index, or the Index Calculation Agent does not make the Index Components, their share weighting and/or the Index Divisor available to the VWAP Calculation Agent, and the Index Sponsor, the Index Calculation Agent or another entity publishes a successor or substitute index that the Note Calculation Agent determines to be comparable to the discontinued Index and for which the Index Components, their share weighting, and/or the Index Divisor are available to the VWAP Calculation Agent (such index being referred to herein as a “successor index”), then the VWAP Level for such successor index will be determined by the VWAP Calculation Agent by reference to the sum of the products of the VWAPs of the components underlying such successor index on the Primary Exchanges and each such component's respective weighting within the successor index (which sum will be adjusted by any index divisor used by such successor index) on the dates and at the times as of which the VWAP Levels for such successor index are to be determined.
nodes.summary:
- Procedures if the Index is discontinued or unavailable: the Note Calculation Agent may designate a comparable successor index; the VWAP Calculation Agent will compute the VWAP Level using the successor’s component VWAPs, weights, and any index divisor. Notice of any successor selection will be provided to the Trustee, issuer, and ETN holders.
- If no successor index is available (or a chosen successor is later discontinued) during relevant calculation dates, the Note Calculation Agent will determine VWAP Levels using the last available components, weights, and divisor of the original or successor index, adjusted for corporate actions, with notice to stakeholders.
- If the index methodology or value is materially changed, the Note Calculation Agent will adjust calculations in good faith to maintain comparability (e.g., neutralizing effects of index splits) and will use the adjusted VWAP Levels for all related values. Discontinuation or changes may adversely affect the ETNs’ value.
- Event of default/acceleration: the cash amount due per ETN equals the Repurchase Amount, calculated as if the acceleration date begins the Repurchase Measurement Period, with the next four Index Business Days used as the remaining days; the Repurchase Fee Amount is set to zero. Notice of the amount due will be provided to the Trustee and DTC within two Business Days.
- Listing: the Alerian ETNs are listed on NYSE Arca under ticker AMJ; continued listing and market liquidity are not assured.

nodes.title: Payment upon an Event of Default
nodes.heading: 37.3.13 Payment upon an Event of Default
nodes.start_phrase: In case an event of default with respect to the Alerian ETNs shall have occurred and be continuing, the amount declared due and payable per Alerian ETN upon any acceleration of the Alerian ETNs will be determined by the Note Calculation Agent and will be an amount in cash equal to the Repurchase Amount, calculated as if the date of acceleration were the first Index Business Day in the Repurchase Measurement Period and the four Index Business Days immediately succeeding the date of acceleration were the corresponding Index Business Days in the accelerated Repurchase Measurement Period.
nodes.summary:
- Fallback procedures if the Index is discontinued or its data (components, weights, divisor) is unavailable: the Note Calculation Agent may adopt a comparable successor index; VWAP Levels will be computed from the successor’s component VWAPs, weights, and divisor, with notice to the Trustee, issuer, and ETN holders.
- If no successor index is available (or a chosen successor is later discontinued) on any relevant calculation date/period (Calculation Date, Final Measurement Period, Repurchase Measurement Period), VWAP Levels will be determined using the last available components and weights before discontinuation, adjusted for corporate actions, with notice to stakeholders.
- Warning that any index discontinuation—even with these alternatives—may adversely affect the value of the Alerian ETNs.
- Adjustments for material changes to index methodology: if calculation methods are modified so the VWAP Level no longer fairly represents the index, the Note Calculation Agent will in good faith adjust calculations to produce a comparable VWAP Level as if no changes occurred (e.g., reversing the effect of an index split).
- Event of default and acceleration: the cash amount due per ETN equals the Repurchase Amount calculated as if the acceleration date were the first Index Business Day of the Repurchase Measurement Period and the next four Index Business Days were the remaining days; the Repurchase Fee Amount is set to zero. Notice of the amount due will be provided to the Trustee and DTC no later than two Business Days after acceleration.
- Listing information: Alerian ETNs are listed on NYSE Arca under the ticker AMJ, with no assurance of continued listing, liquidity, or an active trading market.

nodes.title: Listing
nodes.heading: 37.3.14 Listing
nodes.start_phrase: The Alerian ETNs have been listed on the NYSE Arca under the ticker symbol “AMJ.”
nodes.summary:
- Procedures if the Index is discontinued or data is unavailable: use a comparable successor index, if identified by the Note Calculation Agent, to compute VWAP Levels based on component VWAPs, weights, and any index divisor; provide notice to Trustee, issuer, and holders.
- If no successor index is available (or it is later discontinued) on key dates (Calculation Date, Final or Repurchase Measurement Periods): compute VWAP Levels using the most recent available VWAPs and published weights of components prior to discontinuation, adjusted for corporate actions; provide notice; warns that discontinuation may negatively affect ETN value.
- Adjustments for material changes to index methodology: if calculation methods change such that VWAP no longer fairly represents prior methodology, the Note Calculation Agent will make good-faith adjustments to produce comparable VWAP Levels as if changes (e.g., index splits) had not occurred, and will base all related values on these adjusted levels.
- Payment upon an event of default: accelerated amount per ETN equals the Repurchase Amount calculated as if the acceleration date were the first Index Business Day in the Repurchase Measurement Period and the next four Index Business Days were the remaining measurement days; Repurchase Fee Amount is zero; notice of the cash amount due will be provided to the Trustee and DTC within two Business Days.
- Listing: Alerian ETNs are listed on NYSE Arca under ticker AMJ; no assurance of continued listing, liquidity, or trading market.

nodes.title: Book-Entry Only Issuance — The Depository Trust Company
nodes.heading: 37.3.15 Book-Entry Only Issuance — The Depository Trust Company
nodes.start_phrase: DTC will act as securities depositary for the Alerian ETNs.
nodes.summary: The excerpt outlines issuance and administrative mechanics for Alerian ETNs and defines key terms used in the notes. It states that the ETNs are issued only in book-entry form through DTC, registered to Cede & Co., with global certificates deposited at DTC and no physical notes issued except in limited cases. The Bank of New York Mellon serves as registrar, transfer agent, and paying agent. The issuer may “reopen” or reissue additional ETNs that consolidate with existing notes under the same CUSIP and trade interchangeably upon settlement, increasing the aggregate principal amount; pricing is set at the time of any additional offering. The section also provides core definitions, including Business Day (NYC banking/dollar transaction days), Calculation Date (May 15, 2024, subject to market disruption adjustments), Daily Note Value (principal amount multiplied by the ratio of current VWAP Level to Initial VWAP Level), ex-dividend date, Exchange Business Day, Final Measurement Period (five Index Business Days from the Calculation Date), Final VWAP Level (mean VWAP over the Final Measurement or Repurchase period), Index Business Day, Index Component (energy-oriented MLPs in the Index), Index Divisor, Initial Issue Date (April 6, 2009), Initial VWAP Level (190.36605), and Maturity Date (May 24, 2024, subject to postponement).

nodes.title: Registrar, Transfer Agent and Paying Agent
nodes.heading: 37.3.16 Registrar, Transfer Agent and Paying Agent
nodes.start_phrase: The Bank of New York Mellon or one of its affiliates will act as registrar and transfer agent for the Alerian ETNs.
nodes.summary:
- Describes book-entry only issuance through The Depository Trust Company (DTC): Alerian ETNs are issued as fully registered global notes in the name of Cede & Co., deposited with DTC, with no physical definitive notes except in limited cases.
- Identifies The Bank of New York Mellon as registrar, transfer agent, and paying agent, with the ability to appoint additional paying agents.
- Outlines the ability to “reopen” or reissue ETNs at the issuer’s discretion based on market conditions and VWAP levels; additional issuances share the same CUSIP, are consolidated into a single sub-series, trade interchangeably upon settlement, increase the aggregate principal amount outstanding, and are priced at the time of offering.
- Provides key defined terms relevant to valuation and timing, including:
  - Business Day and Exchange/Index Business Day definitions.
  - Calculation Date (May 15, 2024) and Maturity Date (May 24, 2024), with postponements for Market Disruption Events.
  - Daily Note Value formula based on Principal Amount and the ratio of current VWAP Level to Initial VWAP Level.
  - Final Measurement Period (five Index Business Days) and Final VWAP Level (mean VWAP over that period).
  - Ex-dividend date concept for Index Components.
  - Definitions of Index Components (energy-oriented MLPs), Index Divisor, Initial Issue Date (April 6, 2009), and Initial VWAP Level (190.36605).
  - References to Primary and Related Exchanges and the roles of the VWAP Calculation Agent and Index Calculation Agent.

nodes.title: Reissuances or Reopening Issuances
nodes.heading: 37.3.17 Reissuances or Reopening Issuances
nodes.start_phrase: We may in our sole discretion, “reopen” or reissue the Alerian ETNs based upon market conditions and VWAP Levels at that time.
nodes.summary:
- Book-entry only issuance through DTC; ETNs registered in the name of Cede & Co.; represented by one or more global notes on deposit with DTC; no physical definitive notes except in limited cases.
- The Bank of New York Mellon (or affiliate) serves as registrar and transfer agent; also serves as paying agent and may appoint additional paying agents.
- The issuer may reopen/reissue ETNs at its discretion based on market conditions and VWAP Levels; any additional issuances share the same CUSIP, are immediately fungible with existing notes upon settlement, and increase the aggregate principal outstanding; pricing set at time of offering.
- Key defined terms and dates:
  - Business Day: New York banking day when dollar transactions occur.
  - Exchange Business Day: day the primary trading venue for the ETNs is open.
  - Index Business Day: day each Primary and Related Exchange is open.
  - Calculation Date: May 15, 2024 (postponable for non-Index Business Day or Market Disruption).
  - Final Measurement Period: five Index Business Days from and including the Calculation Date (subject to adjustments/postponement for Market Disruption).
  - Daily Note Value: Principal Amount multiplied by VWAP Level divided by Initial VWAP Level.
  - Final VWAP Level: arithmetic mean of VWAP Levels over the Final Measurement Period (or applicable Repurchase Measurement Period), determined by the VWAP Calculation Agent.
  - Ex-dividend date: first Business Day the Index Component trades without the distribution right on its Primary Exchange.
  - Index Component: energy-oriented MLPs included in the Index.
  - Index Divisor: divisor used by the Index Calculation Agent to compute the Index level.
  - Initial Issue Date: April 6, 2009.
  - Initial VWAP Level: 190.36605 (mean VWAP Levels from March 30 to April 1, 2009).
  - Maturity Date: May 24, 2024 (subject to postponement for Market Disruption).

nodes.title: Key Defined Terms
nodes.heading: 37.3.18 Key Defined Terms
nodes.start_phrase: A “Business Day” means any day other than a day on which the banking institutions in The City of New York are authorized or required by law, regulation or executive order to close or a day on which transactions in dollars are not conducted.
nodes.summary:
- Book-entry only issuance via DTC: Alerian ETNs are issued solely in global form, registered in the name of DTC’s nominee (Cede & Co.), with certificates deposited at DTC; no definitive notes will be issued except in limited cases.
- Agents: The Bank of New York Mellon (or affiliates) serves as registrar and transfer agent; it also acts as paying agent and may appoint additional paying agents.
- Reopenings/reissuances: The issuer may reopen or reissue ETNs at its discretion based on market conditions and VWAP Levels; any additional issuance shares the same CUSIP, forms a single sub-series, trades interchangeably upon settlement, and increases the aggregate principal; pricing of new tranches is set at the time of offering.
- Key dates and calculation periods:
  - Initial Issue Date: April 6, 2009.
  - Calculation Date: May 15, 2024 (postponable for Market Disruption Events).
  - Final Measurement Period: the five Index Business Days starting on the Calculation Date (subject to adjustments for disruptions).
  - Maturity Date: May 24, 2024 (postponable for Market Disruption Events).
- Core defined terms and mechanics:
  - Business Day, Exchange Business Day, Index Business Day defined by exchange/banking schedules.
  - Index Components: energy-oriented MLPs in the Index; Primary Exchange and Related Exchange defined for each component.
  - Index Divisor used by the Index Calculation Agent to compute Index level.
  - VWAP-based measures: Initial VWAP Level = 190.36605 (average VWAP from Mar 30–Apr 1, 2009); Final VWAP Level is the mean VWAP over the Final Measurement Period (or Repurchase Measurement Period).
  - Daily Note Value equals Principal Amount multiplied by the ratio of current VWAP Level to Initial VWAP Level.
  - Quarterly Tracking Fee: 0.2125% per quarter (0.85% per annum) applied to the prior Index Business Day’s Daily Note Value.
  - Dividend-related terms: record date and ex-dividend date for Index Components defined.
- Coupon framework:
  - Coupon Valuation Dates: Feb 15, May 15, Aug 15, Nov 15 (or next Index Business Day), beginning May 15, 2009; the final Coupon Valuation Date is the Calculation Date.
  - Coupon Record Date: 9th Index Business Day after each Coupon Valuation Date.
  - Coupon Ex-Date: generally the Exchange Business Day before the Coupon Record Date.
  - Coupon Payment Date: 15th Index Business Day after each Coupon Valuation Date; final coupon pays on the Maturity Date.
  - Reference Distribution Amount: gross cash distributions a hypothetical Reference Holder would have received on Index Components over the relevant period; if an issuer fails to pay a scheduled distribution before the Coupon Ex-Date, that distribution is treated as zero for that period.
  - Reference Holder: a hypothetical holder sized by each component’s published share weighting divided by (Index Divisor × 10).
- Early repurchase (partial terms provided):
  - Adjusted Coupon Amount for a Repurchase Valuation Date equals Adjusted Reference Distribution Amount minus the Adjusted Tracking Fee.
  - Adjusted Reference Distribution Amount reflects gross cash distributions to the Reference Holder over the period defined by applicable ex-dividend dates (definition excerpt is incomplete in the text).
- Market Disruption Events: multiple definitions and key dates/periods are subject to adjustment or postponement if such events occur.

nodes.title: Additional Key Coupon Payment Terms
nodes.heading: 37.3.19 Additional Key Coupon Payment Terms
nodes.start_phrase: The “Coupon Ex-Date” means, with respect to a Coupon Amount, the first Exchange Business Day on which the Alerian ETNs trade without the right to receive such Coupon Amount.
nodes.summary:
The excerpt outlines key defined terms and mechanics for Alerian ETNs, focusing on trading venues, fees, coupon calculations, and early repurchase adjustments.

- Trading venues and dates:
  - Primary Exchange: The main market where each Index Component primarily trades.
  - Related Exchange: Any market materially affecting futures/options on an Index Component, as determined by the Note Calculation Agent.
  - Record date: The date a holder must be on record to receive an Index Component’s distribution.

- Quarterly Tracking Fee:
  - Equal to 0.2125% (0.85% per annum) of the Daily Note Value as of the immediately preceding Index Business Day, assessed on each determination date.

- Coupon framework:
  - Coupon Ex-Date: First Exchange Business Day the ETNs trade without the right to the related Coupon Amount (generally the day before the Coupon Record Date under NYSE Arca practice).
  - Coupon Record Date: 9th Index Business Day after each Coupon Valuation Date.
  - Coupon Valuation Date: The 15th of February, May, August, and November (or next Index Business Day), starting May 15, 2009; the final one is the Calculation Date.
  - Coupon Payment Date: 15th Index Business Day after each Coupon Valuation Date; the final payment occurs on the Maturity Date.

- Reference Distribution Amount (inputs to coupon):
  - On the first Coupon Valuation Date: Sum of gross cash distributions a Reference Holder would have received on Index Components with ex-dividend dates from (but excluding) the Initial Issue Date through (and including) that Valuation Date.
  - On subsequent Coupon Valuation Dates: Sum of gross cash distributions with ex-dividend dates from (but excluding) the prior Coupon Valuation Date through (and including) the current one.
  - If an Index Component’s scheduled cash distribution due before the Coupon Ex-Date is not actually paid by its scheduled payment date, it is assumed to be zero in the calculation.

- Reference Holder definition:
  - A hypothetical holder of each Index Component in an amount equal to its published share weighting divided by (Index Divisor × 10), as of the determination date.

- Early repurchase terms:
  - Adjusted Coupon Amount (for a Repurchase Valuation Date): Equals the Adjusted Reference Distribution Amount minus the Adjusted Tracking Fee, each calculated as of that Repurchase Valuation Date.
  - Adjusted Reference Distribution Amount: Represents the gross cash distributions a Reference Holder would have been entitled to receive on Index Components with the applicable ex-dividend dates up to the Repurchase Valuation Date (definition continues beyond the excerpt).

nodes.title: Additional Key Early Repurchase Terms
nodes.heading: 37.3.20 Additional Key Early Repurchase Terms
nodes.start_phrase: The “Adjusted Coupon Amount” means, with respect to any applicable Repurchase Valuation Date, a coupon payment, if any, in an amount in cash equal to the difference between:
nodes.summary:
- Defines key trading venues and dates for Index Components:
  - Primary Exchange: main trading market for each Index Component.
  - Related Exchange: venues materially affecting futures/options on an Index Component, as determined by the Note Calculation Agent.
  - Record date: date a unitholder must be registered to receive a distribution.
- Quarterly Tracking Fee: 0.2125% per quarter (0.85% per annum) multiplied by the Daily Note Value as of the immediately preceding Index Business Day.
- Coupon mechanics and schedule for Alerian ETNs:
  - Coupon Ex-Date: first Exchange Business Day the ETNs trade without the right to the Coupon Amount (generally the day before the Coupon Record Date under NYSE Arca practice).
  - Coupon Valuation Date: Feb 15, May 15, Aug 15, Nov 15 (next Index Business Day if not an Index Business Day); first on May 15, 2009; final equals the Calculation Date.
  - Coupon Record Date: 9th Index Business Day after each Coupon Valuation Date.
  - Coupon Payment Date: 15th Index Business Day after each Coupon Valuation Date; final payment on Maturity Date.
- Reference Distribution Amount: gross cash distributions a Reference Holder would have received over the relevant period; any distribution scheduled before the Coupon Ex-Date but not paid by the issuer on the scheduled payment date is deemed zero for that calculation.
- Reference Holder: hypothetical holder with shares equal to the published share weighting divided by (Index Divisor × 10).
- Early Repurchase terms:
  - Adjusted Coupon Amount: Adjusted Reference Distribution Amount minus Adjusted Tracking Fee as of the Repurchase Valuation Date.
  - Adjusted Reference Distribution Amount: gross cash distributions with ex-dividend dates from after the prior Coupon Valuation Date (or Initial Issue Date, if earlier) through the Repurchase Valuation Date.
  - Adjusted Tracking Fee: Tracking Fee Shortfall as of the prior Coupon Valuation Date plus a pro-rated Quarterly Tracking Fee for the period (days/90).
  - Repurchase Valuation Date: last Index Business Day of each week (generally Friday) and the first Index Business Day after delivery of the Repurchase Notice and Confirmation; subject to Market Disruption Event adjustments.
  - Repurchase Date: third Calculation Date after the last Index Business Day of the applicable Repurchase Measurement Period; subject to postponement for Market Disruption Events.
  - Repurchase Fee: 0.125%.
- General Terms of the Series E Notes (under the 2001 Indenture):
  - The notes are direct, unsecured, unsubordinated obligations ranking pari passu with other unsecured unsubordinated debt of JPMorgan Chase & Co.
  - Structural subordination: as a holding company, obligations under the notes are generally junior to claims of creditors of subsidiaries (which include substantial borrowings and liabilities).
  - Summary provided is subject to, and incorporates by reference, the detailed terms and definitions in the 2001 Indenture.
- Events of Default (per the 2001 Indenture):
  - 30-day default in interest payment.
  - Default in payment of principal or other amounts when due.
  - 90-day failure to perform other covenants after notice by the trustee or holders of at least 25% of affected securities.
  - Specified bankruptcy, insolvency, winding up, or liquidation events.
  - Any additional event of default specified in applicable supplemental indentures or forms of security.

nodes.title: General Terms of the Series E Notes
nodes.heading: 37.3.21 General Terms of the Series E Notes
nodes.start_phrase: In this “General Terms of the Series E Notes” section, all references to the “ debt securities ” refer to Series E Notes issued by JPMorgan Chase.
nodes.summary:
- Defines the Adjusted Tracking Fee calculation, including:
  - Inclusion of any Tracking Fee Shortfall since the prior Coupon Valuation Date.
  - Pro rata accrual of the Quarterly Tracking Fee based on days elapsed (days/90) from the prior Coupon Valuation Date (or Initial Issue Date if before the first Coupon Valuation Date) through the Repurchase Valuation Date.
- Establishes repurchase mechanics and costs:
  - Repurchase Valuation Date: the last Index Business Day of each week (generally Friday) and the first Index Business Day after delivery of a Repurchase Notice and Repurchase Confirmation; subject to Market Disruption adjustments.
  - Repurchase Date: the third Calculation Date following the last Index Business Day in the relevant Repurchase Measurement Period; subject to Market Disruption adjustments.
  - Repurchase Fee: 0.125%.
- Outlines the General Terms of the Series E Notes under the 2001 Indenture:
  - Notes are direct, unsecured, unsubordinated obligations of JPMorgan Chase & Co., ranking pari passu with its other unsecured, unsubordinated debt.
  - Structural subordination: as a holding company, claims of the notes are generally junior to creditors of JPMorgan’s subsidiaries, except to the extent JPMorgan is itself a creditor of those subsidiaries; lists examples of subsidiary obligations.
  - Clarifies that the section summarizes, and is qualified by, the 2001 Indenture and related supplemental documents.
- Specifies Events of Default (Section 5.01):
  - 30-day default in interest payments.
  - Default in payment of principal or other amounts when due (at maturity, redemption, acceleration, etc.).
  - 90-day failure to perform covenants after notice by the trustee or holders of at least 25% in aggregate principal amount of affected securities.
  - Specified bankruptcy, insolvency, winding up, or liquidation events.
  - Any additional event of default set forth in applicable supplemental indentures or the form of security.

nodes.title: Events of Default and Waivers
nodes.heading: 37.3.21.1 Events of Default and Waivers
nodes.start_phrase: An “Event of Default” with respect to a series of debt securities issued under the 2001 Indenture is defined in the 2001 Indenture as:
nodes.summary:
- Defines the Adjusted Tracking Fee as the sum of any prior Tracking Fee Shortfall and a pro rata portion of the Quarterly Tracking Fee based on days elapsed since the prior Coupon Valuation Date (or Initial Issue Date if earlier) using a 90-day denominator.
- Specifies timing periods used for fee proration and references to Coupon Valuation Dates, Initial Issue Date, and Repurchase Valuation Dates.
- Establishes repurchase mechanics:
  - Repurchase Valuation Date: last Index Business Day of each week (generally Friday) and the first Index Business Day after delivery of Repurchase Notice and Confirmation; subject to Market Disruption adjustments.
  - Repurchase Date: third Calculation Date following the last Index Business Day in the Repurchase Measurement Period; subject to Market Disruption Event postponements.
  - Repurchase Fee: 0.125%.
- Summarizes that the Series E Notes (including Alerian ETNs) are issued under the 2001 Indenture as direct, unsecured, unsubordinated obligations ranking equally with other unsecured, unsubordinated debt of JPMorgan Chase.
- Notes structural subordination: as a holding company, JPMorgan Chase’s obligations are generally junior to claims of creditors of its subsidiaries, which have significant outstanding liabilities.
- Details Events of Default:
  - 30-day interest payment default.
  - Default in payment of principal or other amounts when due.
  - 90-day uncured breach of covenants after notice.
  - Specified bankruptcy/insolvency/winding-up events.
  - Other events as provided in supplemental indentures or security forms.
- Explains acceleration and waivers:
  - Trustee or holders of at least 25% of affected series may accelerate; scope (series vs. all series) depends on the type of default.
  - Majority holders may annul accelerations and waive past defaults, subject to conditions.
  - An Event of Default in one series does not automatically trigger one in others.
- Outlines trustee duties and holder rights:
  - Trustee must give notice of default within 90 days (may withhold if in holders’ interest, except for payment defaults).
  - Majority of affected series can direct remedies; trustee may require satisfactory indemnity.
  - No-action clause: individual holders generally cannot sue unless notice, 60-day waiting period after a 25% holder request with indemnity, and no contrary direction by a majority.
  - Absolute right of any holder to receive due principal and interest and to sue for payment cannot be impaired without that holder’s consent.
  - Issuer must provide an annual statement to the trustee regarding knowledge of defaults.
- Defines Covenant Breach as a 90-day uncured failure to perform non-payment covenants after notice; does not permit acceleration but allows the trustee to pursue judicial remedies to enforce rights.

nodes.title: Covenant Breach
nodes.heading: 37.3.21.2 Covenant Breach
nodes.start_phrase: Under the 2001 Indenture, a “Covenant Breach” would occur with respect to a series of debt securities if we fail to perform or breach any of the covenants contained in the 2001 Indenture (other than a failure to pay principal or interest on the debt securities) and that failure or breach continues for 90 days after the Trustee or the holders of at least 25% in aggregate principal amount of the outstanding debt securities give written notice of that failure or breach.
nodes.summary:
- Defines Events of Default under a 2001 Indenture, including payment defaults, covenant or agreement failures, specified bankruptcy/insolvency events, and defaults provided in supplemental indentures or forms of security, which may affect one or multiple series.
- Acceleration rights: upon certain continuing defaults, the Trustee or holders of at least 25% in principal amount of the affected series (or of all outstanding debt securities for defaults affecting all series or specified bankruptcy events) may declare principal and accrued interest immediately due and payable.
- Annulment/waiver: holders of a majority in principal amount of the outstanding debt securities of the affected series may annul accelerations and waive past defaults, subject to conditions.
- Series separability: an Event of Default for one series does not automatically constitute an Event of Default for other series.
- Trustee notice: the Trustee must give default notice within 90 days (may withhold if in holders’ interests), except it cannot withhold notice of payment defaults.
- Holder direction: holders of a majority in principal amount of each affected series, voting as a single class, may direct the Trustee’s conduct of remedies; the Trustee may decline unlawful directions and requires satisfactory security or indemnity to act.
- No-action clause: individual holders cannot sue unless they have given default notice, 60 days have passed after a written request by holders of at least 25% of each affected series with reasonable indemnity, and there is no contrary majority direction.
- Individual payment right preserved: any holder’s right to receive due principal and interest and to sue to enforce such payment cannot be impaired without that holder’s consent.
- Reporting: the issuer must deliver an annual statement to the Trustee regarding knowledge of defaults.
- Covenant Breach: occurs if non-payment covenants are breached and remain uncured for 90 days after notice by the Trustee or holders of at least 25% of the outstanding debt securities; Covenant Breach alone does not permit acceleration.
- Remedies: upon a Covenant Breach or Event of Default, the Trustee may pursue judicial proceedings to protect and enforce its and holders’ rights, including specific performance and other appropriate remedies.

nodes.title: Modification of the 2001 Indenture
nodes.heading: 37.3.21.3 Modification of the 2001 Indenture
nodes.start_phrase: The 2001 Indenture contains provisions permitting us and the Trustee to modify the 2001 Indenture or the rights of the holders of debt securities with the consent of the holders of not less than a majority in aggregate principal amount of each outstanding series of debt securities affected by the modification.
nodes.summary:
- Modification of the 2001 Indenture: Most changes require consent from holders of a majority in aggregate principal amount of each affected series. However, each affected holder must consent to fundamental changes, including extending maturity or payment dates; reducing principal, interest, or other amounts; changing payment currency or related provisions; altering calculation methods for payments; reducing redemption amounts; adversely affecting conversion/exchange/payment-in-kind terms; impairing rights to sue or repurchase; or lowering consent thresholds.
- Amendments without holder consent: Permitted to evidence mergers or trustee replacement; cure ambiguities or inconsistencies; make changes deemed necessary or desirable that do not materially and adversely affect holders; and for other specified purposes.
- Consolidation, merger, and asset sales: Prohibited unless JPMorgan Chase & Co. remains the continuing entity or the successor/transferee is a U.S. corporation or LLC that assumes all obligations, and no default exists immediately after the transaction. The indenture provides no additional protections for recapitalizations, changes of control, or highly leveraged transactions unless structured as a merger or substantial asset sale; series-specific protections (e.g., puts or increased interest) may be added via prospectus supplement.
- Trustee and agents: The Bank of New York Mellon (and its London Branch for Euroclear/Clearstream-settled notes) serves as paying agent, registrar, authenticating agent, and transfer agent. Deutsche Bank Trust Company Americas initially serves as trustee for these and other related securities.
- Conflicting interest under the Trust Indenture Act: Because of overlapping roles across multiple JPMorgan securities, an actual or potential event of default could create a conflicting interest requiring the trustee to resign and a successor to be appointed. A “potential” event of default is an event that would be an event of default absent notice or lapse-of-time conditions.
- Banking relationships: JPMorgan Chase & Co. and its subsidiaries maintain broad banking relationships with Deutsche Bank Trust Company Americas and The Bank of New York Mellon (including its London Branch).

nodes.title: Consolidations, Mergers and Sales of Assets
nodes.heading: 37.3.21.4 Consolidations, Mergers and Sales of Assets
nodes.start_phrase: We may not merge or consolidate with any other entity or sell, convey or transfer all or substantially all of our assets to any other entity (other than the sale, conveyance or transfer of all or substantially all of our assets to one or more of our direct or indirect subsidiaries), unless:
nodes.summary:
- Modification of the 2001 Indenture: Most changes require consent of holders of a majority in aggregate principal amount of each affected series. Certain core terms require individual holder consent, including changes to maturity, principal, interest rate, currency, payment determination methods, redemption amounts, conversion/exchange terms, enforcement rights, and the percentage needed to approve modifications.
- Amendments without holder consent: Permitted for administrative or corrective purposes, trustee replacement, mergers to be evidenced, curing ambiguities or inconsistencies, and other changes deemed necessary or desirable that do not materially and adversely affect holders.
- Consolidations, mergers, and sales of assets: Allowed only if JPMorgan Chase & Co. remains the obligor or a U.S. corporation/LLC expressly assumes all obligations, and no default exists immediately after the transaction. No additional covenants protect against recapitalizations, changes of control, or highly leveraged transactions unless specified for particular securities in a prospectus supplement.
- Trustee, paying agent, registrar, and transfer agent: The Bank of New York Mellon (and its London Branch for Euroclear/Clearstream) acts as paying agent, registrar, authenticating agent, and transfer agent for securities under the 2001 Indenture. Deutsche Bank Trust Company Americas initially serves as trustee for various JPMorgan and JPMorgan Financial securities; overlapping roles could create a conflicting interest under the Trust Indenture Act upon an actual or potential event of default, potentially requiring trustee resignation and appointment of a successor. A “potential” event of default is one that would be an event of default but for notice or passage-of-time requirements.

nodes.title: Concerning the Trustee, Paying Agent, Registrar and Transfer Agent
nodes.heading: 37.3.21.5 Concerning the Trustee, Paying Agent, Registrar and Transfer Agent
nodes.start_phrase: Our subsidiaries and we have a wide range of banking relationships with Deutsche Bank Trust Company Americas, The Bank of New York Mellon and The Bank of New York Mellon, London Branch.
nodes.summary:
- Modification of the 2001 Indenture: Most changes to the indenture or affected series of debt securities require consent of holders of a majority in aggregate principal amount. However, certain fundamental changes require the consent of each affected holder, including extensions of maturity, reductions in principal/interest/other amounts, changes to currency or payment-determination methods, reductions in redemption amounts, adverse changes to conversion/exchange or alternative payment terms, impairments of suit or holder repurchase rights, and reductions in required consent thresholds (Sections 8.02).
- Amendments without holder consent: We and the Trustee may amend to reflect mergers or trustee replacement, cure ambiguities or inconsistencies, or make changes deemed necessary or desirable that do not materially and adversely affect holders, among other specified administrative purposes (Section 8.01).
- Consolidations, mergers, and asset sales: Permitted only if we remain the continuing entity or the successor/transferee is a U.S. corporation or LLC that assumes all obligations, and no default exists immediately after the transaction (Section 9.01). The indenture provides no additional protections for recapitalizations, changes of control, or highly leveraged transactions unless structured as a merger, consolidation, or substantially all-asset sale; specific series may include added protections (e.g., put rights or increased interest) described in applicable prospectus supplements.
- Trustee, paying agent, registrar, and transfer agent: The Bank of New York Mellon (and, for Euroclear/Clearstream notes, The Bank of New York Mellon, London Branch) will act as paying agents, registrars, authenticating agents, and transfer agents. Deutsche Bank Trust Company Americas initially serves as trustee for certain of our and JPMorgan Financial’s securities, including under the 2001 Indenture. Because of these roles, an actual or potential event of default could create a conflicting interest under the Trust Indenture Act, potentially requiring the trustee to resign and a successor to be appointed. A “potential” event of default is one that would be an event of default absent notice or passage-of-time requirements. Subsidiaries maintain broad banking relationships with the named institutions.
