nodes.title: Events of Default and Waivers
nodes.heading: 37.4.9.1 Events of Default and Waivers
nodes.start_phrase: An “Event of Default” with respect to a series of debt securities issued under the 2016 Indenture is defined in the 2016 Indenture as:
nodes.summary:
- Acceleration on event of default: If maturity is accelerated, the Issuer or Calculation Agent must notify the Trustee (New York office) and DTC of the cash amount due within two business days of acceleration.
- Listing: Callable Notes are listed on the NYSE under “JPM/32,” with no assurance of continued listing, liquidity, or trading market.
- Book-entry only (DTC): Notes issued solely in fully registered global form in the name of Cede & Co.; deposited with DTC; no definitive notes except in limited cases.
- Registrar/Paying agent: The Bank of New York Mellon (or affiliates) serves as registrar, transfer agent, and paying agent; additional paying agents may be designated.
- Reopening: Issuer may issue additional notes (“reopenings”) that share the same CUSIP, are fungible and trade interchangeably with existing notes; pricing set at time of offering.
- General terms/2016 Indenture overview: Summary of Series A Notes under the 2016 Indenture; debt securities are direct, unsecured, unsubordinated obligations of the Issuer, fully and unconditionally guaranteed by the Guarantor, ranking equally with other unsecured unsubordinated debt.
- Structural subordination: Claims under the guarantee are structurally junior to creditors of the Guarantor’s subsidiaries (e.g., long-term debt, deposits, repo, commercial paper, other borrowings) except to the extent the Guarantor is recognized and paid as a creditor of its subsidiaries.
- Events of Default (EoD): Include (a) 30-day interest payment default; (b) principal/other amounts unpaid when due; (c) covenant breach continuing 90 days after notice by Trustee or holders of ≥25% of affected series; (d) specified Issuer bankruptcy/insolvency/receivership/winding up/liquidation; (e) guarantee ceasing/denial subject to exceptions for Guarantor insolvency/resolution/FDIC actions; (f) any additional EoD in supplemental indentures or forms.
- Remedies/acceleration and waivers: Upon certain continuing EoDs, Trustee or holders of ≥25% may declare principal and accrued interest immediately due; automatic acceleration upon specified Issuer bankruptcy events; majority of holders may waive past defaults subject to conditions.
- Guarantor-related events: Guarantor bankruptcy/insolvency/resolution or non-payment covenant breaches by Guarantor (other than payment default) do not constitute an EoD for the notes and do not permit acceleration absent an Issuer EoD; potential adverse value impact noted.
- Trustee notices and holder rights: Trustee must give default notice within 90 days (may withhold if in holders’ interest, except for payment defaults); majority of affected holders (voting as a single class) may direct remedies; Trustee may require indemnity; individual holders’ suits restricted unless prerequisites (notice, 60-day wait, 25% request, indemnity) are met; absolute right to receive payment or sue for payment preserved.
- Annual compliance statements: Issuer and Guarantor must file annual statements with the Trustee regarding knowledge of defaults.
- Indenture modifications: With consent of holders of a majority in aggregate principal of each affected series; unanimous holder consent required for fundamental changes (maturity extension, principal/interest reductions, currency/method changes, redemption amount reductions, holder repurchase/suit rights, required consent thresholds, adverse changes to guarantee). Certain amendments permitted without holder consent (e.g., mergers evidence, Trustee replacement, curing ambiguities, non-material changes).
- Consolidation, merger, sale of assets: Conditions for Issuer and Guarantor combinations/transfers require a U.S. successor that assumes obligations and no (or continuing) EoD immediately after the transaction.

nodes.title: Modification of the 2016 Indenture
nodes.heading: 37.4.9.2 Modification of the 2016 Indenture
nodes.start_phrase: The 2016 Indenture contains provisions permitting the Issuer, the Guarantor and the Trustee to modify the 2016 Indenture or the rights of the holders of debt securities with the consent of the holders of not less than a majority in aggregate principal amount of each outstanding series of debt securities affected by the modification.
nodes.summary:
- Enforcement and trustee action: Holders of a specified aggregate principal amount of each affected series may, with a written request and reasonable indemnity, require the Trustee to act, so long as a majority in aggregate principal amount of the affected series (voting as a single class) has not directed otherwise. Individual holders’ rights to receive payment when due and to sue to enforce such payment cannot be impaired without their consent.
- Annual compliance statement: The Issuer and Guarantor must annually deliver to the Trustee a written statement indicating whether they have knowledge of any default.
- Modifications with holder consent: The Issuer, Guarantor, and Trustee may modify the Indenture or holder rights with the consent of holders of at least a majority in aggregate principal amount of each affected series. However, each affected holder must consent to changes that would: extend maturity; reduce principal, interest, or other amounts; change payment currency or related foreign currency provisions; alter payment calculation methods; reduce redemption amounts; impair the right to sue or any holder repurchase right (if applicable); lower consent thresholds; or adversely change or release the guarantee.
- Amendments without holder consent: Certain amendments are permitted to evidence mergers or trustee replacement, cure ambiguities or inconsistencies, make non-material/non-adverse changes, and for other limited purposes.
- Consolidations, mergers, and asset transfers: The Issuer and Guarantor may merge, consolidate, or transfer substantially all assets only if a U.S. successor assumes all obligations (including the guarantee for the Guarantor) and no Event of Default (or event that would become one) exists or would result immediately after the transaction.

nodes.title: Consolidations, Mergers, Sales and Transfers of Assets
nodes.heading: 37.4.9.3 Consolidations, Mergers, Sales and Transfers of Assets
nodes.start_phrase: Neither the Issuer nor the Guarantor may merge or consolidate with any other entity or sell, convey or transfer all or substantially all of their respective assets to any other entity, unless:
nodes.summary:
- Holder and trustee rights: Holders owning at least a majority in aggregate principal amount of each affected series (voting as a single class) may request the Trustee to take action with reasonable indemnity, provided no inconsistent majority direction exists (Sec. 5.06). Each holder’s right to receive due payments and to sue for enforcement cannot be impaired without that holder’s consent (Sec. 5.07). The Issuer and Guarantor must annually certify to the Trustee whether they know of any default (Sec. 3.05).
- Indenture modifications: The Issuer, Guarantor, and Trustee may modify the Indenture with consent of holders of a majority in principal amount of each affected series. Certain fundamental changes require consent of each affected holder, including extending maturity, reducing principal/interest/other amounts, changing currency or payment determination methods, reducing redemption amounts, impairing enforcement/specified repurchase rights, lowering required consent thresholds, or adversely changing/releasing the guarantee (Sec. 8.02). Amendments without holder consent are permitted for limited purposes such as mergers evidence, trustee replacement, curing ambiguities/defects, and non-material changes not adverse to holders (Sec. 8.01).
- Consolidations, mergers, and asset transfers: The Issuer and Guarantor may merge, consolidate, or sell all/substantially all assets only if the successor is a U.S. entity that assumes all obligations and no Event of Default (or potential Event of Default) exists immediately after the transaction (Secs. 9.01, 9.02). Transfers of material assets in bankruptcy or resolution proceedings are deemed sales of all or substantially all assets. There are no change-of-control, recapitalization, or highly leveraged transaction covenants; protections, if any, may be provided for specific series in a prospectus supplement.
- JPMorgan Chase guarantee: The Guarantor fully and unconditionally guarantees punctual payment of principal, interest, and other amounts when due; the guarantee is of payment, not collection (Sec. 14.01). The Guarantor is not liable for amounts the Issuer is excused from paying or amounts exceeding what is actually due, and may assert any defenses/counterclaims available to the Issuer (other than those arising solely from the Issuer’s insolvency or bankruptcy status) (Sec. 14.02).
- Trustee and agents: Deutsche Bank Trust Company Americas initially serves as Trustee; The Bank of New York Mellon (and its London Branch for Euroclear/Clearstream notes) serves as paying, authenticating, registrar, and transfer agent. Given multiple roles across related securities, the Trustee may face a conflicting interest under the Trust Indenture Act upon an actual or potential default and may be required to resign, with a successor appointed.
- Governing law: The Indenture, debt securities, and guarantee are governed by New York law (Sec. 11.08).

nodes.title: JPMorgan Chase Guarantee
nodes.heading: 37.4.9.4 JPMorgan Chase Guarantee
nodes.start_phrase: The Guarantor will fully and unconditionally guarantee the full and punctual payment of the principal of, interest on, and all other amounts payable under the debt securities when the same becomes due and payable, whether at maturity, upon redemption, repurchase at the option of the holders of the applicable debt securities or upon acceleration.
nodes.summary:
- Transfers of the Guarantor’s material assets arising from or related to bankruptcy, insolvency, resolution, or similar proceedings (including under U.S. Bankruptcy Code Title 11 and Dodd-Frank Title II) are deemed sales or transfers of all or substantially all assets.
- The 2016 Indenture provides no special protections for recapitalizations, changes of control, or highly leveraged transactions unless structured as a merger, consolidation, or a sale of all/substantially all assets; the Issuer may offer deal-specific protections (e.g., put rights or higher interest) in a prospectus supplement.
- JPMorgan Chase, as Guarantor, fully and unconditionally guarantees timely payment of principal, interest, and other amounts due on the debt securities at maturity, redemption, holder put, or acceleration; the guarantee is of payment (not collection). The Guarantor is not liable for amounts the Issuer is excused from paying or amounts beyond what is actually due, and may assert the Issuer’s defenses/counterclaims other than those based solely on the Issuer’s insolvency status.
- Paying/authenticating/registrar/transfer agents: The Bank of New York Mellon and, for Euroclear/Clearstream notes, The Bank of New York Mellon, London Branch. Trustee: Deutsche Bank Trust Company Americas initially. The Issuer, Guarantor, and affiliates have banking relationships with these institutions. If an event or “potential” event of default arises, the Trustee may have a conflicting interest under the Trust Indenture Act and could be required to resign, prompting appointment of a successor.
- Governing law: New York law governs the debt securities, the 2016 Indenture, and the guarantee.

nodes.title: Concerning the Trustee, Paying Agent, Registrar and Transfer Agent
nodes.heading: 37.4.9.5 Concerning the Trustee, Paying Agent, Registrar and Transfer Agent
nodes.start_phrase: We, the Guarantor and certain of their affiliates have a wide range of banking relationships with Deutsche Bank Trust Company Americas, The Bank of New York Mellon and The Bank of New York Mellon, London Branch.
nodes.summary:
- Bankruptcy/receivership transfers: Any transfer of the Guarantor’s material assets arising from or related to bankruptcy, insolvency, receivership, resolution, or similar proceedings is deemed a sale or transfer of all or substantially all of the Guarantor’s assets.
- Limited holder protections on corporate transactions: The 2016 Indenture contains no change-of-control, recapitalization, or highly leveraged transaction covenants. The merger covenant applies only if such transactions are structured as a merger/consolidation or a sale of all/substantially all assets. The Issuer may add deal-specific protections (e.g., put rights or increased interest) in a prospectus supplement.
- JPMorgan Chase guarantee: The Guarantor fully and unconditionally guarantees timely payment of principal, interest, and other amounts—guarantee of payment, not collection. If the Issuer fails to pay when due, the Guarantor must pay on demand at the same place and manner as under the indenture.

nodes.title: Protection-Based Vesting
nodes.heading: 38.4 Protection-Based Vesting
nodes.start_phrase: This award is intended and expected to vest on the vesting date(s), provided that you are continuously employed by the Firm through such vesting date, or you meet the requirements for continued vesting described under the subsections “--Job Elimination”, “--Full Career Eligibility”, “--Government Office” or “--Disability”.
nodes.summary:

  - Job Elimination: HR determines the job was eliminated; recipient cooperates and provides requested services after notice; Release/Certification Requirements satisfied.
  - Full Career Eligibility: Voluntary termination; at least 5 years of continuous service; age + Recognized Service ≥ 60; at least 180 days’ advance written notice with cooperative service and no work for other employers during the notice period; pre-termination determination that continued vesting is appropriate based on performance and conduct; 36-month post-grant non-compete/non-practice in the recipient’s profession (government, education, and Not-for-Profit work permitted); Release/Certification Requirements satisfied. The Firm may require continued service during the 180-day period or shorten it.

nodes.title: Bonus Recoupment

nodes.title: Termination of Employment

nodes.summary:

- Termination and continued vesting: By default, unvested RSUs are cancelled upon termination. Continued vesting may apply for:

  - Government Office (voluntary termination to accept or run for a qualifying government role; subject to Government Office Requirements).
  - Disability (meets LTD or equivalent criteria; timely written request, documentation, and Firm consent; execution of required release/certifications).
- Release/Certification requirements: Execute a Firm-specified release; obtain written consent where required; for Full Career Eligibility and Government Office, certify ongoing compliance with employment restrictions before each vesting date; comply with all other Award Agreement terms.
- Death: If eligible to vest at death, RSUs vest immediately and are distributed to the designated beneficiary or estate within required timeframes.
- Employee obligations: Non-solicitation of Firm employees and customers/suppliers (including no inducing departures, no prohibited hiring shortly after separation, and no diversion of business) during employment and for the longer of one year post-termination or three years from grant date if the award remains outstanding; additional obligations include confidentiality, non-disparagement, cooperation, compliance with the Award Agreement, and adherence to any notice period policies.

nodes.title: Release/Certification

nodes.summary:

- Confidentiality obligations during and after employment: no use/disclosure of confidential information or media communications about the Firm, customers, or employees except as permitted by the Code of Conduct, law, or legal process; no post-termination access to internal systems; “confidential information” defined by the Code of Conduct. Preserves rights to report suspected legal/Code violations to management, regulators, government, attorneys, or courts and to respond truthfully in legal/regulatory matters.
- Non-disparagement commitment during and after employment, with carve-outs for lawful reporting and truthful participation in investigations or proceedings.
- Cooperation duty to assist the Firm and its counsel in audits, tax matters, litigation, investigations, and governmental proceedings, with reimbursement of reasonable out-of-pocket expenses.
- Compliance and disclosure: obligation to provide information to verify compliance with the Award Agreement; authorization for the Firm to disclose Award Agreement terms to affected third parties, including prospective employers.
- Notice Period requirements: if subject to a contractual/policy notice period, employee must give required advance written notice; Firm may require continued services or place employee on paid leave during the period; employee must devote full time to the Firm, not work elsewhere, and will receive base salary and certain benefits; parties may mutually modify; separate obligation to provide 180 days’ advance notice for “Full Career Eligibility” terminations.
- Remedies section (partially shown) indicating potential cancellation/recapture of awards for detrimental conduct, risk-related issues, and other specified circumstances, referencing other sections such as Protection-Based Vesting and Bonus.

nodes.title: Non-Disparagement
nodes.heading: 38.9.3 Non-Disparagement
nodes.start_phrase: You will not, either during your employment with the Firm or thereafter, make or encourage others to make any public statement or release any information in verbal, written, electronic or any other form,
nodes.summary:
- Non-solicitation/non-interference: Prohibits soliciting or interfering with the Firm’s customers, suppliers, or other parties known through employment, with exceptions for publicly known institutional clients serviced without using confidential information and for authorized actions taken in the normal course of employment.
- Confidentiality: Bars use or disclosure of the Firm’s confidential information and media communications about the Firm, its customers, or employees; prohibits unauthorized post-termination access to internal systems; aligns “confidential information” with the JPMorgan Chase Code of Conduct; includes carve-outs for lawful reporting to management, regulators, government, attorneys, or courts and for truthful responses to legal/regulatory inquiries.
- Non-disparagement: Prohibits public statements that disparage the Firm or its employees, officers, directors, or shareholders as a group, with carve-outs for lawful reporting and truthful participation in legal/regulatory matters.
- Cooperation: Requires full cooperation with the Firm and its counsel in audits, tax matters, litigation, investigations, and government proceedings, with reimbursement of reasonable out-of-pocket expenses.
- Compliance and disclosures: obligates providing information to confirm compliance with the Award Agreement and authorizes the Firm to disclose the agreement’s terms to third parties, including prospective employers.
- Notice period: If subject to a contractual/policy notice requirement, the employee must give advance written notice before resigning; the Firm may require continued service or place the employee on paid leave during the notice period; during this time, the employee must devote full time and loyalty to the Firm, not work elsewhere, and will receive base salary and certain benefits; the period may be mutually modified/waived; a separate 180-day advance notice applies for “Full Career Eligibility.”
- Remedies (introductory, truncated): Signals detrimental conduct, risk-related, and other cancellation/recapture provisions in addition to cancellation under sections such as Protection-Based Vesting and Bonus.

nodes.title: Cooperation
nodes.heading: 38.9.4 Cooperation
nodes.start_phrase: You will cooperate fully with and provide full and accurate information to the Firm and its counsel with respect to any matter (including any audit, tax proceeding, litigation, investigation or governmental proceeding) with respect to which you may have knowledge or information, subject to reimbursement for actual, appropriate and reasonable out-of-pocket expenses incurred by you.
nodes.summary:
- Post-employment non-solicitation/non-interference: restrictions on soliciting or interfering with Firm customers, suppliers, or contacts learned through employment, with an exception for publicly known institutional customers serviced after employment without using the Firm’s confidential information; normal-course, authorized job actions are excluded.
- Confidentiality: prohibition during and after employment on using or disclosing the Firm’s confidential information and on media communications about the Firm, its customers, or employees, except as permitted by the Code of Conduct, policies, law, or legal process; no unauthorized access to internal systems post-termination; “confidential information” follows the Code of Conduct definition.
- Whistleblower and legal rights: nothing prevents reporting suspected legal or Code of Conduct violations to management, directors, regulators, government, attorneys, or courts, or responding truthfully to official inquiries.
- Non-disparagement: no public statements intended to disparage or criticize the Firm or its people, with carve-outs for lawful reporting and truthful cooperation with regulators or courts.
- Cooperation obligation: ongoing duty to cooperate and provide accurate information in audits, tax matters, litigation, investigations, or governmental proceedings, with reimbursement of reasonable out-of-pocket expenses.
- Compliance monitoring: you must provide information needed to confirm compliance with the Award Agreement, and the Firm may disclose agreement terms to affected third parties, including prospective employers.
- Notice period: if subject to a contractual/policy notice period, you must give required advance written notice; during notice, the Firm may require continued service or place you on paid leave; you must devote full time to the Firm and not work elsewhere; pay and certain benefits continue; parties may mutually adjust the notice length; a separate 180-day advance notice applies for “Full Career Eligibility” terminations.
- Remedies/cancellation: references to potential cancellation/recapture for detrimental conduct, risk-related issues, and other reasons, in addition to separate “Protection-Based Vesting,” “Bonus …” provisions (section continues beyond the excerpt).

nodes.title: Compliance with Award Agreement
nodes.heading: 38.9.5 Compliance with Award Agreement
nodes.start_phrase: You will provide the Firm with any information reasonably requested to determine compliance with the Award Agreement, and you authorize the Firm to disclose the terms of the Award Agreement to any third party who might be affected thereby, including your prospective employer.
nodes.summary:
- Non-solicitation and non-interference: Prohibits soliciting or interfering with Firm customers, suppliers, or other relationships learned through employment; exception for publicly known institutional clients serviced post-employment without using Firm confidential information. Normal-course, authorized business actions are excluded.
- Confidentiality: Bars use or disclosure of Firm confidential information and media communications about Firm matters during and after employment, except as permitted by the JPMorgan Chase Code of Conduct, policies, law, or legal process. Post-termination, prohibits unauthorized access to Firm systems. “Confidential information” is as defined in the Code of Conduct.
- Whistleblower and legal cooperation carveouts: Allows reporting suspected legal or Code of Conduct violations to Firm management/directors, regulators, government, attorneys, or courts, and truthful responses to official inquiries.
- Non-disparagement: Prohibits public statements that disparage or criticize the Firm or its stakeholders, with carveouts for lawful reporting and truthful regulatory or legal responses.
- Cooperation duty: Requires full cooperation with the Firm and its counsel in audits, tax matters, litigation, investigations, and governmental proceedings, with reimbursement of reasonable out-of-pocket expenses.
- Compliance with Award Agreement: Requires providing information to confirm compliance and authorizes the Firm to disclose agreement terms to affected third parties, including prospective employers.
- Notice Period: If subject to a contractual/policy notice period, employee must give the required written advance notice to resign. The Firm may require continued service or place the employee on paid leave during the notice period; the employee must devote full time to the Firm, not work elsewhere, and will receive base pay and certain benefits. Parties may agree to modify/waive the period. Separately, a 180-day advance notice applies for “Full Career Eligibility.”
- Remedies (intro): References potential cancellation/recapture for detrimental conduct and risk-related issues, in addition to other cancellation provisions (section truncated).

nodes.title: Notice Period
nodes.heading: 38.9.6 Notice Period
nodes.start_phrase: If you are subject to a notice period or become subject to a notice period after the Grant Date, whether by contract or by policy, that requires you to provide advance written notice of your intention to terminate your employment (“Notice Period”),
nodes.summary:
- Restrictive covenants on solicitation/interference: prohibits soliciting or interfering with Firm relationships; exceptions for publicly known institutional customers when no Firm confidential information is used and for authorized actions in the normal course of employment.
- Confidentiality: bans use/disclosure of Firm confidential information and media communications about the Firm, customers, or employees during and after employment, except as allowed by the Code of Conduct, law, or legal process; prohibits unauthorized access to internal systems post-termination; preserves rights to report concerns to management, regulators, or courts and to respond truthfully in legal/regulatory matters.
- Non-disparagement: prohibits public statements that could disparage or criticize the Firm or its people during and after employment, with exceptions for lawful reporting and truthful participation in investigations or proceedings.
- Cooperation: requires full cooperation and accurate information in audits, tax matters, litigation, investigations, and governmental proceedings, with reimbursement of reasonable out-of-pocket expenses.
- Compliance with Award Agreement: requires providing information to verify compliance and authorizes the Firm to disclose agreement terms to affected third parties, including prospective employers.
- Notice Period: obligates employees subject to a contractual/policy notice period to give advance written notice; the Firm may require continued service or place the employee on paid leave during the period; employee must devote full time to the Firm and not work elsewhere; pay and certain benefits continue; parties may agree to modify/waive; separate 180-day advance notice applies for Full Career Eligibility.
- Remedies (partial): references potential cancellation/recapture for detrimental conduct, risk-related issues, and other grounds, tying to sections such as Protection-Based Vesting and Bonus (details truncated).

nodes.title: Remedies
nodes.heading: 38.10 Remedies
nodes.start_phrase: In addition to the cancellation provisions described under the sections captioned “ Protection-Based Vesting ”, “Bonus Recoupment ”, and “ Termination of Employment ”, up to 100% of your outstanding RSUs under this award may be cancelled if the Firm in its sole discretion determines that:
nodes.summary:
- Non-solicitation/interference: Prohibits soliciting or interfering with the Firm’s customers, suppliers, or other relationships gained through employment, with an exception for publicly known institutional customers serviced after employment without using the Firm’s confidential information; normal, authorized in-role actions are excluded.
- Confidential information and media: Bans use/disclosure of the Firm’s confidential information and communications with media about the Firm, customers, or employees during and after employment, except as allowed by the Code of Conduct, law, or legal process; prohibits post-termination access to internal systems; preserves rights to report concerns to management, regulators, or courts and to respond truthfully in legal/regulatory matters.
- Non-disparagement: Prohibits public statements intended or reasonably likely to disparage the Firm or its stakeholders, with carve-outs for lawful reporting and truthful cooperation with regulators or courts.
- Cooperation: Requires full cooperation and accurate information in audits, tax matters, litigation, investigations, and governmental proceedings; reimburses reasonable out-of-pocket expenses.
- Compliance with Award Agreement: Requires providing information to verify compliance and authorizes the Firm to disclose Award Agreement terms to affected third parties, including prospective employers.
- Notice Period: If subject to a contractual/policy notice period, employee must provide advance written notice; the Firm may require continued service or place the employee on paid leave during notice; during notice, employee must devote full time to the Firm and not work elsewhere, continuing to receive base pay and certain benefits; parties may mutually modify; separate 180-day advance notice under “Full Career Eligibility” also applies.
- Remedies—cancellation/suspension: Up to 100% of outstanding RSUs may be canceled for detrimental conduct causing material financial/reputational harm, awards based on materially inaccurate metrics or misrepresentation, failure to timely identify/raise material risks, termination for (or that could have been for) Cause, failure to meet notice/cooperation/employment restrictions, failure to return required forms, or other violations of “Your Obligations.” The Firm may suspend vesting/distributions during evaluations and is not liable for market fluctuations; suspended units may be reinstated per procedures.
- Remedies—recovery (clawback): The Firm may require repayment up to the fair market value of shares distributed within three years before notice-of-recovery for fraud, knowing/willful misconduct, violations of “Your Obligations,” or violations of post-termination employment restrictions (Full Career Eligibility or Government Office). For detrimental/risk-related conduct, recovery may apply to shares distributed within one year prior to notice. Notice-of-recovery may be electronic and sent to the last known address and preserves the Firm’s rights. Repayment generally excludes amounts tied to irrevocable tax withholdings/payments and may be made in cash or stock; this is a lawful recovery, not a penalty, and does not limit separate Bonus Recoupment obligations.

nodes.title: Recovery
nodes.heading: 38.10.1 Recovery
nodes.start_phrase: In addition, you may be required to pay the Firm up to an amount equal to the Fair Market Value (determined as of the applicable vesting date) of the gross number of shares of Common Stock previously distributed under this award as follows:
nodes.summary:
- Sets out JPMorgan Chase’s right to cancel up to 100% of outstanding RSUs for detrimental or risk-related conduct, including: causing material financial or reputational harm; awards based on materially inaccurate metrics (regardless of fault) or your misrepresentation; failure to timely identify/raise material risks; termination for Cause (or that termination could have been for Cause); failure to meet advance notice/cooperation or post-employment restrictions; failure to return required Release/Certification forms; or violation of “Your Obligations.”
- Allows the Firm to suspend vesting and/or share distributions while it evaluates cancellation, recovery, or distribution conditions; the Firm isn’t liable for market fluctuations during suspension, and suspended units may be reinstated per plan procedures; subject to other ownership/limitations provisions.
- Establishes recovery (clawback) of up to the Fair Market Value of previously distributed shares:
  - Within three years before a notice-of-recovery for fraud, knowing and willful misconduct, violations of “Your Obligations,” or violations of post-employment restrictions (Full Career Eligibility or Government Office).
  - Within one year before a notice-of-recovery for specified detrimental and risk-related conduct.
- Defines notice-of-recovery (including electronic notice) and deems good-faith delivery to the last known address sufficient; a notice that the Firm is evaluating recovery preserves its rights, and completion of the evaluation is at the Firm’s discretion.
- Clarifies tax treatment: “distributed” includes shares withheld for taxes, but the intent is to seek repayment only for shares effectively retained after taxes; no repayment required for amounts representing irrevocable tax withholdings or unrecoverable tax payments, as determined by the Firm or its nominee.
- Permits repayment in shares or cash; characterizes repayment as a lawful recovery, not a penalty; states these provisions do not limit separate “Bonus Recoupment” obligations.

nodes.title: Right to an Injunction
nodes.heading: 38.10.2 Right to an Injunction
nodes.start_phrase: You acknowledge that a violation or attempted violation of the obligations set forth herein will cause immediate and irreparable damage to the Firm, and therefore agree that the Firm shall be entitled as a matter of right to an injunction, from any court of competent jurisdiction, restraining any violation or further violation of such obligations; such right to an injunction, however, shall be cumulative and in addition to whatever other remedies the Firm may have under law or equity.
nodes.summary:
- Right to an injunction: Any breach or attempted breach causes irreparable harm; the firm is entitled to injunctive relief in addition to other legal/equitable remedies.
- Tax withholding: The firm may retain or sell shares, withhold from cash compensation, or hold vested shares/dividend equivalents to satisfy withholding and other tax obligations.
- Right to set off: The firm may use vested shares or funds to satisfy debts you owe the firm (subject to applicable law and Section 409A), but will not recover amounts from your funds or unrestricted securities held at the firm without your consent, except for certain accounts referenced under other limitations.
- No ownership rights before vesting: RSUs confer no ownership or voting rights until shares are issued post-vesting; the firm may open a brokerage or book-entry account to deliver vested shares.
- Suspension/cancellation and restrictions: RSUs may be suspended or canceled per referenced provisions (Protection-Based Vesting, Bonus Recoupment, Termination of Employment, Remedies, Amendment). The firm may impose post-vesting restrictions on transfer, sale, pledging, hedging, or encumbrance of issued shares (voting/dividend rights remain). If recovery applies during a restricted period, you may owe the firm up to the FMV of the gross restricted shares.
- Binding agreement: The Award Agreement binds JPMorgan Chase’s successors.
- Not an employment contract: Employment remains at-will; no promise of future awards; award value does not count for severance.
- Section 409A compliance: The award is intended to comply with Section 409A; includes conditions affecting specified employees upon separation from service, addressing distributions that could occur within six months (details truncated).

nodes.title: Administrative Provisions
nodes.heading: 38.11 Administrative Provisions
nodes.start_phrase: Withholding Taxes : As a result of legal and/or tax obligations the Firm, in its sole discretion, may (i) retain from each distribution the number of shares of Common Stock required to satisfy applicable tax obligations or (ii) implement any other desirable or necessary procedures, so that appropriate withholding and other taxes are paid to the competent authorities with respect to the vested shares, dividend equivalents and the award.
nodes.summary:
- Remedy for breach: The firm is entitled to immediate injunctive relief for violations of the agreement, in addition to other legal or equitable remedies.
- Administrative provisions – Withholding taxes: The firm may satisfy tax obligations by retaining or selling shares, withholding from cash compensation, or holding vested shares/dividend equivalents until taxes are paid, and will remit appropriate taxes to authorities.
- Right to set off: The firm may use vested shares or funds from the award to satisfy debts you owe the firm, to the extent permitted by law (including Section 409A). It will not recoup from your unrestricted accounts at the firm without consent, except for accounts referenced under “No Ownership Rights/Other Limitations.”
- No ownership rights/other limitations: RSUs confer no ownership or voting rights until vesting. The firm may establish a brokerage or book-entry account in your name to deliver vested shares. Vesting may be suspended and RSUs may be canceled under specified provisions (e.g., protection-based vesting, bonus recoupment, termination, remedies). The firm may impose post-vesting restrictions (e.g., sale, transfer, pledge, hedge) on issued shares for a period; voting/dividend rights remain. You may be required to repay up to the fair market value of restricted shares if recovery provisions apply, despite set-off limits.
- Binding effect: The award agreement binds successors to JPMorgan Chase.
- No employment contract: Employment remains at-will; the award does not guarantee continued employment or future awards and is not counted for severance purposes.
- Section 409A compliance: The award is intended to comply with Section 409A; terms are to be interpreted accordingly. If you are a specified employee who separates from service, distributions that are deferred compensation may be delayed up to six months (text truncated).

nodes.title: Right to Set Off
nodes.heading: 38.11.1 Right to Set Off
nodes.start_phrase: Although the Firm expects to settle this award in share(s) of Common Stock as of the applicable vesting date, as set forth in your Award Agreement, the Firm may, to the maximum extent permitted by applicable law (including Section 409A of the Code to the extent it is applicable to you), retain for itself funds or the Common Stock resulting from any vesting of this award to satisfy any obligation or debt that you owe to the Firm.
nodes.summary:
- Right to an injunction: Any breach or attempted breach of the agreement causes irreparable harm, allowing the Firm to obtain injunctive relief in addition to other legal or equitable remedies.

- Administrative provisions:
  - Withholding taxes: The Firm may retain or sell shares, withhold from cash compensation, or hold vested shares/dividend equivalents until applicable taxes are paid to authorities.
  - Right to set off: The Firm may use vested shares or funds from this award to satisfy debts you owe the Firm, to the extent permitted by law (including Section 409A). It will not use funds or unrestricted securities in your personal Firm brokerage accounts without your consent, except for certain accounts referenced under “No Ownership Rights/Other Limitations.”
  - No ownership rights/limitations: RSUs confer no ownership or voting rights until vesting and issuance. The Firm may open a brokerage or book-entry account in your name to deliver vested shares. RSUs may be suspended or canceled under specified provisions (e.g., protection-based vesting, bonus recoupment, termination, remedies, amendment).
  - Post-vesting restrictions: The Firm may temporarily restrict the sale, transfer, pledge, assignment, hedging, or encumbrance of issued shares; voting and dividend rights remain. If recovery/recoupment applies during such restriction, you may have to repay up to the fair market value of the gross restricted shares, notwithstanding set-off limits.

- Binding agreement: The Award Agreement binds JPMorgan Chase’s successors.

- Not an employment contract: Employment remains at-will; the award does not guarantee continued employment, future awards, or severance compensation treatment.

- Section 409A compliance: The award is intended to comply with Section 409A and will be interpreted accordingly. If you are a specified employee who separates from service and any portion of the award is deferred compensation payable within six months due to that separation, payment may be subject to a six-month delay.

nodes.title: No Ownership Rights/Other Limitations
nodes.heading: 38.11.2 No Ownership Rights/Other Limitations
nodes.start_phrase: RSUs do not convey the rights of ownership of Common Stock and do not carry voting rights.
nodes.summary:
- Right to an Injunction: The firm can immediately seek court injunctions to stop any actual or attempted violations of the agreement, in addition to other legal or equitable remedies.
- Withholding Taxes: The firm may satisfy tax obligations by retaining or selling shares, withholding from cash compensation, or holding vested shares/dividend equivalents until taxes are paid.
- Right to Set Off: Subject to applicable law (including Section 409A), the firm may retain funds or vested shares to cover debts you owe to the firm, but will not draw from your other unrestricted accounts at the firm without consent; certain authorized accounts are excluded.
- No Ownership Rights/Other Limitations: RSUs confer no ownership or voting rights until vesting. The firm may open a brokerage or book-entry account to deliver vested shares. RSUs may be canceled if applicable cancellation provisions apply during suspended vesting. The firm may impose post-vesting restrictions (e.g., on transfer, pledge, hedging). If recovery provisions apply during any restriction period, you may owe the firm up to the fair market value of the gross restricted shares, despite setoff limits.
- Binding Agreement: The award binds JPMorgan Chase’s successors.
- Not a Contract of Employment: Employment remains at-will; the award does not guarantee continued employment, future awards, or severance compensation treatment.
- Section 409A Compliance: Distributions are intended to comply with Section 409A; includes a six-month delay for specified employees upon separation from service when required. References are made to Protection-Based Vesting, Bonus Recoupment, Termination of Employment, Remedies, and Amendment provisions.

nodes.title: Binding Agreement
nodes.heading: 38.11.3 Binding Agreement
nodes.start_phrase: The Award Agreement will be binding upon any successor in interest to JPMorgan Chase, by merger or otherwise.
nodes.summary:
- Provides the Firm a right to injunctive relief for any violations of the agreement’s obligations, in addition to other legal/equitable remedies.
- Outlines administrative provisions for tax withholding, including retaining or selling shares to cover taxes, withholding from cash compensation, and holding vested shares until taxes are paid.
- Grants the Firm a right to set off vested shares or funds to satisfy debts owed by the employee, subject to applicable law and limits; excludes recoupment from other unrestricted accounts without consent (with certain exceptions).
- Clarifies that RSUs do not confer ownership or voting rights until vesting; authorizes the Firm to open a brokerage or book-entry account and deliver vested shares; allows suspension and potential cancellation of RSUs under certain provisions; permits the Firm to impose post-vesting restrictions on transfer/hedging without affecting voting or dividends; and allows recovery of amounts up to the fair market value if recovery provisions apply during restricted periods.
- States the agreement binds JPMorgan Chase’s successors.
- Confirms the award is not an employment contract; employment remains at-will; no guarantee of future awards; award value excluded from severance calculations.
- Affirms intent to comply with Section 409A of the U.S. Internal Revenue Code, including potential six-month distribution delay for specified employees after separation from service (provision partially shown).

nodes.title: Not a Contract of Employment
nodes.heading: 38.11.4 Not a Contract of Employment
nodes.start_phrase: Nothing contained in the Award Agreement constitutes a contract of employment or continued employment.
nodes.summary:
- Right to an injunction: The Firm can seek immediate injunctive relief for any violation of obligations, in addition to other legal or equitable remedies.
- Tax withholding: The Firm may retain shares, sell shares on your behalf, withhold from cash compensation, or hold vested shares/dividend equivalents until taxes are paid to satisfy withholding and other tax obligations.
- Right to set-off: Subject to applicable law (including Section 409A), the Firm may retain funds or shares from vesting to satisfy debts you owe to the Firm, but will not recoup from your funds or unrestricted securities held at the Firm without your consent; certain account exceptions apply.
- No ownership rights/limitations: RSUs do not confer ownership or voting rights until vesting; the Firm may open a brokerage/book-entry account to deliver vested shares; unvested RSUs may be suspended or canceled per award provisions; after vesting, the Firm may impose transfer/pledge/hedging restrictions on shares (voting and dividend rights remain); if recovery applies during the restriction period, you may owe the Firm up to the fair market value of the restricted shares at vesting.
- Binding agreement: The Award Agreement binds JPMorgan Chase’s successors.
- Not a contract of employment: Employment remains at-will; the award does not guarantee future awards and is not counted for severance.
- Section 409A compliance: Distributions are intended to comply with Section 409A; special rules apply for “specified employees” upon separation from service (text indicates a six-month related limitation but is truncated).

nodes.title: Section 409A Compliance
nodes.heading: 38.11.5 Section 409A Compliance
nodes.start_phrase: To the extent that Section 409A of the Code is applicable to this award, distributions of shares and cash hereunder are intended to comply with Section 409A of the Code, and the Award Agreement, including these terms and conditions, shall be interpreted in a manner consistent with such intent.
nodes.summary:
- Establishes the Firm’s right to seek immediate injunctive relief for any violation of award obligations, in addition to other legal or equitable remedies.
- Details tax withholding procedures, allowing the Firm to withhold or sell shares, withhold from cash compensation, or retain vested shares/dividend equivalents to satisfy tax liabilities.
- Grants the Firm a right of set-off against vested shares/funds to satisfy debts owed by the employee, with limits on recoupment from certain unrestricted accounts without consent.
- Clarifies that RSUs confer no ownership or voting rights until vesting; authorizes the Firm to open brokerage/book-entry accounts and deliver vested shares; permits suspension and cancellation of RSUs per referenced provisions.
- Allows the Firm to impose post-vesting restrictions (e.g., transfer, sale, pledge, hedge limits) and require repayment up to the fair market value of restricted shares if recovery provisions apply.
- States the Award Agreement is binding on JPMorgan Chase successors.
- Confirms employment is at-will; the award is not an employment contract, offers no right to future awards, and is not severance compensation.
- Affirms compliance intent with Section 409A; includes six-month payment delay for specified employees after separation, and defines payment timing for vested shares and dividend equivalents where applicable.
- Provides for equitable adjustments to RSUs in the event of corporate actions (splits, dividends, mergers, recapitalizations, etc.).
- Vests sole authority in the Committee to interpret and administer the award, determine termination reasons, apply post-employment and recovery provisions, decide claims, delegate authority, and make non-uniform determinations.
- Reserves the Committee’s right to amend the Award Agreement, with limits on materially adverse changes without consent except to comply with law, accounting rules, or to adjust vesting dates/impose restrictions consistent with Section 409A; amendments require HR Director’s signature.
- Includes severability and reformation of unenforceable provisions to make them enforceable.
- Permits accelerated distribution if required by government ethics/conflict-of-interest rules (subject to 409A), with rules for terminations under Government Office Requirements, Job Elimination, or Full Career Eligibility; accelerated awards remain subject to original recovery and employment restrictions.
- Acknowledges processing and disclosure of personal data to administer the award, including to service providers and tax/regulatory authorities.

nodes.title: Change in Outstanding Shares
nodes.heading: 38.11.6 Change in Outstanding Shares
nodes.start_phrase: In the event of any change in the outstanding shares of Common Stock by reason of any stock dividend or split, recapitalization, issuance of a new class of common stock, merger, consolidation, spin-off, combination or exchange of shares or other similar corporate change, or any distributions to stockholders of Common Stock other than regular cash dividends, the Committee will make an equitable substitution or proportionate adjustment, in the number or kind of shares of Common Stock or other securities issued or reserved for issuance pursuant to the Plan and to any RSUs outstanding under this award for such corporate events.
nodes.summary:
- Distribution timing and Section 409A: If you separate from service, delivery of shares may be delayed until the first calendar month after six full months post-separation to comply with Section 409A. If the award is no longer subject to a substantial risk of forfeiture, vested portions are paid on payment dates within the same calendar year following each vesting date, and dividend equivalents are paid on JPMorgan Chase’s dividend payment dates.
- Adjustments for corporate actions: In the event of stock splits/dividends, recapitalizations, new class issuance, mergers, consolidations, spin‑offs, share exchanges, or other similar events (excluding regular cash dividends), the Committee will make equitable substitutions or proportionate adjustments to shares or securities under the plan and outstanding RSUs.
- Administration and interpretation: The Committee has sole authority to interpret the plan and this award, determine termination reasons, apply post-employment and clawback provisions, decide claims, and delegate authority. Its (and the Firm’s/HR’s) determinations are binding and need not be uniform; selective, non‑uniform decisions and modifications are permitted.
- Amendment rights: The Committee (or nominee) may amend the Award Agreement at any time for any reason. No material adverse change without your consent, except as deemed advisable to comply with laws/regulations/accounting rules or to change vesting dates/impose certain restrictions consistent with Section 409A. Amendments must be in writing signed by the Director of Human Resources.
- Severability/reformation: If any portion is unenforceable, the Firm, a court/arbitrator, or the HR Director may reform it (e.g., duration, geography, scope) to make it enforceable under applicable law.
- Accelerated distribution for government ethics/conflicts: If required by applicable ethics/conflict‑of‑interest rules due to government employment, the Firm may accelerate distribution to meet divestiture deadlines, provided it does not violate Section 409A. Acceleration does not alter clawback/recovery timeframes (which track original vesting/distribution dates).
- Termination scenarios and acceleration scope: After voluntary termination meeting “Government Office Requirements,” acceleration applies to the portion that would continue to vest. If the award remains outstanding due to job elimination or full career eligibility, acceleration may apply to the full outstanding award.
- Continuing obligations after acceleration: Even if accelerated, you remain subject to all original award terms as if unaccelerated, including repayment (“Remedies”) and employment restrictions (“Protection‑Based Vesting,” “Government Office Requirements,” and “Full Career Eligibility”).
- Personal data use: By accepting the award, you consent to the Firm processing and disclosing your personal data to administer the award (e.g., share/unit registration, brokerage account setup) and to third parties such as service providers or tax/regulatory authorities for reporting and payroll.

nodes.title: Interpretation/Administration
nodes.heading: 38.11.7 Interpretation/Administration
nodes.start_phrase: The Committee has sole and complete authority to interpret and administer this Award Agreement, including,
nodes.summary:
- Post-separation distribution timing: If you separate from service, vested shares are delivered during the first calendar month after six full months from separation. If the award is no longer subject to a substantial risk of forfeiture under Section 409A, payment dates include the remainder of each calendar year following each vesting date for share delivery, and JPMorgan Chase’s dividend payment dates for dividend equivalents.
- Adjustments for corporate actions: In the case of stock splits/dividends, recapitalizations, mergers, spin-offs, exchanges, or similar events, the Committee will make equitable substitutions or proportional adjustments to plan share reserves and outstanding RSUs.
- Interpretation and administration: The Committee has sole authority to interpret the Plan/Award Agreement, determine termination reasons, apply post-employment obligations and recovery provisions, decide claims, and delegate authority. Determinations are binding and may be non-uniform or selective across participants.
- Amendments: The Committee (or nominee) may amend the Award Agreement at any time for any reason. nodes.title: Government Office Requirements

nodes.title: Eligibility
nodes.heading: 38.13.1 Eligibility
nodes.start_phrase: Eligibility for continued vesting is conditioned on your providing the Firm:
nodes.summary:

- Key definitions:
  - Firmwide Financial Threshold: Cumulative return on tangible common equity of at least 15% across calendar years 2023–2025, calculated as total net income over the three years divided by average year-end tangible equity over the same period.
  - Government Office: Full-time elected or appointed public office (including outside the U.S. or supranational roles) not intended as a full-career position, or a bona fide full-time campaign after formal filing where full-time campaigning is customary.
  - Line of Business (LoB): A business unit of the firm; Corporate Functions (including the Chief Investment Office) are treated as one LoB.
  - Line of Business Financial Thresholds: Performance triggers, based on management reporting, defined as:
    - Asset & Wealth Management: Annual negative pre-tax pre-provision income (PTPP).
    - Card and Auto; Commercial Banking; Consumer Banking, J.P. Morgan Wealth Management and Business Banking; Home Lending: Annual negative pre-tax pre-loan loss reserve income (PTPLLRI).
    - Corporate Investment Bank (CIB): Annual negative PTPP for CIB overall, or annual negative allocated product revenues (excluding XVA) for Fixed Income, Equities, Securities Services, Global Investment Banking, Payments.
    - Corporate Functions (incl. CIO): Annual negative PTPP at the Firm level.
    - PTPP = Revenue minus Expenses; PTPLLRI = Revenue minus (Expenses + Net Charge-offs).
  - Not-for-Profit Organization: U.S. Section 501(c)(3) entities and foreign equivalents organized exclusively for specified charitable, religious, educational, scientific, public safety testing, amateur sports, or cruelty-prevention purposes.
  - Recognized Service: Employee service as determined under the firm’s service-related policies.

- Government Office Requirements (continued vesting policy upon resignation for government service or candidacy):
  - Full Career Eligibility carve-out: If an employee qualifies for Full Career Eligibility at resignation, this section does not apply.
  - Eligibility conditions for continued vesting:
    - Provide at least 60 days’ advance written notice; cooperate professionally during notice; do not work for another employer during this period (firm may shorten the notice).
    - Confirm, in a form acceptable to the firm, that continued vesting complies with law/regulation.
    - Provide satisfactory documentation that resignation is to accept a Government Office or to become a candidate.
  - Portion of awards eligible for continued vesting (the “CV Award”):
    - 50% with ≥3 and <4 years of continuous service.
    - 75% with ≥4 and <5 years.
    - 100% with ≥5 years.
    - The non-eligible portion is canceled at termination.
  - Conditions to retain continued vesting:
    - Non-elective Government Office: Serve two or more years post-termination to receive the full CV Award; if service is shorter than two years, only tranches vesting during the service period are retained.
    - Elective office campaign: Employee’s name must appear on the primary or final public ballot.
  - Satisfaction of conditions:
    - If the above conditions are met (including if not elected after appearing on the ballot), any then-outstanding CV Awards continue to vest on the original schedule, subject to the same terms and employment restrictions as if the employee had resigned with Full Career Eligibility. References an “Accelerated Distribution for Ethics or Conflict Reasons Resulting From Employment by a Government Entity” provision for cases requiring accelerated share delivery.
  - Failure to satisfy conditions:
    - Outstanding RSUs under the CV Award are canceled.
    - Clawback: Repayment of the Fair Market Value (measured at distribution date, before withholding) of shares previously distributed that would otherwise have remained outstanding as RSUs but for accelerated distribution due to government ethics/conflict requirements.

- Notes:
  - Thresholds and results are aligned with the firm’s management reporting.
  - Employment restrictions continue to apply during the vesting period for CV Awards.
  - The document references additional sections (e.g., accelerated distribution for government ethics/conflicts, Full Career Eligibility) not fully included here.

nodes.title: Portion of Your Awards Subject to Continued Vesting
nodes.heading: 38.13.2 Portion of Your Awards Subject to Continued Vesting
nodes.start_phrase: Subject to the conditions below, the percentage of your outstanding awards that will continue to vest in accordance with this award’s original schedule will be based on your years of continuous service completed with the Firm immediately preceding your termination date, as follows:
nodes.summary:
- Requires documentation acceptable to the Firm that the resignation is to accept a Government Office or to become a candidate.
- Defines the portion of outstanding awards that continue to vest (the “CV Award”) based on continuous service at termination: 50% for 3–<4 years, 75% for 4–<5 years, 100% for 5+ years; the remainder is canceled at termination.
- Conditions to retain CV Awards:
  - Non-elective Government Office: serve 2+ years post-termination to receive full CV Award; if service is under 2 years, you keep only the portions scheduled to vest during your government service.
  - Elective office campaign: your name must appear on the primary or final ballot.
- If conditions are satisfied (2+ years in office, or on the ballot and not elected), any outstanding CV Awards—and awards that would have been outstanding but for ethics/conflict-driven accelerated distributions—continue to be subject, for the remaining vesting period, to the same terms as a resignation with Full Career Eligibility, including employment restrictions during vesting.
- If conditions are not met: remaining RSUs under the CV Award are canceled, and you must repay the fair market value (measured on the distribution date) of any shares previously distributed that would have still been outstanding as RSUs at the time of failure but for the accelerated distribution.

nodes.title: Conditions for Continued Vesting of Awards
nodes.heading: 38.13.3 Conditions for Continued Vesting of Awards
nodes.start_phrase: You must remain in a non-elective Government Office for two or more years after your employment with the Firm terminates to receive in full your CV Award; provided that if your non-elective Government Office is for a period less than two years, you will be entitled to retain any portion of the CV Award with a vesting date during your period of Government Service; or
nodes.summary:
- Purpose and documentation: Employee must provide documentation satisfactory to the Firm that resignation is to accept a Government Office or to become a candidate for a Government Office.
- Continued vesting eligibility: A portion of outstanding awards may continue to vest (the “CV Award”) based on continuous service at termination: 50% for 3–<4 years; 75% for 4–<5 years; 100% for 5+ years. Any portion not subject to continued vesting is canceled at termination.
- Conditions to keep CV Awards:
  - Non‑elective office: Must remain in a non‑elective Government Office for at least two years after termination. If the office term is shorter than two years, only the portion with vesting dates during the period of Government Service is retained.
  - Elective office candidacy: If resigning to campaign, the employee’s name must appear on the primary or final public ballot.
- Satisfaction of conditions: If the above conditions are met (including being on the ballot and not elected), any then‑outstanding CV Awards—and any awards that would have been outstanding but for accelerated distributions due to ethics/conflict rules—continue under the Award Agreement for the remaining vesting period on the same terms as if the employee had resigned with Full Career Eligibility, including applicable employment restrictions during vesting.
- Failure to satisfy conditions: All outstanding RSUs under each CV Award are canceled, and the employee must repay the Fair Market Value (measured on distribution date, before withholdings) of any shares previously distributed early due to ethics/conflict reasons that would have remained outstanding as RSUs on the failure date.

nodes.title: Satisfaction of Conditions
nodes.heading: 38.13.4 Satisfaction of Conditions
nodes.start_phrase: If your service in a Government Office ends two years or more after your employment with the Firm terminates, or in the case of resignation from the Firm to campaign for a Government Office, your name is on the primary or final public ballot for the election and you are not elected, any CV Awards then outstanding and any such awards that would have then been outstanding but for an accelerated distribution of shares (as described in the subsection captioned “Accelerated Distribution for Ethics or Conflict Reasons Resulting From Employment by a Government Entity”) will be subject for the remainder of the applicable vesting period to the same terms and conditions of this Award Agreement, including employment restrictions during the vesting period, as if you had resigned from the Firm having met the requirements for Full Career Eligibility.
nodes.summary:

- Conditions to keep vesting:
  - Non‑elective office: must serve 2+ years post-termination to retain the full CV Award; if service is under 2 years, only tranches with vesting dates during the government service are retained.

- If conditions are satisfied:

  - Clawback: repay the Fair Market Value (measured at distribution date) of shares previously distributed via accelerated distribution that would have remained outstanding RSUs on the failure date.
- References and notes: incorporates defined terms (e.g., Full Career Eligibility), and references accelerated distributions for ethics/conflict reasons tied to government employment; employment restrictions apply during any remaining vesting.

nodes.title: Failure to Satisfy Conditions
nodes.heading: 38.13.5 Failure to Satisfy Conditions
nodes.start_phrase: If you do not satisfy the above “Conditions for Continued Vesting of Awards”, any outstanding RSUs under each CV Award will be cancelled.

nodes.title: Award Agreement

nodes.title: Protection-Based Vesting

nodes.start_phrase: This award is intended and expected to vest on the vesting date(s), provided that you are continuously employed by the Firm through such vesting date, or you meet the requirements for continued vesting described under the subsections “--Job Elimination”, “--Full Career Eligibility”, “--Government Office” or “--Disability”.
nodes.summary:
- Document sets terms for a January 17, 2023 Restricted Stock Unit (RSU) award under the JPMorgan Chase & Co. Long-Term Incentive Plan for Operating Committee members; the Plan governs in case of conflict and, with the Prospectus, supersedes prior agreements.

- Termination of employment: RSUs are generally cancelled upon termination unless specific exceptions apply (Job Elimination, Full Career Eligibility, Government Office, Disability, or Death). Continued vesting may occur if conditions are met.

nodes.title: Holding Requirement
nodes.heading: 38.19 Holding Requirement
nodes.start_phrase: As of each vesting date, you shall be entitled to a distribution equal to the Fair Market Value of the number of RSUs vesting on such date, less the number being withheld to satisfy tax withholding obligations.
nodes.summary:

nodes.title: Bonus Recoupment
nodes.heading: 38.20 Bonus Recoupment
nodes.start_phrase: In consideration of the grant of this award, you agree that you are subject to the JPMorgan Chase Bonus Recoupment Policy (or successor policy) as in effect from time to time as it applies both to the cash incentive compensation awarded to you for performance year 2022 and to this award.

Continued vesting post-termination is only available under those exceptions and remains subject to other terms (Protection-Based Vesting, Recoupment, EMEA Malus/Clawback, Obligations, Remedies).

nodes.title: EMEA Malus and Clawback Policy – Identified Staff
nodes.heading: 38.21 EMEA Malus and Clawback Policy – Identified Staff
nodes.start_phrase: In consideration of grant of this award, and without prejudice to any other provision of this Award Agreement, you agree that you are subject to the JPMorgan Chase EMEA Malus and Clawback Policy - Identified Staff (and any applicable supplement(s) to that policy) or successor policy as in effect from time to time as it applies both to the cash incentive compensation awarded to you for performance year 2022 and to this award.
