nodes.title: Termination of Employment
nodes.heading: 38.22 Termination of Employment
nodes.start_phrase: Except as explicitly set forth below under the subsections captioned “--Job Elimination”, “--Full Career Eligibility”, “--Government Office” or “--Disability” or under the section captioned “ Death ”, any RSUs outstanding under this award will be cancelled effective on the date your employment with the Firm terminates for any reason.
nodes.summary:
Summary of main points in the partial document:

- Scope and governance: Sets terms for JPMorgan Chase RSU awards, including protection-based vesting. Any determinations on such vesting are subject to Compensation and Management Development Committee ratification; for the CEO, by the Committee and ratified by the Board.

- Interaction with government-related employment: If employment ends due to Job Elimination, Full Career Eligibility, Government Office, or Disability, cancellation rules for At Risk RSUs still apply, including potential accelerated distribution for ethics/conflict reasons tied to Government employment.

- Holding requirement: On each vest date, vested RSUs are distributed at fair market value net of tax withholding, then held in a restricted, non-transferable account for 12 months; these restrictions lapse upon death.

- Bonus Recoupment Policy: Award and 2022 cash incentive are subject to JPMorgan Chase’s Bonus Recoupment Policy; nothing in the award limits the Firm’s rights under that policy.

- EMEA Malus and Clawback (Identified Staff): Award and 2022 cash incentive are subject to malus/clawback provisions permitting reduction or recovery, including in a material firm performance downturn or increased capital needs; aligns with Firmwide recoupment and protection-based vesting terms.

- General termination rule: RSUs cancel upon employment termination unless specifically covered under Job Elimination, Full Career Eligibility, Government Office, Disability, or Death. Any continued vesting remains subject to protection-based vesting, recoupment, EMEA malus/clawback, and other obligations/remedies.

- Continued vesting—Job Elimination: Requires HR determination that the role was eliminated, cooperative/professional transition services, and satisfaction of release/certification requirements.

- Continued vesting—Full Career Eligibility: Requires voluntary termination; at least 5 years continuous service; 15+ years Recognized Service or 30+ combined Recognized Service and external experience; at least 180 days advance written notice with cooperative service and no outside work during notice; a pre-termination appropriateness determination based on performance/conduct; 36 months post-grant restriction on working for a Financial Services Company or in one’s profession (government/education/not-for-profit permitted); and release/certification. The Firm may require continued service during the notice period or shorten it (not earlier than service requirement); additional notice policies may apply.

- Continued vesting—Government Office: Applies when voluntarily leaving to accept or run for a Government Office, subject to the Government Office Requirements and definitions.

- Continued vesting—Disability: Applies if termination is due to qualifying long-term disability (under the Firm’s LTD plan or equivalent, or would qualify), with a written request within 30 days, supporting documentation, Firm consent, and release/certification.

- Release/Certification requirements: Include executing a release of claims; for Full Career, pre-termination confirmation of eligibility and written consent; for Full Career and Government Office, ongoing certification of compliance with employment restrictions before each vest; for Disability, timely notice/documentation and consent; and compliance with all other award obligations.

- Death: If death occurs while eligible to vest, RSUs immediately vest and are distributed (net of withholding) to the designated beneficiary; restrictions on held distributions also lapse upon death.

nodes.title: Release/Certification
nodes.heading: 38.23 Release/Certification
nodes.start_phrase: To qualify for continued vesting after termination of your employment under any of the foregoing circumstances:
nodes.summary:
Summary of main points in the partial document:

- Continued vesting under “Full Career Eligibility” after voluntary termination:
  - At least 5 years of continuous service immediately before termination.
  - Either 15+ years of Recognized Service, or 30+ years combined Recognized Service and external professional experience (as attested).
  - At least 180 days’ advance written notice; during notice you must perform requested services cooperatively, professionally, and not work for any other employer.
  - Firm must determine, before termination, that continued vesting is appropriate based on your performance and conduct.
  - For 36 months from grant, you must not work in any capacity for a Financial Services Company or in your profession; exception allows work for government, education, or Not‑for‑Profit organizations.
  - Must satisfy Release/Certification Requirements.
  - Firm may require you to continue working during the notice period or may shorten it (not earlier than the date you meet the service requirement). Additional notice period policies may apply.

- Government Office:
  - Special treatment if you voluntarily leave to accept or run for a Government Office, subject to separate “Government Office Requirements” and definitions.

- Disability:
  - Continued vesting possible if employment ends due to long‑term disability (under the JPMorgan Chase LTD Plan or equivalent, or a disability that would qualify), provided you:
    - Request continued vesting in writing within 30 days of termination,
    - Provide requested documentation, and
    - Receive the Firm’s written consent,
    - And satisfy Release/Certification Requirements.

- Release/Certification Requirements for any continued vesting:
  - Execute a Firm‑specified release of claims.
  - For Full Career Eligibility: before termination, confirm eligibility (including 180‑day notice) with management and obtain written consent.
  - For Full Career Eligibility and Government Office: certify before each vesting date that you have complied with post‑termination employment restrictions.
  - For Disability: meet notice/documentation requirements and obtain written consent.
  - Comply with all other terms of the Award Agreement.

- Death:
  - If you die while eligible to vest, RSUs immediately vest and are distributed (after tax withholding) to your designated beneficiary on file; fallback recipient is referenced but the text is truncated.

- Notes/References:
  - Concepts defined elsewhere include Recognized Service, Financial Services Company, Not‑for‑Profit Organization, Government Office, and Notice Period.

nodes.title: Death
nodes.heading: 38.24 Death
nodes.start_phrase: If you die while you are eligible to vest in RSUs under this award, the RSUs will immediately vest and will be distributed in shares of Common Stock (after applicable tax withholding) to your designated beneficiary on file with the Firm’s Stock Administration Department, or if no beneficiary has been designated or survives you or if beneficiary designation is not recognized locally, then to your estate unless otherwise required by local legislation.
nodes.summary:
- Outlines conditions for continued vesting of RSUs after voluntary termination under “Full Career Eligibility,” requiring: at least 5 years of continuous service; 15 years of Recognized Service or 30 years combined internal/external experience; 180 days’ advance written notice; cooperative service during notice with no outside work; HR’s prior determination based on performance/conduct; and a 36-month post-grant restriction from working in any capacity for a Financial Services Company or in one’s profession (with permitted work for government, education, or not-for-profit). The firm may require work during the notice period or shorten it (not before service eligibility), and additional notice rules may apply.
- Provides separate pathways for continued vesting upon voluntary termination to accept or run for a Government Office, subject to defined “Government Office Requirements.”
- Provides continued vesting eligibility in cases of long-term disability aligned with the applicable LTD Plan, contingent on timely written request, documentation, and firm consent.
- Specifies Release/Certification requirements: execute a firm-specified release of claims; pre-termination confirmation and written consent for Full Career Eligibility; ongoing certification of compliance with employment restrictions prior to each vesting date for Full Career Eligibility and Government Office; disability-related notices/documentation and consent; and compliance with all Award Agreement terms.
- Details death provisions: immediate vesting and distribution of RSUs to the designated beneficiary (or estate), generally within 60 days of receiving required documentation and no later than the end of the calendar year following death.
- Sets post-employment obligations:
  - Non-solicitation of employees and customers: for the longer of 1 year post-termination or 3 years from grant if the award is not canceled, prohibits soliciting/hiring certain employees and soliciting/diverting customers/suppliers known through employment, with limited exceptions (e.g., publicly known institutional customers and authorized actions during employment).
  - Confidentiality: prohibits use/disclosure of confidential information and media communications about the firm; bans accessing internal systems post-termination; includes safe harbors for lawful reporting, regulators, and truthful legal responses.
  - Non-disparagement: prohibits public statements that disparage the firm or its stakeholders, with exceptions for lawful reporting and truthful legal responses.
  - Cooperation: requires cooperation in audits, litigation, investigations, etc., with reimbursement of reasonable out-of-pocket expenses.
  - Compliance with Award Agreement: requires providing information to verify compliance and authorizes the firm to disclose award terms to affected third parties, including prospective employers.

nodes.title: Your Obligations
nodes.heading: 38.25 Your Obligations
nodes.start_phrase: In consideration of the grant of this award, you agree to comply with and be bound by the obligations set forth below next to the subsections captioned “--Non-Solicitation of Employees and Customers”, “--Confidential Information”, “--Non-Disparagement”, ”-- Cooperation”, “--Compliance with Award Agreement” and “--Notice Period.”
nodes.summary:
- Post-death share handling: Upon a participant’s death, any shares are to be distributed to the beneficiary or estate (subject to local law) no later than the end of the calendar year following the year of death. Administratively, the firm aims to register shares in the beneficiary’s or estate’s name within 60 days after receiving required documentation.
- Employee obligations as consideration for the award:
  - Non-solicitation of employees and customers: During employment and for the longer of (i) one year post-termination or (ii) three years from the grant date if the award is not canceled at termination, the participant may not solicit or hire certain firm employees, or solicit/induce/divert firm customers, suppliers, or other business relationships serviced by or known to the participant through employment, with limited exceptions (e.g., publicly known institutional customers without use of confidential information; normal, authorized actions during employment; certain job-elimination or six-month separation hiring exceptions).
  - Confidential information: No use or disclosure of the firm’s confidential information or media communications about the firm, its customers, or employees during or after employment, except as permitted by the Code of Conduct, law, or legal process; no unauthorized access to internal systems after termination. Whistleblowing and truthful cooperation with regulators, government, courts, or firm leadership are expressly permitted.
  - Non-disparagement: No public statements intended or reasonably likely to disparage the firm or its employees, officers, directors, or shareholders, with carveouts for lawful reporting and truthful responses to government, regulatory, or court inquiries.
  - Cooperation: Ongoing duty to fully cooperate and provide accurate information in audits, tax matters, litigation, investigations, or governmental proceedings, with reimbursement for reasonable out-of-pocket expenses.
  - Compliance with Award Agreement: Obligation to provide information reasonably requested to assess compliance and authorization for the firm to disclose agreement terms to affected third parties, including prospective employers.
  - Notice Period: Identified as an obligation category, though details are not included in this excerpt.

nodes.title: Non-Solicitation of Employees and Customers
nodes.heading: 38.25.1 Non-Solicitation of Employees and Customers
nodes.start_phrase: During your employment by the Firm and for the longer of the (i) one year period following the termination of your employment or, (ii) if your award is not cancelled as of your termination date, the three year period from Grant Date, you will not directly or indirectly, whether on your own behalf or on behalf of any other party, without the prior written consent of the Director of Human Resources: (i) solicit, induce or encourage any of the Firm’s then current employees to leave the Firm or to apply for employment elsewhere, unless such current employee has received official, written notice that his or her employment will be terminated due to job elimination, (ii) hire any employee or former employee who was employed by the Firm at the date your employment terminated, unless the individual’s employment terminated because his or her job was eliminated, or the individual’s employment with the Firm has been terminated for more than six months, (iii) to the fullest extent enforceable under applicable law, solicit or induce or attempt to induce to leave the Firm, or divert or attempt to divert from doing business with the Firm, any then current customers, suppliers or other persons or entities that were serviced by you or whose names became known to you by virtue of your employment with the Firm, or otherwise interfere with the relationship between the Firm and such customers, suppliers or other persons or entities.
nodes.summary:
- Death and distribution: Any shares due at death are distributed to the designated beneficiary or estate (subject to local law) no later than the end of the calendar year following the year of death; administratively, the firm aims to register such shares to the beneficiary/estate within 60 days of receiving required documentation.
- Non-solicitation: During employment and for the longer of 1 year post-termination or 3 years from the grant date (if the award isn’t canceled), you may not solicit or induce employees to leave, hire recent former employees (with exceptions for job eliminations or those separated more than six months), or solicit/divert customers, suppliers, or other parties you serviced or learned of through your role (with a carve-out for publicly known institutional customers serviced after leaving without using confidential information). Normal authorized job duties are excluded.
- Confidentiality: During and after employment, you may not use or disclose the firm’s confidential information or communicate with media about firm matters except as allowed by policy, law, or legal process; after termination, you may not access internal systems without authorization. Safe harbors permit reporting suspected legal or Code of Conduct violations to management, regulators, government, attorneys, or courts and truthful responses to official inquiries.
- Non-disparagement: You may not make or encourage public statements that disparage the firm or its employees, officers, directors, or shareholders as a group, with exceptions for lawful reporting or cooperation with regulators or courts.
- Cooperation: You must cooperate fully and provide accurate information in audits, tax matters, litigation, investigations, or governmental proceedings, with reimbursement of reasonable out-of-pocket expenses.
- Compliance: You must provide information requested to assess compliance with the Award Agreement and authorize the firm to disclose its terms to affected third parties, including prospective employers.
- Referenced but not detailed here: a “Notice Period” obligation.

nodes.title: Confidential Information
nodes.heading: 38.25.2 Confidential Information
nodes.start_phrase: You will not, either during your employment with the Firm or thereafter, directly or indirectly (i) use or disclose to anyone any confidential information related to the Firm’s business, or (ii) communicate with the press or other media about matters related to the Firm, its customers or employees, including matters and activities relating to your employment, or the employment of others, by the Firm, in the case of either (i) or (ii), except as explicitly permitted by the JPMorgan Chase Code of Conduct and applicable policies or law or legal process.
nodes.summary:
- Post-death distribution: Any award shares pass to your beneficiary or estate (subject to local law). Distribution occurs no later than the end of the calendar year following the year of death; as an administrative practice, shares are registered to the beneficiary/estate within 60 days after required documents are received.
- Obligations tied to the award:
  - Non-solicitation of employees and customers: During employment and for the longer of (i) one year after termination or (ii) three years from the grant date if the award isn’t canceled at termination, you may not: solicit or induce Firm employees to leave; hire recent Firm employees (with defined exceptions); or, to the fullest extent permitted by law, solicit/divert Firm customers, suppliers, or others you serviced or learned of through your job. Exceptions include actions taken in the ordinary course of your role and publicly known institutional customers served after employment without using the Firm’s confidential information.
  - Confidential information: You may not use or disclose Firm confidential information or communicate with the media about Firm-related matters during or after employment, except as allowed by the JPMorgan Chase Code of Conduct, law, or legal process. After termination, you may not access the Firm’s internal systems without written authorization. Safe harbors allow truthful reporting to management, directors, government/regulators, attorneys, or courts.
  - Non-disparagement: No public statements intended to disparage the Firm or its people during or after employment, with the same legal/reporting carve-outs as above.
  - Cooperation: You must fully cooperate and provide accurate information to the Firm and its counsel in audits, tax matters, litigation, investigations, or governmental proceedings, with reimbursement of reasonable out-of-pocket expenses.
  - Compliance with Award Agreement: You must provide information reasonably requested to verify compliance and authorize the Firm to disclose the agreement’s terms to affected third parties, including prospective employers.
- The “Notice Period” subsection is referenced among obligations but its terms are not included in this excerpt.

nodes.title: Non-Disparagement
nodes.heading: 38.25.3 Non-Disparagement
nodes.start_phrase: You will not, either during your employment with the Firm or thereafter, make or encourage others to make any public statement or release any information in verbal, written, electronic or any other form, that is intended to, or reasonably could be foreseen to, disparage, embarrass or criticize the Firm or its employees, officers, directors or shareholders as a group.
nodes.summary:
- Post-death share handling: Shares from the award are to be distributed by the end of the calendar year following the year of death; administratively, the firm aims to register shares to the beneficiary or estate within 60 days after receiving required documentation.
- Non-solicitation: For the longer of one year post-termination or three years from grant (if the award isn’t canceled at termination), the employee may not solicit or hire certain current/former employees, nor solicit or divert customers, suppliers, or other business relationships known through employment, with noted exceptions (e.g., job eliminations, six-month lapse, publicly known institutional customers without using confidential information, and authorized actions in the normal course of employment).
- Confidentiality: During and after employment, the employee may not use or disclose the firm’s confidential information or communicate with media about firm-related matters, and post-termination cannot access internal systems without authorization. “Confidential information” follows the firm’s Code of Conduct. Whistleblowing and truthful responses to government/regulatory/legal requests are expressly permitted.
- Non-disparagement: Prohibits public statements likely to disparage the firm or its group of employees/officers/directors/shareholders, with carveouts for lawful reporting and truthful cooperation with authorities or courts.
- Cooperation: Requires full cooperation and accurate information in audits, tax matters, litigation, investigations, or governmental proceedings, with reimbursement of reasonable out-of-pocket expenses.
- Compliance with Award Agreement: Employee must provide information to verify compliance and authorizes the firm to disclose award terms to affected third parties, including prospective employers.

nodes.title: Cooperation
nodes.heading: 38.25.4 Cooperation
nodes.start_phrase: You will cooperate fully with and provide full and accurate information to the Firm and its counsel with respect to any matter (including any audit, tax proceeding, litigation, investigation or governmental proceeding) with respect to which you may have knowledge or information, subject to reimbursement for actual, appropriate and reasonable out-of-pocket expenses incurred by you.
nodes.summary:
- Specifies post-death share handling: shares transferred to beneficiary or estate and registered within about 60 days upon receipt of required documents; in all cases distributed no later than the end of the calendar year following the year of death.
- Sets employee obligations as consideration for the award, covering Non-Solicitation, Confidential Information, Non-Disparagement, Cooperation, Compliance with the Award Agreement, and a referenced Notice Period.
- Non-Solicitation: For the longer of (i) one year after employment ends or (ii) three years from grant date if the award isn’t canceled at termination, prohibits (a) soliciting or encouraging Firm employees to leave (with job-elimination exception), (b) hiring Firm employees for six months post-employment unless their role was eliminated, and (c) soliciting/diverting Firm customers, suppliers, or other relationships known or serviced through employment, to the fullest extent permitted by law; excludes publicly known institutional customers serviced without using confidential information and normal, authorized actions taken during employment.
- Confidential Information: Prohibits using or disclosing Firm confidential information and communicating with media about Firm matters during and after employment, and bars post-employment access to Firm systems without authorization; allows lawful reporting to management, directors, government, regulators, self-regulatory agencies, attorneys, or courts, and truthful responses to legal/regulatory inquiries.
- Non-Disparagement: Prohibits public statements that could disparage or criticize the Firm or its stakeholders, with carve-outs for lawful reporting and truthful participation in legal or regulatory matters.
- Cooperation: Requires full cooperation and accurate information in audits, tax matters, litigation, investigations, or governmental proceedings, with reimbursement of reasonable out-of-pocket expenses.
- Compliance with Award Agreement: Requires providing information to verify compliance and authorizes the Firm to disclose award terms to affected third parties, including prospective employers.

nodes.title: Compliance with Award Agreement
nodes.heading: 38.25.5 Compliance with Award Agreement
nodes.start_phrase: You will provide the Firm with any information reasonably requested to determine compliance with the Award Agreement, and you authorize the Firm to disclose the terms of the Award Agreement to any third party who might be affected thereby, including your prospective employer.
nodes.summary:
- Sets post-death handling of shares: distribution by the end of the year following death; administrative practice to register shares to beneficiary/estate within 60 days after receiving required documentation, subject to local law.
- Conditions of award acceptance include obligations on non-solicitation, confidentiality, non-disparagement, cooperation, compliance with the award agreement, and a referenced notice period.
- Non-solicitation: for the longer of 1 year post-termination or 3 years from grant date (if award not canceled), prohibits soliciting or hiring certain Firm employees, and soliciting/diverting customers, suppliers, or other business contacts known through employment; allows normal-course authorized actions and excludes publicly known institutional customers serviced post-employment without using confidential information.
- Confidentiality: no use or disclosure of Firm confidential information or media communications about Firm matters during or after employment; no access to Firm internal systems post-termination without authorization; confidentiality defined by the Firm’s Code of Conduct; preserves rights to report to management, regulators, government, attorneys, or courts and to respond truthfully to legal/regulatory inquiries.
- Non-disparagement: no public statements intended or reasonably likely to disparage the Firm or groups of its people; preserves rights to report violations and respond truthfully in legal/regulatory contexts.
- Cooperation: obligation to assist the Firm and its counsel in audits, tax matters, litigation, investigations, or governmental proceedings, with reimbursement of reasonable out-of-pocket expenses.
- Compliance: must provide information to confirm adherence to the Award Agreement and authorize the Firm to disclose its terms to affected third parties, including prospective employers.

nodes.title: Notice Period
nodes.heading: 38.25.6 Notice Period
nodes.start_phrase: If you are subject to a notice period or become subject to a notice period after the Grant Date, whether by contract or by policy, that requires you to provide advance written notice of your intention to terminate your employment (“Notice Period”), then as consideration for this award and continued employment, you will provide the Firm with the necessary advance written notice that applies to you, as specified by such contract or policy.
nodes.summary:
- Establishes Notice Period obligations: if subject to a contractual or policy-based notice period, employee must give the required advance written notice to terminate employment. After notice, the Firm may require continued work or place the employee on paid leave during the period. During the Notice Period, the employee must devote full time and loyalty to the Firm, refrain from working for others, and will receive base salary and certain benefits. The length can be mutually waived/modified. Separately, a 180‑day advance notice under “Full Career Eligibility” is required when terminating under that subsection.
- Details Remedies—Cancellation/Recapture: up to 100% of outstanding RSUs may be canceled at the Firm’s sole discretion for detrimental or risk-related conduct, including: conduct causing material financial or reputational harm; awards based on materially inaccurate performance metrics (regardless of fault) or material misrepresentation; failure to timely identify/raise/assess material risks; termination for Cause or post-termination determination that Cause existed; failure to comply with advance notice/cooperation requirements or employment restrictions related to termination; failure to return required Release/Certification forms by deadline; or violations of “Your Obligations.” The Firm may suspend vesting and/or share distributions while evaluating cancellation/recovery and is not responsible for market fluctuations during suspension; units may be reinstated per plan procedures.
- Outlines Recovery (clawback) of distributed shares: employee may be required to repay up to the fair market value of gross shares previously distributed. Recovery can apply to shares distributed within three years prior to a notice-of-recovery for fraudulent acts, knowing and willful misconduct, violations of “Your Obligations,” or violations of post-termination employment restrictions under “Full Career Eligibility” or “Government Office.” Recovery can also apply to shares distributed within one year prior to notice-of-recovery for the detrimental/risk-related conduct listed above. A notice-of-recovery is written (including electronic) notice requiring or evaluating repayment.

nodes.title: Remedies
nodes.heading: 38.26 Remedies
nodes.start_phrase: In addition to the cancellation provisions described under the sections captioned “ Protection-Based Vesting ”, “Bonus Recoupment ”, “EMEA Malus and Clawback Policy - Identified Staff ”, and “ Termination of Employment ”, up to 100% of your outstanding RSUs under this award may be cancelled if the Firm in its sole discretion determines that:
nodes.summary:
- Notice Period obligations:
  - If you are subject to a contractual or policy-based notice period, you must provide the required advance written notice before resigning.
  - After notice, the Firm may have you continue working or place you on paid leave during the notice period.
  - During the notice period, you must devote full time and loyalty to the Firm, not work for another employer, and you will continue to receive base salary and certain benefits.
  - The length of the notice period can be mutually waived or modified.
  - Separately, a 180‑day advance notice applies if you terminate under the “Full Career Eligibility” provision.

- Remedies—cancellation/recapture of RSUs (Firm’s sole discretion):
  - Up to 100% of outstanding RSUs may be cancelled if:
    - You engage in conduct causing material financial or reputational harm to the Firm.
    - The award was based on materially inaccurate performance metrics (regardless of your responsibility).
    - The award was based on your material misrepresentation.
    - You improperly or with gross negligence fail to identify, raise, or assess material risks in a timely, reasonably expected manner.
    - Your employment is terminated for Cause, or it is determined post-termination that Cause existed.
    - You fail to comply with advance notice, cooperation requirements, or employment restrictions.
    - You fail to return required Release/Certification forms by the deadline.
    - You violate obligations outlined under “Your Obligations.”
  - The Firm may suspend vesting and/or share distribution while evaluating cancellation, recovery, or distribution conditions; it is not responsible for price fluctuations during suspension, and suspended units may be reinstated per plan procedures.

- Recovery (clawback of previously distributed shares):
  - You may have to repay up to the Fair Market Value (at vesting) of shares previously distributed:
    - For shares distributed within three years before a notice-of-recovery if the Firm determines you committed fraud, engaged in knowing and willful misconduct, violated “Your Obligations,” or violated post-employment restrictions under “Full Career Eligibility” or “Government Office.”
    - For shares distributed within one year before a notice-of-recovery if appropriate due to the detrimental/risk-related conduct listed above.
  - “Notice-of-recovery” is written (including electronic) notice requiring payment or stating the Firm is evaluating requiring payment.

nodes.title: Detrimental Conduct, Risk Related and Other Cancellation/Recapture
nodes.heading: 38.26.1 Detrimental Conduct, Risk Related and Other Cancellation/Recapture
nodes.start_phrase: In addition to the cancellation provisions described under the sections captioned “ Protection-Based Vesting ”, “Bonus Recoupment ”, “EMEA Malus and Clawback Policy - Identified Staff ”, and “ Termination of Employment ”, up to 100% of your outstanding RSUs under this award may be cancelled if the Firm in its sole discretion determines that:
nodes.summary:
- Notice Period obligations: If subject to a contractual or policy-based advance notice requirement, you must provide written notice before resigning. After notice, the Firm may require you to continue working or place you on paid leave during the notice period. During this time, you must devote full time and loyalty to the Firm, refrain from working for others, and will continue to receive base salary and certain benefits. The notice period length may be mutually modified. Regardless of any individual notice requirement, a 180-day advance notice under “Full Career Eligibility” applies if you terminate under that subsection.

- Remedies—Cancellation/Recapture of RSUs: Up to 100% of outstanding RSUs may be cancelled, in addition to other policy-based provisions, if the Firm determines any of the following:
  - Detrimental or risk-related conduct, including: material financial or reputational harm to the Firm; awards based on materially inaccurate performance metrics or your material misrepresentation; improper or grossly negligent failure to timely identify/raise/assess material risks; termination for Cause or post-termination determination that Cause existed.
  - Failure to comply with advance notice/cooperation requirements or employment restrictions upon termination.
  - Failure to return required Release/Certification forms by the deadline.
  - Violation of “Your Obligations.”

- Suspension rights: The Firm may suspend vesting and/or share distributions while evaluating cancellation/recovery or distribution conditions. It is not responsible for price fluctuations during suspension; suspended units may be reinstated per plan procedures. See also “No Ownership Rights/Other Limitations.”

- Recovery (clawback) of previously distributed shares: You may be required to repay up to the Fair Market Value (as of vesting) of shares already distributed:
  - For any shares distributed within three years prior to a notice-of-recovery if the Firm determines you committed a fraudulent act, engaged in knowing and willful misconduct, violated “Your Obligations,” or violated employment restrictions under “Full Career Eligibility” or “Government Office” after termination.
  - For any shares distributed within one year prior to a notice-of-recovery if the Firm deems it appropriate due to the detrimental/risk-related conduct listed above.
  - Notice-of-recovery is written (including electronic) notice requiring or indicating evaluation of repayment.

nodes.title: Recovery
nodes.heading: 38.26.2 Recovery
nodes.start_phrase: In addition, you may be required to pay the Firm up to an amount equal to the Fair Market Value (determined as of the applicable vesting date) of the gross number of shares of Common Stock previously distributed under this award as follows:
nodes.summary:
- Notice Period obligations: Employees subject to a contractual/policy notice period must give advance written notice as a condition of the award and continued employment. The Firm may require work or place the employee on paid leave during the Notice Period; the employee must devote full time and loyalty, not work elsewhere, and will receive base pay and certain benefits. The length may be mutually waived/modified. Separately, a 180‑day advance notice applies for terminations under “Full Career Eligibility.”
- Remedies—Cancellation/Recapture: Up to 100% of outstanding RSUs can be canceled at the Firm’s discretion for detrimental or risk‑related conduct, including material financial/reputational harm, awards based on inaccurate metrics or misrepresentation, failure to identify/escalate material risks, termination for (or that could have been for) Cause, failure to meet notice/cooperation or employment restrictions, failure to return required Release/Certification forms, or violating “Your Obligations.” The Firm may suspend vesting and/or share distributions during evaluations; it is not responsible for market fluctuations during suspension.
- Recovery (clawback): The Firm may require repayment up to the FMV of previously distributed shares (gross, as of vest dates). Recovery can apply to shares distributed within three years before notice-of-recovery for fraud, knowing/willful misconduct, violations of “Your Obligations,” or post‑termination employment restriction breaches (“Full Career Eligibility” or “Government Office”). It can also apply to shares distributed within one year for the detrimental/risk‑related conduct noted above. Notice-of-recovery may be electronic and is effective upon good‑faith delivery to the last known address; evaluation notices preserve recovery rights. Recovery targets shares retained after tax liabilities; amounts representing irrevocable tax withholdings/payments will not be required. Repayment may be in shares or cash and is not a penalty. Obligations under separate Bonus Recoupment and EMEA Malus/Clawback policies remain in force.
- Right to an injunction: The Firm may seek injunctive relief for violations, in addition to other legal/equitable remedies.
- Administrative provisions:
  - Withholding taxes: The Firm may retain shares, sell shares, withhold from cash compensation, or hold shares until taxes are paid to satisfy tax obligations.
  - Right to set‑off: Subject to law (including Section 409A), the Firm may retain funds/shares from vesting to satisfy debts owed to the Firm, but will not recover from the employee’s funds/unrestricted securities held at the Firm without consent (except for certain accounts referenced elsewhere).
  - No ownership rights/other limitations: RSUs confer no ownership or voting rights until vesting; shares are issued per Firm procedures. By accepting, the employee authorizes establishment of a brokerage/book‑entry account for delivery of vested shares. Vesting may be suspended and outstanding RSUs canceled if cancellation provisions apply. The Firm may impose post‑vesting restrictions (e.g., sale, transfer, pledge, hedging) for specified periods without affecting voting/dividend rights.

nodes.title: Right to an Injunction
nodes.heading: 38.26.3 Right to an Injunction
nodes.start_phrase: You acknowledge that a violation or attempted violation of the obligations set forth herein will cause immediate and irreparable damage to the Firm, and therefore agree that the Firm shall be entitled as a matter of right to an injunction, from any court of competent jurisdiction, restraining any violation or further violation of such obligations; such right to an injunction, however, shall be cumulative and in addition to whatever other remedies the Firm may have under law or equity.
nodes.summary:
- Defines notice-of-recovery: deemed delivered if the Firm makes a good-faith written/electronic attempt to your last known address; such notice preserves JPMorgan Chase’s right to require repayment, and the Firm may complete or discontinue its evaluation at its sole discretion.
- Clarifies recovery scope for tax-withheld shares: “shares distributed” include shares withheld for taxes, but repayment will only apply to shares you retain after tax determination; no repayment is required for irrevocable tax withholdings or tax payments that cannot be recovered; the Firm (or its nominee) decides this in its sole discretion.
- Permits repayment in cash or Common Stock and characterizes any repayment as a lawful recovery, not a penalty.
- States that these provisions do not limit obligations under Bonus Recoupment and the EMEA Malus and Clawback Policy – Identified Staff.
- Provides a right to injunctive relief: any breach causes irreparable harm, allowing the Firm to obtain an injunction in addition to other legal or equitable remedies.
- Withholding taxes: the Firm may withhold shares, sell shares to cover taxes, withhold from cash compensation as required by law, or retain vested shares until you pay taxes to authorities.
- Right to set-off: subject to applicable law (including Section 409A), the Firm may retain funds or stock from vesting to satisfy debts you owe the Firm; it will not recover from your funds or unrestricted securities held at the Firm without your consent, except for certain accounts referenced under No Ownership Rights/Other Limitations.
- No ownership rights before vesting: RSUs confer no stock ownership or voting rights until vest; shares are issued per Firm procedures; you authorize the Firm to open a brokerage or book-entry account to deliver vested shares.
- Potential suspension/cancellation: RSUs can be suspended or canceled per referenced sections (Protection-Based Vesting, Bonus Recoupment, EMEA Malus and Clawback, Termination, Remedies) and amendment provisions.
- Post-vesting restrictions: the Firm may temporarily restrict sale, transfer, pledge, assignment, hedging, or encumbrance of issued shares; these restrictions do not affect voting or dividend rights.

nodes.title: Administrative Provisions
nodes.heading: 38.27 Administrative Provisions
nodes.start_phrase: Withholding Taxes : As a result of legal and/or tax obligations the Firm, in its sole discretion, may (i) retain from each distribution the number of shares of Common Stock required to satisfy applicable tax obligations or (ii) implement any other desirable or necessary procedures, so that appropriate withholding and other taxes are paid to the competent authorities with respect to the vested shares and the award.
nodes.summary:
- Sets out the firm’s notice-of-recovery process: good-faith written/electronic notice to the last known address is sufficient; such notice preserves JPMorgan Chase’s right to require repayment, and the firm retains sole discretion over completing its evaluation.
- Clarifies repayment scope on distributed shares, including those withheld for taxes: employees are only required to repay amounts tied to shares they retain post-tax; no repayment is required for irrevocable tax withholdings or tax payments that cannot be recovered; the firm or its nominee determines amounts attributable to such taxes.
- Allows repayment in Common Stock or cash and characterizes any repayment as a lawful recovery, not a penalty.
- States that these terms do not limit obligations under Bonus Recoupment and the EMEA Malus and Clawback Policy – Identified Staff.
- Provides a right to injunctive relief: violations cause irreparable harm and entitle the firm to an injunction in addition to other legal or equitable remedies.
- Administrative provisions:
  - Tax withholding: the firm may retain vested shares, sell shares to cover taxes, withhold from cash compensation if required, or hold shares until taxes are paid to authorities.
  - Right to set-off: subject to applicable law (including Section 409A), the firm may retain funds or stock from vesting to satisfy debts owed to the firm; it will not recover from certain client accounts holding funds or unrestricted securities without consent, except for specific accounts referenced elsewhere.
  - No ownership rights: RSUs confer no ownership or voting rights before vesting; shares are issued only after vest; by accepting the award, the employee authorizes the firm to establish brokerage/book-entry accounts to deliver vested shares; RSUs may be canceled if cancellation provisions apply during any suspension of vesting, with cross-references to Protection-Based Vesting, Bonus Recoupment, EMEA Malus and Clawback, Termination of Employment, Remedies, and Amendment (allowing suspension).
  - Post-vesting restrictions: the firm may, at vesting, impose time-limited restrictions on transfer, sale, pledging, assignment, hedging, or encumbrance of shares without affecting voting or dividend rights; the excerpt ends mid-sentence regarding recovery determinations during such periods.

nodes.title: Withholding Taxes
nodes.heading: 38.27.1 Withholding Taxes
nodes.start_phrase: As a result of legal and/or tax obligations the Firm, in its sole discretion, may (i) retain from each distribution the number of shares of Common Stock required to satisfy applicable tax obligations or (ii) implement any other desirable or necessary procedures, so that appropriate withholding and other taxes are paid to the competent authorities with respect to the vested shares and the award.
nodes.summary:
- Defines notice-of-recovery: deemed provided if the Firm makes a good-faith attempt to deliver written/electronic notice to the employee’s last known address; such notice preserves JPMorgan Chase’s recovery rights, and the Firm has sole discretion whether to complete its evaluation.
- Clarifies repayment scope: “shares distributed” include shares withheld for taxes, but the Firm intends to require repayment only for shares the employee retains after tax determination; no repayment is required for irrevocable tax withholdings or non-recoverable tax payments. The Firm (or its nominee) determines amounts attributable to such withholdings.
- Allows repayment in cash or shares; characterizes any repayment as a lawful recovery, not a penalty; confirms these terms do not limit obligations under Bonus Recoupment or the EMEA Malus and Clawback Policy for Identified Staff.
- Grants the Firm a right to injunctive relief for any violation or attempted violation, in addition to other legal or equitable remedies.
- Administrative provisions:
  - Tax withholding: the Firm may retain vested shares, sell shares to cover taxes, withhold from cash compensation, or hold shares until taxes are paid to authorities.
  - Right of set-off: subject to applicable law (including Section 409A), the Firm may retain funds or shares from vesting to satisfy debts owed by the employee; it will not recover from other funds or unrestricted securities in the employee’s accounts at the Firm without consent, except for certain accounts referenced elsewhere.
  - No ownership rights before vesting: RSUs confer no stock ownership or voting rights until vesting; shares are issued per Firm procedures. The Firm may open a brokerage or book-entry account to deliver vested shares. RSUs may be canceled if cancellation provisions apply during a suspension of vesting. The Firm may impose post-vesting restrictions (e.g., on sale, transfer, pledge, assignment, hedging, encumbrance) without affecting voting or dividend rights.
- The excerpt concludes amid a clause addressing recovery determinations during periods when such share restrictions are in place.

nodes.title: Right to Set Off
nodes.heading: 38.27.2 Right to Set Off
nodes.start_phrase: Although the Firm expects to settle this award in share(s) of Common Stock as of the applicable vesting date, as set forth in your Award Agreement, the Firm may, to the maximum extent permitted by applicable law (including Section 409A of the Code to the extent it is applicable to you), retain for itself funds or the Common Stock resulting from any vesting of this award to satisfy any obligation or debt that you owe to the Firm.
nodes.summary:
- Establishes that a notice-of-recovery is deemed provided if the firm makes a good-faith written (including electronic) attempt to your last known address; such notice preserves JPMorgan Chase’s rights and the firm may complete or not complete its evaluation in its sole discretion.
- Clarifies repayment scope: “shares distributed” include tax-withheld shares, but repayment is intended only for shares you retain after tax; no repayment is required for irrevocable tax withholdings or prior tax payments you cannot recover. The firm or its nominee may determine the amount represented by such taxes and exclude it from repayment.
- Allows repayment in shares of Common Stock or cash and states such recovery is lawful, not a penalty.
- States these provisions do not limit other recoupment policies (Bonus Recoupment; EMEA Malus and Clawback Policy – Identified Staff).
- Grants the firm the right to seek injunctive relief for violations, in addition to other legal or equitable remedies.
- Administrative tax provisions: the firm may satisfy withholding obligations by retaining vested shares, selling shares to cover taxes, withholding from cash compensation where required, or retaining shares until you pay taxes to authorities.
- Right to set-off: to the extent permitted by law (including Section 409A), the firm may retain funds or shares from vesting to satisfy debts you owe; it will not recover from other funds or unrestricted securities in your name at the firm without your consent, except for specified award-related accounts.
- Confirms RSUs confer no ownership or voting rights before vesting; shares are issued only after vesting per firm procedures; you authorize the firm to open a brokerage or book-entry account to deliver vested shares.
- Notes RSUs may be canceled if cancellation provisions apply during any suspension of vesting, with references to protection-based vesting, recoupment, malus/clawback, termination, remedies, and amendment rights.
- Permits the firm to impose time-limited post-vesting restrictions on transfer, sale, pledge, assignment, hedging, or encumbrance of issued shares without affecting voting or dividend rights.
- Excerpt ends as it references determinations about recovery during restricted periods.

nodes.title: No Ownership Rights/Other Limitations
nodes.heading: 38.27.3 No Ownership Rights/Other Limitations
nodes.start_phrase: RSUs do not convey the rights of ownership of Common Stock and do not carry voting rights.
nodes.summary:
- Establishes notice-of-recovery rules: good-faith written notice to last known address suffices; preserves the Firm’s rights; evaluation may be discontinued at the Firm’s discretion.
- Clarifies repayment scope: “shares” include tax-withheld shares; intent to recoup only for shares you retain after taxes; no repayment required for irrevocable tax withholdings/payments; amounts excluded determined at the Firm’s discretion.
- Repayment method: in cash or shares; treated as lawful recovery, not a penalty; obligations under Bonus Recoupment and EMEA Malus and Clawback Policy remain unaffected.
- Injunctive relief: Firm entitled to an injunction for violations, in addition to other legal/equitable remedies.
- Withholding taxes: Firm may withhold shares, sell shares, withhold cash compensation, or retain shares until taxes are paid to satisfy tax obligations.
- Right to set off: Firm may use vested shares/funds from this award to satisfy your debts to the Firm, subject to law (including Section 409A); no recoupment from unrelated accounts without consent, except certain internal accounts noted elsewhere.
- No ownership rights before vesting: RSUs carry no voting rights or ownership; Firm may open accounts and deliver vested shares; vesting can be suspended and RSUs canceled under specified provisions; post-vesting restrictions (e.g., transfer, hedge, pledge) may be imposed without affecting voting/dividend rights; during restriction periods, recovery may require payment up to the vest-date fair market value of gross restricted shares.
- Binding effect: Award Agreement binds JPMorgan Chase successors.
- Employment status: Not an employment contract; employment is at-will; no promise of future awards; award value excluded from severance calculations.
- Section 409A compliance: Award intended to comply; six-month payment delay for specified employees after separation, when applicable; sets payment dates following vesting where no substantial risk of forfeiture remains.
- Corporate changes: Equitable adjustments to shares/RSUs for stock splits, dividends, mergers, spin-offs, or similar events.
- Administration: Committee has sole authority to interpret, determine termination reasons, apply cancellation/recovery, decide claims, and delegate; determinations may be non-uniform and selective.
- Amendment: Committee may amend at any time; no material adverse changes without consent except to comply with law/accounting or adjust vesting/restrictions consistent with Section 409A; amendments must be signed by the Firm’s HR Director.
- Severability: Unenforceable provisions may be reformed (by the Firm, court/arbitrator, or HR Director) to be enforceable under applicable law.

nodes.title: Binding Agreement
nodes.heading: 38.27.4 Binding Agreement
nodes.start_phrase: The Award Agreement will be binding upon any successor in interest to JPMorgan Chase, by merger or otherwise.
nodes.summary:
- Potential recoupment: You may be required to repay up to the fair market value (as of the vesting date) of the gross number of shares if recoupment provisions apply, notwithstanding any set-off limitations (see Bonus Recoupment and Remedies).
- Binding on successors: The Award Agreement binds any successor to JPMorgan Chase.
- No employment contract: Employment remains at-will; the award does not guarantee continued employment, future awards, or count as compensation for severance.
- Section 409A compliance: The award is intended to comply with Section 409A. If you are a specified employee who separates from service and the award is deferred compensation, distributions triggered within six months post-separation are delayed and paid in the first calendar month after six full months. If no substantial risk of forfeiture applies, distributions of vested portions may occur at any payment date during the remainder of the calendar year following each vesting date.
- Share adjustments: In the event of stock splits, dividends (other than regular cash), mergers, spin-offs, recapitalizations, or similar events, equitable substitutions or adjustments will be made to the plan and outstanding RSUs.
- Administration and interpretation: The Committee has sole authority to interpret the plan and agreement, determine termination reasons, apply post-employment obligations and recovery provisions, decide claims, and delegate authority. Determinations need not be uniform; selective, non-uniform decisions are permitted.
- Amendment rights: The Committee may amend the agreement at any time. Material adverse changes require your consent except when needed to comply with law/regulatory/accounting changes, to adjust scheduled vesting dates, or to impose “No Ownership Rights/Other Limitations,” in each case as permitted by Section 409A. Amendments must be in writing signed by JPMorgan Chase’s Director of Human Resources.
- Severability/reformation: If any provision is unenforceable, a court, arbitrator, or the Director of Human Resources may reform it (e.g., duration, geography, scope) to make it enforceable under applicable law.

nodes.title: Not a Contract of Employment
nodes.heading: 38.27.5 Not a Contract of Employment
nodes.start_phrase: Nothing contained in the Award Agreement constitutes a contract of employment or continued employment.
nodes.summary:
- Potential clawback/recoupment: you may have to repay up to the fair market value of restricted shares upon certain triggers, notwithstanding set-off limits, with references to Bonus Recoupment and Remedies.
- Binding on successors: the Award Agreement applies to any successor to JPMorgan Chase.
- No employment contract: employment remains at-will; the award does not guarantee future awards and is not counted for severance.
- Section 409A compliance: distributions intended to comply with tax rules; includes a six-month payment delay for specified employees after separation; defines post-vesting payment timing.
- Corporate actions adjustment: equitable substitutions/adjustments to RSUs and share reserves for stock splits, dividends, mergers, spin-offs, etc.
- Administration and interpretation: the Committee has sole authority to interpret, determine termination reasons, enforce post-employment obligations and recovery, decide claims, and delegate; determinations may be non-uniform/selective.
- Amendment rights: the Committee may amend at any time; no materially adverse changes without consent except to comply with laws/regulations/accounting or to adjust vesting/restrictions as permitted by 409A; amendments must be in writing signed by the HR Director.
- Severability/reformation: unenforceable provisions may be reformed to an enforceable scope (e.g., time, geography, scope) by the Firm, HR Director, or a court/arbitrator.

nodes.title: Section 409A Compliance
nodes.heading: 38.27.6 Section 409A Compliance
nodes.start_phrase: To the extent that Section 409A of the Code is applicable to this award, distributions of shares hereunder are intended to comply with Section 409A of the Code, and the Award Agreement, including these terms and conditions, shall be interpreted in a manner consistent with such intent.
nodes.summary:
- Potential recoupment: You may be required to repay the firm up to the fair market value of restricted shares if certain recoupment or remedies provisions apply, even beyond normal set-off limits (see Bonus Recoupment and Remedies).
- Binding effect: The Award Agreement binds JPMorgan Chase’s successors (e.g., via merger).
- No employment contract: Employment remains at-will; the award does not guarantee continued employment, future awards, or count as compensation for severance purposes.
- Section 409A compliance: The award is intended to comply with IRC Section 409A. For specified employees who separate from service, distributions triggered within six months are delayed until after six full months. For awards not subject to a substantial risk of forfeiture, distributions may occur during the remainder of each calendar year following each vesting date.
- Corporate changes: In the event of stock splits/dividends (other than regular cash), recapitalizations, mergers, spin-offs, and similar events, equitable adjustments may be made to outstanding RSUs and shares reserved under the plan.
- Administration and interpretation: The Committee has sole authority to interpret the plan and agreement, determine termination reasons, apply post-employment and clawback provisions, decide claims, and delegate authority. Its (and designated officials’) decisions are binding and may be non-uniform across participants.
- Amendments: The Committee may amend the agreement at any time. Material adverse changes require your consent unless needed to comply with laws/regulations/accounting, or to adjust vesting dates/impose certain restrictions consistent with Section 409A. Amendments must be in writing and signed by the Director of Human Resources.
- Severability/reformation: If any provision is unenforceable, it may be reformed (by the firm, HR Director, or a court/arbitrator) to the extent necessary to be enforceable under applicable law.

nodes.title: Change in Outstanding Shares
nodes.heading: 38.27.7 Change in Outstanding Shares
nodes.start_phrase: In the event of any change in the outstanding shares of Common Stock by reason of any stock dividend or split, recapitalization, issuance of a new class of common stock, merger, consolidation, spin-off, combination or exchange of shares or other similar corporate change, or any distributions to stockholders of Common Stock other than regular cash dividends, the Committee will make an equitable substitution or proportionate adjustment, in the number or kind of shares of Common Stock or other securities issued or reserved for issuance pursuant to the Plan and to any RSUs outstanding under this award for such corporate events.
nodes.summary:
- Potential clawback/recoupment: you may be required to repay the Firm up to the fair market value (as of the vesting date) of the gross shares subject to restrictions, notwithstanding set‑off limits (see Bonus Recoupment and Remedies).
- Binding effect: the Award Agreement binds JPMorgan Chase’s successors (e.g., by merger).
- No employment contract: employment remains at-will; the award does not guarantee continued employment, future awards, or severance compensation treatment.
- Section 409A compliance: distributions are intended to comply with Section 409A; includes a six‑month payment delay for “specified employees” after separation from service when required; payment timing aligns with 409A rules, including post‑vesting distribution within the remainder of the following calendar year when not subject to substantial risk of forfeiture.
- Corporate changes: equitable adjustments to shares/RSUs for stock splits, dividends, mergers, recapitalizations, spin‑offs, and similar events.
- Administration and interpretation: the Committee has sole authority to interpret the Plan/Award, determine termination reasons, apply post‑employment obligations and recovery provisions, decide claims, and delegate; decisions are binding and need not be uniform across participants.
- Amendment rights: the Committee may amend the Award Agreement at any time; no materially adverse changes without consent except to comply with laws/regulations/accounting or to adjust vesting dates/impose certain restrictions as permitted by Section 409A; amendments must be in writing signed by the Director of Human Resources.
- Severability/reformation: unenforceable provisions may be reformed (e.g., scope, time, geography) by the Firm, a court, or an arbitrator to make them enforceable under applicable law.

nodes.title: Interpretation/Administration
nodes.heading: 38.27.8 Interpretation/Administration
nodes.start_phrase: The Committee has sole and complete authority to interpret and administer this Award Agreement, including, without limitation, the power to (i) interpret the Plan and the terms of this Award Agreement; (ii) determine the reason for termination of employment; (iii) determine application of the post-employment obligations and cancellation and recovery provisions; (iv) decide all claims arising with respect to this award; and (v) delegate such authority as it deems appropriate.
nodes.summary:
- Clawback/recoupment: You may be required to repay the Firm up to the fair market value of the gross number of shares if certain provisions apply, notwithstanding any right of set‑off limits (see Bonus Recoupment and Remedies).
- Binding effect: The Award Agreement binds JPMorgan Chase’s successors (e.g., by merger).
- No employment contract: Employment remains at-will; the award creates no guarantee of continued employment, no entitlement to future awards, and is not counted as compensation for severance.
- Section 409A compliance: The award is intended to comply with Section 409A. For specified employees who separate from service, any deferred compensation shares payable within six months post‑separation are delayed and delivered in the first calendar month after six full months. If not subject to a substantial risk of forfeiture, the remainder of each calendar year following each vesting date is a payment date for distributing vested shares.
- Corporate changes: Equitable adjustments may be made to outstanding RSUs and shares reserved under the plan for stock splits, dividends, recapitalizations, mergers, spin‑offs, exchanges, or other similar events.
- Administration/interpretation: The Committee has sole authority to interpret the Plan and Award Agreement, determine termination reasons, apply post‑employment and recovery provisions, decide claims, and delegate authority. Determinations are binding and may be non‑uniform or selective across participants.
- Amendments: The Committee (or its nominee) may amend the Award Agreement at any time. No material adverse change without your consent, except as advisable to comply with laws/regulations/accounting rules, or to change a vesting date/impose certain restrictions consistent with Section 409A. Amendments must be in writing signed by the JPMorgan Chase Director of Human Resources.
- Severability: If any provision is unenforceable, it may be reformed (by the Firm, a court/arbitrator, or the HR Director) as needed to be enforceable under applicable law.

nodes.title: Amendment
nodes.heading: 38.27.9 Amendment
nodes.start_phrase: The Committee or its nominee reserves the right to amend this Award Agreement in any manner, at any time and for any reason; provided, however, that no such amendment shall materially adversely affect your rights under this Award Agreement without your consent except to the extent that the Committee or its delegate considers advisable to (x) comply with applicable laws or changes in or interpretation of applicable laws, regulatory requirements and accounting rules or standards and/or (y) make a change in a scheduled vesting date or impose the restrictions described above under “No Ownership Rights/Other Limitations”, in either case, to the extent permitted by Section 409A of the Code if it is applicable to you.
nodes.summary:
- Potential recoupment: You may be required to repay the firm up to the fair market value of restricted shares, notwithstanding any prior set-off limits, per Bonus Recoupment and Remedies provisions.
- Binding effect: The Award Agreement binds JPMorgan Chase and any successors (e.g., via merger).
- Employment status: The award is not an employment contract; employment remains at-will; no right to future or similar awards; award value is excluded from severance calculations.
- Section 409A compliance: The award intends to comply with Section 409A. For specified employees who separate from service, any deferred-compensation shares payable within six months will be delayed and delivered after six full months. If no substantial risk of forfeiture exists post-vesting, distributions may occur during the remainder of the calendar year following each vesting date.
- Adjustments for corporate actions: Equitable substitutions/adjustments may be made to shares/RSUs in events like stock splits, dividends, recapitalizations, mergers, spin-offs, or similar changes.
- Administration and interpretation: The Committee has sole authority to interpret the Plan/Award, determine termination reasons, apply post-employment and clawback provisions, decide claims, and delegate authority. Determinations need not be uniform and may be selective.
- Amendments: The Committee (or nominee) may amend the Award Agreement at any time. No material adverse changes without your consent, except to comply with laws/regulations/accounting rules or to adjust vesting/ownership restrictions consistent with Section 409A. Amendments must be in writing signed by the Director of Human Resources.
- Severability: Unenforceable provisions may be reformed (e.g., duration, geography, scope) by the Firm, a court/arbitrator, or HR to make them enforceable under applicable law.

nodes.title: Severability
nodes.heading: 38.27.10 Severability
nodes.start_phrase: If any portion of the Award Agreement is determined by the Firm to be unenforceable in any jurisdiction, any court or arbitrator of competent jurisdiction or the Director of Human Resources may reform the relevant provisions (e.g., as to length of service, time, geographical area or scope) to the extent the Firm (or court/arbitrator) considers necessary to make the provision enforceable under applicable law.
nodes.summary:
- Potential clawback/recoupment: If certain provisions apply, you may have to repay the Firm up to the fair market value (as of the vesting date) of the gross number of shares, notwithstanding any “Right to Set Off” limits; references Bonus Recoupment and Remedies sections.
- Binding on successors: The Award Agreement binds any successor to JPMorgan Chase (e.g., by merger).
- No employment contract: Employment remains at-will; the award does not guarantee continued employment, future awards, or severance compensation treatment.
- Section 409A compliance: Distributions are intended to comply with Section 409A. For specified employees who separate from service, any deferred compensation shares payable within six months will be delayed to the first month after six full months post-separation. If no substantial risk of forfeiture remains, the remainder of each calendar year after each vesting date is a payment date for the vested portion.
- Adjustments for corporate actions: In the event of stock splits/dividends, recapitalizations, mergers, spin-offs, or similar changes, equitable substitutions or proportional adjustments will be made to plan share reserves and outstanding RSUs.
- Interpretation and administration: The Committee has sole authority to interpret the Plan/Award, determine termination reasons, apply post-employment and recovery provisions, decide claims, and delegate. Determinations and modifications may be non-uniform and selective.
- Amendment rights: The Committee may amend the Award Agreement at any time for any reason; it will not materially adversely affect your rights without consent except as advisable to comply with laws/regulations/accounting standards or to change vesting dates/impose certain restrictions, consistent with Section 409A. Amendments must be in writing signed by JPMorgan Chase’s Director of HR.
- Severability/reformation: If any provision is unenforceable, the Firm, Director of HR, or a court/arbitrator may reform it (e.g., duration, geography, scope) to make it enforceable under applicable law.

nodes.title: Accelerated Distribution for Ethics or Conflict Reasons Resulting From Employment by a Government Entity
nodes.heading: 38.27.11 Accelerated Distribution for Ethics or Conflict Reasons Resulting From Employment by a Government Entity
nodes.start_phrase: Upon receipt of satisfactory evidence that applicable United States federal, state, local, foreign or supranational ethics or conflict of interest laws or regulations require you to divest your interest in JPMorgan Chase RSUs, the Firm may accelerate the distribution of all or part of your outstanding award effective on or before the required divestiture date; provided that no accelerated distribution shall occur if the Firm determines that such acceleration will violate Section 409A of the Code.
nodes.summary:
- Accelerated distribution of RSUs may occur if required by ethics or conflict-of-interest rules tied to government employment, subject to Section 409A compliance. Acceleration does not change “Remedies” timing; recovery is based on original vesting schedules. Applies to portions continuing to vest under “Government Office Requirements,” and to full awards outstanding due to “Job Elimination” or “Full Career Eligibility.” All original Award Agreement obligations (clawbacks, Protection-Based Vesting, Government Office Requirements) continue as if unaccelerated.
- Use of Personal Data: Acceptance authorizes the Firm to process and disclose personal data for award administration (including share registration and brokerage accounts) and to transfer data internationally, even to jurisdictions with lower protections. Authorization may be terminated where permitted by law (excluding tax/regulatory obligations); termination cancels the award.
- Governing Law: New York law.
- Choice of Forum: Disputes may be compelled to AAA arbitration at the Firm’s election; otherwise, exclusive jurisdiction and venue in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York. Waiver of objections to personal jurisdiction and venue; agreement not to file elsewhere.
- Waiver of Jury Trial/Class Claims: All employment-related claims must be brought individually; jury trial and class/collective/representative actions are waived.
- Litigation: If the Firm prevails in enforcing the Award Agreement, it may recover reasonable attorneys’ fees and expenses; no advancement or indemnification under Firm By-Laws in such suits.
- Non-transferability: RSUs/awards and related rights may not be assigned, pledged, transferred, hedged, or encumbered; transfer permitted only upon death by will, descent, or designated beneficiary.
- Outstanding Awards: Administrative provisions apply to and amend any RSU awards already outstanding.
- Definitions: Begins defining “Cause,” including violations of laws/regulations, felony indictment/conviction, fraud, and breaches of the Code of Conduct or policies (text truncated).

nodes.title: Use of Personal Data
nodes.heading: 38.27.12 Use of Personal Data
nodes.start_phrase: By accepting this award, you acknowledge that the Firm may process your personal data for the purposes of providing you this award (to include registration of shares and units or establishing a brokerage account on your behalf) and disclosing to third parties, such as service providers or tax and regulatory authorities (e.g., for compensation reporting and payroll tax withholding purposes).
nodes.summary:
- Accelerated distribution for ethics/conflict reasons tied to government employment: RSUs may be distributed early to meet mandatory divestiture laws, provided doing so does not violate Section 409A. Acceleration does not change the timing for remedies/recovery, which remain tied to original vesting/distribution dates. If you voluntarily leave and meet “Government Office Requirements,” acceleration applies to the portion that would continue to vest; for “Job Elimination” or “Full Career Eligibility,” it applies to the full outstanding award. Despite acceleration, all original award terms and restrictions (including Remedies, Protection-Based Vesting, Government Office Requirements, and Full Career Eligibility) continue as if vesting occurred on the original schedule.
- Use of personal data: Acceptance authorizes the Firm to process and disclose personal data for award administration and regulatory/tax purposes, including cross-border transfers to jurisdictions with lesser protections. Where allowed, you may revoke authorization (except for tax/regulatory obligations), but doing so cancels the award.
- Governing law: New York law governs, without regard to conflicts of law principles.
- Choice of forum: The Firm may elect AAA arbitration for disputes; if not arbitrable, exclusive jurisdiction and venue lie in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York. You waive objections to personal jurisdiction/venue and agree not to sue elsewhere.
- Waiver of jury trial/class claims: You waive the right to a jury trial and agree all claims will be brought on an individual basis only; no class, collective, representative, or joint actions.
- Litigation: In Firm-initiated enforcement actions where the Firm prevails (excluding derivative suits), the Firm may recover reasonable attorneys’ fees and expenses. You are not entitled to advancement of fees or indemnification under the Firm’s By-Laws in such suits.
- Non-transferability: RSU awards and related rights may not be assigned, pledged, transferred, hedged, hypothecated, or subjected to liens; transfer is permitted only upon death via will, descent, or beneficiary designation.
- Outstanding awards: The stated administrative provisions apply to and amend any RSU awards already outstanding.
- Definitions: Begins defining “Cause,” including termination for legal/regulatory violations, felony indictment/conviction, fraud, or violations of the Code of Conduct or Firm policies (definition continues).

nodes.title: Governing Law
nodes.heading: 38.27.13 Governing Law
nodes.start_phrase: This award shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of New York, without regard to conflicts of law principles.
nodes.summary:
- Allows accelerated distribution of JPMorgan Chase RSUs when required by ethics or conflict-of-interest laws tied to government employment, provided it doesn’t violate Section 409A; acceleration does not change recovery timelines tied to original vesting/distribution dates.
- Specifies when acceleration applies after employment ends: proportionally if voluntarily leaving and meeting Government Office Requirements; fully if award remains outstanding due to Job Elimination or Full Career Eligibility.
- Clarifies that, despite acceleration, all original award terms continue to apply as if vesting occurred on schedule, including repayment (Remedies) and employment restrictions (Protection-Based Vesting, Government Office Requirements, Full Career Eligibility).
- Authorizes Firm’s processing, disclosure, and cross-border transfer of personal data for award administration and compliance; permits revocation where allowed by law (excluding tax/regulatory obligations), with revocation resulting in award cancellation.
- Establishes New York law as governing law.
- Sets dispute resolution: Firm may elect AAA arbitration; otherwise, exclusive jurisdiction and venue in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York; waives objections to jurisdiction/venue and filing elsewhere.
- Waives jury trial and class/collective/representative actions; claims must be brought individually.
- Provides that if the Firm prevails in enforcing award terms, it may recover reasonable attorney fees and expenses; employee waives rights to fee advancement and indemnification under Firm By-Laws in such suits.
- States awards and rights are non-transferable (no assignment, pledge, hedge, lien), except upon death by will, descent laws, or designated beneficiary.
- Applies administrative provisions to all outstanding RSU awards as of the document date, amending them accordingly.
- Begins defining “Cause” to include termination for legal/regulatory violations related to Firm business, felony indictment/conviction, fraud, and violations of the Code of Conduct or other Firm policies (definition excerpted).

nodes.title: Choice of Forum
nodes.heading: 38.27.14 Choice of Forum
nodes.start_phrase: By accepting this award under the Plan, you agree (and have agreed) that to the extent not otherwise subject to arbitration under an arbitration agreement between you and the Firm, any dispute arising directly or indirectly in connection with this award or the Plan shall be submitted to arbitration in accordance with the rules of the American Arbitration Association if so elected by the Firm in its sole discretion.
nodes.summary:
- Accelerated distribution for ethics or conflict-of-interest reasons tied to government employment: RSUs may be distributed early if required by applicable laws, subject to Section 409A; original recovery timelines remain; applies proportionally after voluntary termination meeting Government Office Requirements and fully after job elimination or Full Career Eligibility; all original award obligations (Remedies, Protection-Based Vesting, Government Office Requirements, Full Career Eligibility) continue despite acceleration.
- Use of personal data: consent to processing and disclosure to service providers and tax/regulatory authorities, including cross-border transfers to jurisdictions with potentially lower protections; authorization may be terminated where allowed (excluding tax/regulatory needs), but doing so cancels the award.
- Governing law: New York law governs.
- Choice of forum: Firm may elect AAA arbitration; otherwise, exclusive jurisdiction and venue in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York; waiver of objections to personal jurisdiction and venue; no filing in other forums.
