You may terminate this authorization where permitted by law (excluding required legal/regulatory reporting), but doing so will cancel the award.

nodes.title: Non-transferability
nodes.heading: 38.27.17 Non-transferability
nodes.start_phrase: Neither this award or any other outstanding awards of RSUs, nor your interests or rights in any such awards, shall be assigned, pledged, transferred, hedged, hypothecated or subject to any lien.

- Use of personal data: consent to process and share data for award administration (including brokerage setup) and for tax/regulatory reporting; permission for cross-border transfers to jurisdictions without equivalent protections; right to terminate authorization where allowed by law (except for tax/regulatory obligations), with termination resulting in award cancellation.

- Definitions: begins defining “Cause,” including violations of laws/regulations, felony indictment/conviction, fraudulent acts, and violations of the Code of Conduct or Firm policies (excerpt incomplete).

nodes.title: Definitions
nodes.heading: 38.28 Definitions
nodes.start_phrase: “Cause ” means a determination by the Firm that your employment terminated as a result of your (i) violation of any law, rule or regulation (including rules of self-regulatory bodies) related to the Firm’s business, (ii) indictment or conviction of a felony, (iii) commission of a fraudulent act, (iv) violation of the JPMorgan Chase Code of Conduct or other Firm policies or misconduct related to your duties to the Firm (other than immaterial and inadvertent violations or misconduct), (v) grossly inadequate performance of the duties associated with your position or job function or failure to follow reasonable directives of your manager, or (vi) any act or failure to act that is injurious to the interests of the Firm or its relationship with a customer, client or an employee.
nodes.summary:
- Accelerated distribution for ethics/conflict reasons tied to government employment: the Firm may accelerate RSU distributions if required by applicable ethics or conflict-of-interest laws, provided no violation of Section 409A occurs. Acceleration does not change recovery timelines in Remedies, and you remain bound by Award Agreement terms as if vesting had continued normally. Applies to eligible terminations (e.g., Government Office Requirements, Job Elimination, Full Career Eligibility) as specified.
- Use of personal data: acceptance authorizes the Firm to process and share personal data with service providers and tax/regulatory authorities, including cross-border transfers to jurisdictions with lesser protections. You may revoke authorization where allowed by law (not for tax/regulatory obligations); revocation cancels the award.
- Governing law: New York law applies.
- Choice of forum: disputes may be compelled to AAA arbitration at the Firm’s discretion; otherwise, exclusive jurisdiction/venue in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York; waiver of objections to jurisdiction/venue and commitment not to sue elsewhere.
- Waiver of jury trial/class claims: all claims must proceed on an individual basis; jury trial and class/collective/representative actions are waived.
- Litigation costs: in Firm-initiated actions to enforce award terms where the Firm prevails, it may recover reasonable attorneys’ fees and expenses; no advancement or indemnification under Firm By-Laws for such Firm-initiated suits.
- Non-transferability: RSUs and related rights cannot be assigned, pledged, transferred, hedged, or encumbered; transfer permitted at death via will, descent, or beneficiary designation.
- Outstanding awards: administrative provisions apply to and amend any RSU awards outstanding as of the document date.
- Key definitions provided, including:
  - Cause (enumerated misconduct, legal violations, poor performance, etc.).
  - Financial Services Company (broad list including banking, insurance, investment services, fintech, private equity/real estate, and similar activities).
  - Firmwide Financial Threshold: cumulative ROTCE ≥ 15% for 2023–2025.
  - Government Office: specified full-time elected/appointed roles or bona fide full-time campaign.
  - Line of Business and Line of Business Financial Thresholds: negative income/revenue criteria by LOB (e.g., AWM, Card and Auto, CIB product lines, Corporate Functions, etc.).
  - Not-for-Profit Organization and Recognized Service.
- Government Office Requirements (continued vesting on resignation to accept or campaign for a Government Office):
  - Not applicable if Full Career Eligibility is satisfied at termination.
  - Eligibility conditions: at least 60 days’ advance written notice and cooperation; confirmations that continued vesting is lawful; documentation of government role/candidacy.
  - Portion eligible for continued vesting (CV Award) based on continuous service: 50% (≥3<4 years), 75% (≥4<5 years), 100% (≥5 years); remainder is canceled at termination.
  - Conditions: remain in a non-elective Government Office for ≥2 years (or retain vesting scheduled during a shorter service period); for elective roles, name must appear on the primary or final ballot.
  - If conditions are satisfied: remaining awards (including those previously accelerated for ethics reasons) continue under original terms and employment restrictions as if Full Career Eligibility applied.
  - Failure to satisfy: cancellation of outstanding RSUs under the CV Award and repayment of the fair market value of shares previously distributed that would otherwise still be outstanding as RSUs but for acceleration.

nodes.title: Government Office Requirements
nodes.heading: 38.29 Government Office Requirements
nodes.start_phrase: You may be eligible to continue vesting in all or part of your award if you voluntarily resign to accept a Government Office (as defined above) or to become a candidate for an elective Government Office.
nodes.summary:
- Defines “Recognized Service” per the firm’s service-related policies.
- Outlines “Government Office Requirements,” allowing continued vesting of awards if an employee voluntarily resigns to accept a Government Office or to run for elective office; does not apply if the employee qualifies for Full Career Eligibility at termination.
- Sets eligibility conditions for continued vesting: at least 60 days’ advance written notice and cooperative service during notice; firm may shorten the period; proof that continued vesting is legally compliant; documentation confirming resignation is to accept or pursue a Government Office.
- Specifies the portion of awards that continue to vest (the “CV Award”) based on continuous service: 50% (3–<4 years), 75% (4–<5 years), 100% (≥5 years); the remainder is cancelled at termination.
- Details conditions for continued vesting: remain in a non-elective Government Office for two or more years (or retain only tranches vesting during a shorter government service); for elective office, the employee’s name must appear on the primary or final ballot.
- Describes satisfaction of conditions: if met (including candidacy where not elected), any outstanding or would-be outstanding awards (notwithstanding any prior accelerated distribution for ethics/conflict reasons) continue under the original award terms and employment restrictions as if separated with Full Career Eligibility.
- Explains failure to satisfy conditions: cancellation of outstanding RSUs under the CV Award and repayment of the fair market value of shares previously distributed that would have remained unvested but for an accelerated distribution tied to ethics/conflict considerations.
- References an “Accelerated Distribution for Ethics or Conflict Reasons Resulting From Employment by a Government Entity.”
- Includes a general reference to organizations recognized under law for charitable, religious, scientific, public safety testing, literary, educational, amateur sports, or prevention of cruelty purposes.

nodes.title: Full Career Eligibility
nodes.heading: 38.29.1 Full Career Eligibility
nodes.start_phrase: “Government Office Requirements ” does not apply to you if you satisfy the subsection captioned “--Full Career Eligibility” as of the date that you voluntarily terminate your employment with the Firm.
nodes.summary:
- Defines “Recognized Service” as service credited under the firm’s service-related policies, and references definitions that include certain tax‑exempt (501(c)(3)-type) organizations.
- Establishes “Government Office Requirements,” allowing employees who voluntarily resign to accept or run for a Government Office to continue vesting in part or all of their equity awards.
- Clarifies that these Government Office provisions do not apply if the employee meets “Full Career Eligibility” at termination.
- Sets eligibility conditions for continued vesting: at least 60 days’ advance written notice (firm may shorten), continued professional cooperation and no outside employment during notice, confirmation that continued vesting is legally compliant, and documentation proving the resignation is to accept or pursue a Government Office.
- Specifies the portion of outstanding awards that continue to vest (the “CV Award”) based on continuous service at termination:
  - 50% with 3 to <4 years
  - 75% with 4 to <5 years
  - 100% with 5+ years
  The non-CV portion is canceled at termination.
- States conditions to retain the CV Award:
  - Serve in a non-elective Government Office for at least two years post-termination (or retain only tranches vesting during a shorter non-elective term), or
  - If resigning to campaign for an elective office, the employee’s name must appear on the primary or final ballot.
- Describes satisfaction of conditions: if met (including if not elected), remaining CV Awards continue under the original schedule and are subject to the Award Agreement’s terms and employment restrictions, similar to meeting Full Career Eligibility; references possible accelerated distributions required for ethics/conflict compliance when employed by a government entity.
- Outlines failure consequences: cancellation of outstanding RSUs under the CV Award and repayment of the fair market value of shares previously accelerated that would otherwise have remained unvested at the time of failure.

nodes.title: Eligibility
nodes.heading: 38.29.2 Eligibility
nodes.start_phrase: Eligibility for continued vesting is conditioned on your providing the Firm:
nodes.summary:
- Defines categories of tax‑exempt organizations (religious, charitable, scientific, public safety testing, literary, educational, amateur sports, prevention of cruelty to children or animals).

- Outlines “Government Office Requirements,” allowing continued vesting of awards if an employee resigns to accept or run for a Government Office.
- States that these Government Office provisions do not apply if the employee qualifies for Full Career Eligibility at termination.
- Sets eligibility conditions for continued vesting: at least 60 days’ advance written notice and cooperation/non-service for other employers during notice; confirmation that continued vesting is legally compliant; documentation proving the resignation is to accept or pursue a Government Office.
- Specifies the portion of awards eligible for continued vesting (the “CV Award”) based on continuous service: 50% (3–<4 years), 75% (4–<5 years), 100% (≥5 years); the remainder is cancelled at termination.
- Details conditions to keep CV Awards: serving in a non‑elective Government Office for at least two years (or retaining only installments vesting during a shorter office term), or, for elective office, having the candidate’s name on the primary or final ballot.
- Provides that, upon satisfying conditions (including if not elected), remaining CV Awards are subject to the same terms as if the employee had resigned with Full Career Eligibility, including ongoing employment restrictions during vesting; references possible accelerated distributions for ethics/conflict reasons related to government employment.
- States consequences for failure to meet conditions: cancellation of outstanding RSUs under CV Awards and repayment of the fair market value of shares previously distributed via accelerated vesting that would otherwise still be unvested.

nodes.title: Portion of Your Awards Subject to Continued Vesting
nodes.heading: 38.29.3 Portion of Your Awards Subject to Continued Vesting
nodes.start_phrase: Subject to the conditions below, the percentage of your outstanding awards that will continue to vest in accordance with this award’s original schedule will be based on your years of continuous service completed with the Firm immediately preceding your termination date, as follows:
nodes.summary:
- Defines “Recognized Service” per the firm’s service-related policies.
- Outlines “Government Office Requirements” for employees who voluntarily resign to accept or run for a Government Office, including that these provisions don’t apply if the employee meets Full Career Eligibility at termination.
- Sets eligibility conditions for continued vesting: at least 60 days’ advance written notice while remaining cooperative and not working elsewhere; firm’s right to shorten notice; required confirmations that continued vesting is legally compliant; and documentation proving acceptance of or candidacy for a Government Office.
- Specifies the portion of outstanding awards that continue to vest based on years of continuous service immediately before termination: 50% (3–<4 years), 75% (4–<5 years), 100% (≥5 years). The non-eligible portion is canceled at termination. The eligible portion is the “CV Award.”
- Establishes conditions to keep vesting: serve in a non-elective Government Office for at least two years (or retain only those tranches vesting during a shorter service period); or, for elective roles, have your name on the primary or final ballot.
- Details what happens upon satisfying conditions: remaining CV Awards continue under the award’s original terms as if the employee resigned with Full Career Eligibility, including ongoing employment restrictions during vesting; addresses cases where shares were accelerated for ethics/conflict reasons tied to government employment.
- Explains consequences of failing conditions: cancellation of outstanding CV RSUs and repayment of the fair market value of any shares previously accelerated that would otherwise still be unvested.
- The excerpt also references qualifying charitable/educational organizations (indicative of a broader definitions section) but primarily focuses on continued vesting rules tied to Government Office transitions.

nodes.title: Conditions for Continued Vesting of Awards
nodes.heading: 38.29.4 Conditions for Continued Vesting of Awards
nodes.start_phrase: You must remain in a non-elective Government Office for two or more years after your employment with the Firm terminates to receive in full your CV Award; provided that if your non-elective Government Office is for a period less than two years, you will be entitled to retain any portion of the CV Award with a vesting date during your period of Government Service; or
nodes.summary:
- Defines “Recognized Service” per the firm’s service-related policies.
- Lays out “Government Office Requirements” allowing continued vesting of equity awards if an employee resigns to accept or run for a Government Office, except when the employee already meets Full Career Eligibility.
- Eligibility conditions for continued vesting: at least 60 days’ advance written notice and cooperation/no outside work during notice; confirmation that continued vesting is legally permissible; documentation proving acceptance of or candidacy for a Government Office.
- Specifies the portion of awards that continue to vest based on continuous service with the firm: 50% (3–<4 years), 75% (4–<5 years), 100% (≥5 years). The eligible portion is the “CV Award”; the remainder is cancelled at termination.
- Conditions to retain CV Awards: remain in a non-elective Government Office for at least two years (or retain only tranches vesting during a shorter term), or, for elective office, have the employee’s name on the primary or final ballot.
- If conditions are satisfied (2+ years of non-elective service, or candidacy with name on ballot but not elected), remaining CV Awards continue under the award’s original terms as if the employee had Full Career Eligibility, including ongoing employment restrictions; addresses handling of any accelerated distributions for ethics/conflict reasons tied to government employment.
- If conditions are not met: cancel outstanding RSUs under the CV Award and require repayment of the fair market value of any shares previously distributed early that would otherwise have remained unvested.
- Includes a fragment referencing entities organized exclusively for religious, charitable, scientific, public safety testing, literary, educational, amateur sports, or prevention of cruelty purposes, indicating a definition of qualifying nonprofit/charitable organizations under applicable laws.

nodes.title: Satisfaction of Conditions
nodes.heading: 38.29.5 Satisfaction of Conditions
nodes.start_phrase: If your service in a Government Office ends two years or more after your employment with the Firm terminates, or in the case of resignation from the Firm to campaign for a Government Office, your name is on the primary or final public ballot for the election and you are not elected, any CV Awards then outstanding and any such awards that would have then been outstanding but for an accelerated distribution of shares (as described in the subsection captioned “Accelerated Distribution for Ethics or Conflict Reasons Resulting From Employment by a Government Entity”) will be subject for the remainder of the applicable vesting period to the same terms and conditions of this Award Agreement, including employment restrictions during the vesting period, as if you had resigned from the Firm having met the requirements for Full Career Eligibility.
nodes.summary:
- Focus: Rules for continued vesting of equity awards when an employee voluntarily resigns to accept or run for a Government Office, plus related definitions, eligibility, conditions, and consequences.
- Definitions:
  - Recognized Service: Period of employment per the Firm’s service policies.
  - CV Award: The portion of outstanding awards that continue to vest after termination under this provision.
  - Government Office: Referenced as defined elsewhere.
- Full Career Eligibility: If met at termination, the Government Office requirements do not apply.
- Eligibility requirements for continued vesting:
  - At least 60 days’ advance written notice; cooperate professionally and do not work for another employer during notice (Firm may shorten the notice period).
  - Provide confirmation that continued vesting would not violate any law/regulation/rule.
  - Provide documentation that resignation is to accept or campaign for a Government Office.
- Portion of awards eligible for continued vesting (CV Award) based on continuous service:
  - 50% for 3 to <4 years,
  - 75% for 4 to <5 years,
  - 100% for 5+ years.
  - Non-CV portion is canceled at termination.
- Conditions to keep vesting:
  - Non-elective Government Office: Must remain in office for 2+ years to receive full CV Award; if service is <2 years, only keep vesting scheduled during the period of service.
  - Elective office: Your name must appear on the primary or final public ballot; if not elected, employment restrictions may apply thereafter.
- If conditions are satisfied:
  - Any outstanding CV Awards (and those that would have been outstanding but for an accelerated distribution due to ethics/conflict reasons tied to government employment) continue under the same terms as if the employee resigned with Full Career Eligibility, including employment restrictions during the remaining vesting period.
- If conditions are not satisfied:
  - Outstanding RSUs in the CV Award are canceled.
  - Repayment required of the Fair Market Value (pre-withholding) of shares previously distributed that would otherwise have remained outstanding as RSUs but for accelerated distribution.
- Reference to an “Accelerated Distribution for Ethics or Conflict Reasons Resulting From Employment by a Government Entity” provision affecting timing/distribution.
- The text also includes a fragment referencing organizations operated exclusively for charitable, scientific, educational, amateur sports, or cruelty-prevention purposes (a 501(c)(3)-type description).

nodes.title: Failure to Satisfy Conditions
nodes.heading: 38.29.6 Failure to Satisfy Conditions
nodes.start_phrase: If you do not satisfy the above “Conditions for Continued Vesting of Awards”, any outstanding RSUs under each CV Award will be cancelled.
nodes.summary:
- Defines “Recognized Service” per the firm’s service-related policies and references entities organized exclusively for charitable/religious/scientific/educational, etc., purposes (indicative of tax-exempt definitions).
- Outlines “Government Office Requirements,” allowing continued vesting if an employee resigns to accept or campaign for a Government Office.
- States exception: these requirements don’t apply if the employee meets “Full Career Eligibility” at termination.
- Sets eligibility conditions for continued vesting: at least 60 days’ advance written notice; professional cooperation and no outside employment during notice; firm’s right to shorten notice; confirmation of legal compliance; documentation proving resignation is for Government Office or candidacy.
- Specifies the portion of awards eligible for continued vesting (“CV Award”) based on continuous service: 50% (3–<4 years), 75% (4–<5), 100% (≥5); the remainder is canceled at termination.
- Conditions for continued vesting: remain in a non-elective Government Office for ≥2 years (or retain only tranches vesting during a shorter service period); for elective office, the individual’s name must appear on the primary or final ballot.
- Satisfaction of conditions: if service in Government Office lasts ≥2 years, or candidacy results in appearing on the ballot but not being elected, remaining CV Awards continue under original terms (including employment restrictions) as if the employee qualified for Full Career Eligibility; addresses treatment of any accelerated distributions for ethics/conflict reasons related to government employment.
- Failure to satisfy conditions: cancellation of outstanding RSUs under the CV Award and repayment of the Fair Market Value of any shares previously distributed that would otherwise have remained as RSUs absent accelerated distribution, valued as of distribution date.

nodes.title: JPMORGAN CHASE & CO. LONG-TERM INCENTIVE PLAN TERMS AND CONDITIONS OF ______________, 20____ PERFORMANCE SHARE UNIT AWARD OPERATING COMMITTEE (Protection-Based Vesting Provisions) Award Agreement
nodes.heading: 39 JPMORGAN CHASE & CO. LONG-TERM INCENTIVE PLAN TERMS AND CONDITIONS OF ______________, 20____ PERFORMANCE SHARE UNIT AWARD OPERATING COMMITTEE (Protection-Based Vesting Provisions) Award Agreement
nodes.start_phrase: These terms and conditions are made part of the Award Agreement dated as of ________________, 20____ (“Grant Date”) awarding performance share units (“PSUs”) pursuant to the terms of the JPMorgan Chase & Co. Long-Term Incentive Plan (“Plan”).
nodes.summary:
- Document sets terms for a Performance Share Unit (PSU) award under the JPMorgan Chase & Co. Long-Term Incentive Plan for Operating Committee members, with protection-based vesting provisions.
- Plan governs over any conflicting award terms; the Award Agreement, Plan, and Prospectus supersede prior related agreements.
- Grant requires passive acceptance by a deadline; if declined by the specified deadline/method, the award is canceled as of the Grant Date.
- PSUs are non-transferable rights to receive JPMorgan Chase common stock at vesting; purpose is to emphasize sustained long-term performance and align interests with shareholders.
- Vesting quantity: Target Award Number multiplied by an Award Payout Percentage determined via a Performance Table, based on a Performance Ranking calculated for the Performance Period.
- Performance Ranking is determined by a Calculation Agent using defined metrics, including Average Tangible Common Equity (if applicable), Calculated PSUs, Firm Reported ROTCE, Performance Table (and footnote), and ROTCE.
- Dividend equivalents: dividends declared during the vesting period are treated as reinvested at fair market value on each dividend date, creating additional “Reinvested Dividend Equivalent Share Units” delivered at vesting with the PSUs.
- Delivery/timing of vested shares is subject to Section 409A compliance; shares will be delivered no later than the timing specified under that subsection.
- On vesting, shares equal to vested PSUs plus dividend equivalent units (net of tax withholding) are issued and placed in a restricted account.
- Two-year post-vesting holding requirement prohibits transfer, assignment, hedging, sale, pledge, or encumbrance; restrictions may lapse earlier only upon death or for an accelerated distribution due to ethics/conflict reasons from government employment.
- Vesting and payout remain subject to cancellation in whole or part under the terms and conditions of the Award Agreement.

nodes.title: Form and Purpose of Award
nodes.heading: 39.1 Form and Purpose of Award
nodes.start_phrase: Each PSU represents a non-transferable right to receive one share of Common Stock as of the vesting date as set forth in your Award Agreement.
nodes.summary:
- Terms and conditions for a JPMorgan Chase & Co. Long-Term Incentive Plan Performance Share Unit (PSU) Award for Operating Committee members, with protection-based vesting provisions.
- The Award Agreement is governed by the Plan (Plan controls in case of conflict) and, along with the Prospectus, supersedes other related agreements. Acceptance is by not declining by the stated deadline; declining cancels the award as of the Grant Date.
- Capitalized terms follow the Plan; “JPMorgan Chase” and the “Firm” are defined.
- Form and purpose: each non-transferable PSU entitles the holder to one share of Common Stock upon vesting, intended to promote sustained long-term performance and align interests with shareholders.
- Vesting amount: on the vesting date, PSUs vest based on Target Award Number multiplied by the Award Payout Percentage determined by the Performance Table; additional shares may vest from Reinvested Dividend Equivalent Share Units; delivery timing is subject to Section 409A compliance.
- Reinvested Dividend Equivalent Share Units: if dividends are paid during the vesting period, additional units are credited at vesting by hypothetically reinvesting dividends on the actual distributable shares at the Fair Market Value on each dividend payment date.
- Holding requirement: net shares (after tax withholding) are held in an account with a two-year prohibition on transfer, assignment, hedging, sale, pledge, or encumbrance; early lapse of restrictions only upon death or accelerated distribution for ethics/conflict reasons related to government employment.
- Performance ranking: determined by a Calculation Agent for the Performance Period using defined measures, including Average Tangible Common Equity (if applicable), Calculated PSUs, Firm Reported ROTCE, the Performance Table (and its footnote), and ROTCE.

nodes.title: Number to Vest on the Vesting Date
nodes.heading: 39.2 Number to Vest on the Vesting Date
nodes.start_phrase: On the vesting date, you will vest in a number of PSUs derived by multiplying the Target Award Number by the Award Payout Percentage determined using the Performance Table.
nodes.summary:
- Terms and conditions for a JPMorgan Chase & Co. Long-Term Incentive Plan Performance Share Unit (PSU) Award for Operating Committee members, with protection-based vesting provisions.
- The Plan governs in case of conflict; the Award Agreement, Plan, and Prospectus supersede prior related agreements.
- Acceptance occurs unless the award is declined by the specified deadline; declining cancels the award as of the Grant Date.
- Each PSU is a non-transferable right to one share of JPMorgan Chase common stock upon vesting; the award’s purpose is to promote sustained long-term performance and align interests with shareholders.
- Vesting amount on the vesting date equals the Target Award Number multiplied by the Award Payout Percentage determined from a Performance Table; additional shares may be earned from Reinvested Dividend Equivalent Share Units.
- Dividend equivalents: dividends paid during the vesting period are treated as reinvested into additional units based on fair market value on each dividend date, calculated on the actual number of shares distributable at vesting.
- Holding requirement: net vested shares (after tax withholding) are issued but subject to a two-year restriction on transfer, assignment, hedging, sale, pledge, or encumbrance; restrictions may lapse early upon death or for accelerated distribution due to ethics or conflict reasons tied to government employment.
- Performance ranking calculation: the Calculation Agent determines rankings for the Firm and peer companies over the performance period using defined metrics, including ROTCE, Firm Reported ROTCE, Average Tangible Common Equity, Calculated PSUs, and the Performance Table.
- Administrative notes: references to capitalized terms default to Plan definitions; “JPMorgan Chase” refers to the company and its subsidiaries; delivery timing is subject to Section 409A compliance.

nodes.title: Reinvested Dividend Equivalent Share Units
nodes.heading: 39.3 Reinvested Dividend Equivalent Share Units
nodes.start_phrase: If dividends are paid on Common Stock during the Vesting Period while the award is outstanding, you will receive on the vesting date additional units representing shares of Common Stock as calculated in this section.
nodes.summary:
- Document type and scope: Terms and conditions for JPMorgan Chase & Co. Long-Term Incentive Plan Performance Share Unit (PSU) Award for Operating Committee participants, with protection-based vesting provisions; forms part of the Award Agreement and is governed by the Plan in case of conflict.
- Acceptance and governance: Award becomes binding unless declined by the specified deadline; if declined, it is canceled as of the Grant Date. The Award Agreement, Plan, and Prospectus supersede other related agreements. Capitalized terms follow the Plan/Definitions.
- Nature and purpose of PSUs: Each PSU is a non-transferable right to receive one share of JPMorgan Chase common stock at vesting; the award is intended to promote sustained long-term performance and alignment with shareholders.
- Vesting mechanics: On the vesting date, vested PSUs equal the Target Award Number multiplied by the Award Payout Percentage determined by a Performance Table. Additional shares may vest via Reinvested Dividend Equivalent Share Units. Delivery timing observes Section 409A compliance.
- Dividend equivalents: During the vesting period, cash dividends (if any) are notionally reinvested to create additional share units, calculated based on dividends that would have been paid on the actual vested shares and the fair market value on each dividend date.
- Holding requirement: Net shares delivered at vesting (after tax withholding) are subject to a two-year transfer/hedging/pledging restriction. Early lapse of restrictions only upon death or for ethics/conflict reasons tied to government employment.
- Performance ranking and metrics: A Calculation Agent determines the Firm’s and peer companies’ rankings for the performance period using defined measures (e.g., ROTCE, Firm Reported ROTCE, Average Tangible Common Equity) and the Performance Table (including its footnote), which drives the Award Payout Percentage.

nodes.title: Holding Requirement
nodes.heading: 39.4 Holding Requirement
nodes.start_phrase: As of the vesting date set forth in your Award Agreement, you shall be entitled to be issued a number of shares of the Common Stock of JPMorgan Chase equal to the number of PSUs, if any, plus any additional Reinvested Dividend Equivalent Share Units, vesting on such date, less the number withheld to satisfy tax withholding obligations.
nodes.summary:
- Document type and scope: Terms and conditions for a JPMorgan Chase & Co. Long‑Term Incentive Plan Performance Share Unit (PSU) Award for Operating Committee members, featuring protection-based vesting provisions, and governed by the Plan and Prospectus (which supersede other agreements). 
- Acceptance and governance: Award is effective on the Grant Date unless declined by the stated deadline; if declined, it is canceled as of the Grant Date. Capitalized terms follow Plan definitions. 
- Nature and purpose of award: Each PSU is a non-transferable right to receive one share of JPMorgan Chase common stock at vesting; the award is intended to drive sustained long-term performance and align interests with shareholders. 
- Vesting and payout mechanics: 
  - Number of PSUs vesting equals the Target Award Number multiplied by the Award Payout Percentage determined from a Performance Table. 
  - Performance Ranking and Award Payout Percentage are calculated by a Calculation Agent using defined metrics, including ROTCE (return on tangible common equity), Firm Reported ROTCE, Average Tangible Common Equity (if applicable), and the Performance Table (and its footnote) over the Performance Period. 
  - Delivery of vested shares occurs by a date consistent with Section 409A compliance (as referenced). 
- Dividend equivalents: During the vesting period, cash dividends on common stock are notionally reinvested into additional units (Reinvested Dividend Equivalent Share Units) based on the fair market value on each dividend payment date, but only on the actual number of shares that vest. These additional units are delivered at vesting. 
- Taxes and net share issuance: On the vesting date, shares equal to vested PSUs plus dividend equivalent units are issued net of shares withheld for tax obligations. 
- Post-vest holding requirement: Net shares are subject to a two-year transfer restriction (no transferring, assigning, hedging, selling, pledging, or encumbering). Early lapse of restrictions is allowed only upon death or for accelerated distribution due to ethics/conflict considerations tied to employment by a government entity. 
- Cancellation/forfeiture: Award may be canceled in whole or in part pursuant to the terms and conditions.

nodes.title: Calculation of Performance Ranking
nodes.heading: 39.5 Calculation of Performance Ranking
nodes.start_phrase: For purposes of the Performance Ranking, the ranking of the Firm and of each Performance Company for the Performance Period shall be determined and calculated by the Calculation Agent, using the definitions of “Average Tangible Common Equity” (if otherwise applicable), “Calculated PSUs”, “Firm Reported ROTCE”, “Performance Table” (including its footnote) and “ROTCE” as set forth in the “Definitions ” section of these terms and conditions.
nodes.summary:
- Document type and scope: Terms and conditions for a JPMorgan Chase & Co. Long-Term Incentive Plan Performance Share Unit (PSU) award for Operating Committee members, featuring protection-based vesting provisions. The Plan governs over any conflicting award terms; Award Agreement, Plan, and Prospectus supersede prior agreements.
- Acceptance/decline: Award is effective as of the Grant Date unless declined by the stated deadline; if declined, it is cancelled as of the Grant Date.
- Form and purpose: Each PSU is a non-transferable right to one share of JPMorgan Chase common stock upon vesting; designed to promote sustained long-term performance and alignment with shareholders.
- Vesting outcome: Number of PSUs that vest equals Target Award Number multiplied by an Award Payout Percentage determined via a Performance Table; performance calculations use defined metrics (e.g., ROTCE, Average Tangible Common Equity) and are binding; rounding to the nearest hundredth and tie rules apply. Delivery timing is subject to Section 409A compliance.
- Dividend equivalents: During the vesting period, cash dividends are notionally reinvested into additional units (Reinvested Dividend Equivalent Share Units) based on the fair market value on each dividend date; these vest and are delivered with the PSUs.
- Holding requirement: Net shares delivered at vest (after tax withholding) are restricted from transfer, assignment, hedging, sale, pledge, or encumbrance for two years post-vesting; restrictions can lapse earlier in case of death or an accelerated distribution for ethics/conflict reasons tied to government employment.
- Capital ratio performance threshold: If the Firm’s CET1 ratio falls below a set threshold at any year-end during the performance period, up to one-third of the Target Award Number may be downward adjusted by the CMDC for each such year.
- Vesting period definition: From Grant Date to the vesting date; Firm may extend the vesting period and may restrict delivered shares post-vesting as noted.
- Protection-based vesting and potential cancellation: Award is intended to vest if continuously employed through vest date or upon qualifying termination (Job Elimination, Full Career Eligibility, Government Office, Disability), but up to 50% of the award (including related dividend units) designated as “At Risk PSUs” may be cancelled at the CEO’s discretion, subject to CMDC ratification (Board involvement for CEO awards), based on:
  - Sustained unsatisfactory performance by you or the Firm versus stated priorities (including metrics such as net income, total net revenue, EPS, capital ratios, absolute and relative to peers).
  - Negative Firm-level annual pre-tax pre-provision income in any year of the vesting period.
  - RSU cancellations within a Line of Business you oversee due to failure to meet its annual financial threshold.
  - Failure to meet the Firmwide Financial Threshold.
  - Cancellation may occur before the performance period ends and continues to apply after qualifying terminations that allow continued vesting.
- Tax withholding: Shares are net-settled with shares withheld to satisfy tax obligations.
- Bonus recoupment: Award and the corresponding cash incentive for the performance year are subject to the JPMorgan Chase Bonus Recoupment Policy (as amended from time to time); the policy’s rights are not limited by these terms.
- Other notes: Calculations performed by the Calculation Agent; references to defined terms and detailed performance/ranking mechanics are provided in the Definitions and Performance Table sections.

nodes.title: Capital Ratio Performance Threshold
nodes.heading: 39.6 Capital Ratio Performance Threshold
nodes.start_phrase: Unvested PSUs are subject to reduction if the Firm’s Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) capital ratio at any year end falls below a predetermined threshold of ______%.
nodes.summary:
- This excerpt outlines key terms and conditions for JPMorgan Chase Performance Share Units (PSUs), with cross-references to the “Definitions” and “Performance Table” sections.
- Calculation standards: Except for Firm Reported ROTCE, performance calculations are shown as percentages to two decimal places, rounded to the nearest hundredth; tie-breaking rules are in the “Definitions—Performance Table.” All performance calculations are binding on recipients and their successors.
- Capital Ratio Performance Threshold: If the Firm’s CET1 ratio is below a preset threshold at any year-end during the Performance Period, up to one-third of the Target Award PSUs may be reduced for each such year by the Compensation and Management Development Committee (CMDC).
- Vesting Period: Runs from Grant Date to vesting date. The Firm may extend the vesting period and may restrict delivered shares post-vesting per referenced sections (Administrative Provision—Amendment, Holding Period, No Ownership Rights/Other Limitations).
- Protection-based vesting: Although intended to vest if employed through the vesting date or upon qualifying events (Job Elimination, Full Career Eligibility, Government Office, Disability), up to 50% of the award (At Risk PSUs, including reinvested dividend equivalents) may be canceled at the CEO’s discretion based on:
  - Sustained underperformance by the individual or Firm against stated priorities (considering metrics such as net income, total net revenue, EPS, and capital ratios, absolute and relative to peers).
  - Negative Firm-level annual pre-tax pre-provision income during the vesting period.
  - RSU cancellations in a Line of Business under the recipient’s responsibility due to failing its annual Financial Threshold.
  - The Firm failing to meet the Firmwide Financial Threshold.
  Cancellations can occur before the Performance Period ends and are capped at 50% of the Target Award. These cancellation conditions continue to apply after qualifying terminations that allow continued vesting. Determinations require CMDC ratification; for current or former CEOs, the Committee decides and the Board ratifies.
- Bonus Recoupment: The award and the cash incentive for the specified performance year are subject to the JPMorgan Chase Bonus Recoupment Policy (or successor). The policy is accessible on the Firm’s corporate governance website, and the terms do not limit the Firm’s rights under that policy.
- Additional cross-references: “Number to Vest on Vesting Date,” “Remedies,” and other administrative and holding period provisions.

nodes.title: Vesting Period
nodes.heading: 39.7 Vesting Period
nodes.start_phrase: The period from the Grant Date to the vesting date is the “Vesting Period”.
nodes.summary:
- Covers performance share unit (PSU) terms, referencing a “Definitions” section and stating that, except for Firm Reported ROTCE, all calculations are shown to two decimal places and rounded to the nearest hundredth; tie outcomes are governed by the “Definitions—Performance Table,” and all performance calculations are binding on the participant and successors.
- Establishes a Capital Ratio Performance Threshold: if the Firm’s year-end CET1 ratio falls below a predetermined percentage in any year of the Performance Period, up to one-third of the Target Award PSUs may be reduced by the Compensation and Management Development Committee (CMDC) for each such year.
- Defines the Vesting Period as the time from Grant Date to vesting date, noting the Firm’s right to extend vesting, impose post-vesting restrictions, and apply a holding period.
- Details Protection-Based Vesting: the award is intended to vest if the participant remains employed through vesting or meets continued vesting criteria (Job Elimination, Full Career Eligibility, Government Office, Disability), but vesting remains subject to other terms including performance thresholds and remedies.
- Authorizes the CEO to cancel up to 50% of the award (including Reinvested Dividend Equivalent Share Units) as “At Risk PSUs,” based on factors such as sustained underperformance against priorities (including metrics like net income, revenue, EPS, capital ratios), negative firm-level pre-tax pre-provision income in any calendar year, cancellation of RSUs in a participant’s Line of Business due to failing its financial threshold, or failure to meet the Firmwide Financial Threshold; cancellations can occur before the end of the Performance Period and continue to apply even if employment ends under continued-vesting scenarios.
- Requires ratification of protection-based vesting determinations by the CMDC; for any current or former CEO award, determinations are made by the Committee and ratified by the Board.
- Subjects the participant to the JPMorgan Chase Bonus Recoupment Policy (as amended from time to time) for both the relevant performance year’s cash incentive and this award, without limiting the Firm’s rights under that policy.

nodes.title: Protection-Based Vesting
nodes.heading: 39.8 Protection-Based Vesting
nodes.start_phrase: This award is intended and expected to vest on the vesting date, provided that you are continuously employed by the Firm through such vesting date, or you meet the requirements for continued vesting described under the subsections “--Job Elimination”, “--Full Career Eligibility”, “--Government Office” or “--Disability”.
nodes.summary:
- Cross-references to Definitions and Performance Table sections; performance calculations (except Firm Reported ROTCE) rounded to the nearest hundredth (xx.yy%) and deemed binding and conclusive.
- Capital Ratio Performance Threshold: If JPMorgan Chase’s year-end CET1 ratio falls below a preset threshold in any year of the Performance Period, up to one-third of the Target PSUs may be reduced by the CMDC for each such year.
- Vesting Period runs from Grant Date to vesting date; the Firm may extend vesting and impose post-vesting share restrictions under separate provisions.
- Protection-Based Vesting: While awards are intended to vest with continuous employment (or upon Job Elimination, Full Career Eligibility, Government Office, or Disability), up to 50% of the award (including reinvested dividend equivalent units) may be cancelled at the CEO’s discretion, subject to CMDC ratification (and Board ratification for CEO awards), based on:
  - Sustained unsatisfactory individual or Firm performance against priorities (considering metrics such as net income, revenue, EPS, and capital ratios, absolute and relative to peers).
  - Negative Firm-level annual pre-tax, pre-provision income in any year during the vesting period.
  - Cancellation of RSUs in a Line of Business under the recipient’s responsibility due to not meeting its LOB Financial Threshold.
  - Failure to meet the Firmwide Financial Threshold.
- Such cancellations can occur before the end of the Performance Period, capped at 50% of the Target Award; cancellation provisions continue to apply even if employment ends under the eligible continued-vesting scenarios.
- Bonus Recoupment: Both the cash incentive for the applicable performance year and this award are subject to the JPMorgan Chase Bonus Recoupment Policy; nothing in the terms limits the Firm’s recoupment rights.

nodes.title: Bonus Recoupment
nodes.heading: 39.9 Bonus Recoupment
nodes.start_phrase: In consideration of the grant of this award, you agree that you are subject to the JPMorgan Chase Bonus Recoupment Policy (or successor policy) as in effect from time to time as it applies both to the cash incentive compensation awarded to you for performance year 20______ and to this award.
nodes.summary:
- Calculation conventions and authority: Performance calculations (except Firm Reported ROTCE) are expressed to two decimal places and rounded to the nearest hundredth; tie-handling is per the “Definitions—Performance Table.” All performance-based calculations are binding and conclusive on the participant and successors.
- Capital Ratio Performance Threshold: If the Firm’s CET1 ratio at any year-end during the Performance Period falls below a predetermined threshold (blank in excerpt), up to one-third of the Target Award Number of PSUs may be reduced for each such year at the discretion of the Compensation and Management Development Committee (CMDC).
- Vesting Period: Defined as the period from Grant Date to vesting date; the Firm may extend the vesting period and may impose post-vesting restrictions on delivered shares. References are made to related provisions (Administrative Provision—Amendment, No Ownership Rights/Other Limitations, and Holding Period).
- Protection-based vesting framework: Award is intended to vest if continuously employed through vesting, or upon meeting continued vesting conditions for Job Elimination, Full Career Eligibility, Government Office, or Disability. Actual vesting remains subject to other sections (e.g., Number to Vest, Capital Ratio Performance Threshold, Remedies).
- At Risk PSUs and potential cancellation: Up to 50% of the award (including Reinvested Dividend Equivalent Share Units) may be cancelled at the CEO’s discretion, based on:
  - Sustained unsatisfactory performance by the participant or Firm/Operating Committee priorities (metrics may include net income, total net revenue, EPS, and capital ratios, absolute or relative to peers).
  - Negative Firm-level annual pre-tax pre-provision income in any year during the vesting period.
  - RSU cancellations within a Line of Business under the participant’s (current or prior) responsibility due to not meeting its Line of Business Financial Threshold.
  - Failure to meet the Firmwide Financial Threshold.
  Cancellation can occur before the Performance Period ends, capped at 50% of the Target Award Number.
- Continued vesting scenarios: If employment ends under Job Elimination, Full Career Eligibility, Government Office (with possible acceleration), or Disability, the cancellation conditions above still apply during continued vesting.
- Governance of determinations: Protection-based vesting decisions require ratification by the CMDC; for awards to a current or former CEO, decisions are made by the CMDC and ratified by the Board.
- Bonus Recoupment: The participant agrees to be subject to JPMorgan Chase’s Bonus Recoupment Policy (as amended from time to time) for both the cash incentive for the specified performance year (blank in excerpt) and this award; nothing in these terms limits the Firm’s rights under that policy.

nodes.title: Termination of Employment
nodes.heading: 39.10 Termination of Employment
nodes.start_phrase: Except as explicitly set forth below under the subsections captioned “--Job Elimination”, “--Full Career Eligibility”, “--Government Office” or “--Disability” or under the section captioned “ Death ”, this award (for avoidance of doubt, including any associated Reinvested Dividend Equivalent Share Units) will be cancelled in full effective on the date your employment with the Firm terminates for any reason.
nodes.summary:
- Core rule: Upon termination of employment for any reason, the award (including any Reinvested Dividend Equivalent Share Units) is cancelled immediately, except as provided under Job Elimination, Full Career Eligibility, Government Office, Disability, or Death.
- Post-termination vesting: You may continue to vest as if still employed, subject to all terms (including Protection-Based Vesting, Number to Vest on Vesting Date, Bonus Recoupment, Your Obligations, and Remedies) if one of the following applies:
  - Job Elimination: HR Director (or nominee) determines your role was eliminated; you cooperated professionally after notice; and you meet the Release/Certification Requirements.
  - Full Career Eligibility: HR (or nominee) determines you voluntarily resigned; you had at least 5 years of continuous service; your age plus Recognized Service ≥ 60; you gave at least 180 days’ advance written notice, cooperated during that period, and performed no services for any other employer; HR determines before termination that continued vesting is appropriate based on your performance and conduct; for 36 months from grant you do not work in any capacity for a Financial Services Company or in your profession (government, education, or Not‑for‑Profit work permitted); and you meet the Release/Certification Requirements. The Firm may require continued service during the notice period or shorten it (not earlier than when age/service criteria are met). Additional notice policies may apply.
  - Government Office: You voluntarily leave to accept or run for an elective Government Office, per the Government Office Requirements (see Definitions).
  - Disability: Termination occurs because you cannot return to work while on LTD Plan benefits (or local equivalent), or due to a qualifying long‑term disability if not covered by the LTD Plan; you request continued vesting in writing within 30 days, provide required documentation, obtain the Firm’s written consent, and meet the Release/Certification Requirements.
- Several conditions rely on defined terms and requirements referenced elsewhere (e.g., Release/Certification Requirements, Notice Period, Definitions).

nodes.title: Release/Certification
nodes.heading: 39.11 Release/Certification
nodes.start_phrase: To qualify for continued vesting after termination of your employment under any of the foregoing circumstances:
nodes.summary:
- Sets conditions for continued vesting after employment ends, requiring a timely release of claims and compliance certifications.
- Details “Full Career Eligibility” prerequisites: advance written notice (at least 180 days), confirmation of eligibility, and written consent; certification of compliance with employment restrictions for “Full Career Eligibility” and “Government Office.”
- Outlines requirements for continued vesting in case of Disability (notice/documentation and written consent).
- States that all other Award Agreement terms must be met to maintain vesting eligibility.
- Describes death benefits: beneficiary/estate receives shares based on completed-year performance (average of completed calendar years), vesting one-third of target PSUs per completed year, with 100% payout assumption for remaining years; includes dividend equivalent share units through date of death.
- Provides distribution timing upon death: no later than the end of the calendar year following death (administrative practice aims for registration within ~60 days after required documentation is received).
- Enumerates participant obligations tied to receiving the award: non-solicitation, confidentiality, non-disparagement, cooperation, compliance with the agreement, and notice period.
- Non-solicitation covenant: for the longer of one year post-termination or three years from grant date (if award not canceled), prohibits soliciting/inducing Firm employees, hiring recent Firm employees with limited exceptions, and soliciting/diverting Firm customers/suppliers known or serviced through employment (with a carveout for publicly known institutional customers when no confidential information is used); excludes authorized actions taken in the normal course of employment.
- Confidentiality covenant: prohibits using or disclosing Firm confidential information and communicating with media about Firm-related matters during and after employment, except as allowed by the Code of Conduct, policies, law, or legal process (section text is partially truncated).

nodes.title: Death
nodes.heading: 39.12 Death
nodes.start_phrase: If you die while you are eligible to vest in this award, your designated beneficiary on file with the Firm’s Stock Administration Department (or your estate or if no beneficiary has been designated or survives you or if beneficiary designation is not recognized locally) may be entitled to receive a distribution of a number of shares of Common Stock associated with your award.
nodes.summary:
- Sets conditions for continued vesting after employment termination, requiring: timely execution of a Firm-specified release of claims; for Full Career Eligibility, advance confirmation of eligibility (including at least 180 days’ written notice) and written consent; for Full Career Eligibility and Government Office, certification prior to each vesting date of compliance with post-employment restrictions; for Disability, required notice/documentation and written consent; and overall compliance with the Award Agreement.
- Details death provisions: beneficiary (or estate) may receive Common Stock tied to the award; payout uses average performance for completed calendar years with one-third of Target PSUs per completed year and assumes 100% payout for remaining years; includes Reinvested Dividend Equivalent Share Units through date of death; distribution no later than the end of the calendar year following death (administrative practice targets registration within 60 days after required documents are received).
- Outlines participant obligations tied to the award:
  - Non-Solicitation of Employees and Customers: during employment and for the longer of one year post-termination or three years from grant (if the award isn’t canceled at termination), prohibitions on soliciting or hiring certain Firm employees and on soliciting/diverting customers, suppliers, or other business relationships, with carve-outs for normal course authorized actions and publicly known institutional customers not using Firm confidential information.
  - Confidential Information: prohibition during and after employment on using or disclosing Firm confidential information and on media communications about Firm-related matters, except as permitted by the Code of Conduct, Firm policies, or law/legal process.
- References additional obligations (Non-Disparagement, Cooperation, Compliance with Award Agreement, Notice Period) noted but not fully detailed in the excerpt.

nodes.title: Your Obligations
nodes.heading: 39.13 Your Obligations
nodes.start_phrase: In consideration of the grant of this award, you agree to comply with and be bound by the obligations set forth below next to the subsections captioned “--Non-Solicitation of Employees and Customers”, “--Confidential Information”, “--Non-Disparagement”, ”-- Cooperation”, “--Compliance with Award Agreement”, and “--Notice Period”.
nodes.summary:
- Sets conditions for continued vesting after employment ends, requiring a timely release of claims, compliance with the Award Agreement, and specific certifications/consents depending on circumstance.
- Full Career Eligibility: must confirm eligibility with management before termination, provide at least 180 days’ advance written notice, request treatment as eligible, and receive written consent; must certify ongoing compliance with post-employment restrictions on the firm’s authorized form prior to each vesting date.
- Government Office: must certify compliance with applicable post-employment restrictions on the firm’s authorized form prior to vesting dates while restrictions are outstanding.
- Disability: must meet notice and documentation requirements and obtain written consent for continued vesting.
- Death: beneficiary (or estate) may receive shares based on the average performance for completed years, vesting one-third of target PSUs per completed calendar year, and assuming 100% payout for remaining years; also includes reinvested dividend equivalent share units through date of death. Shares are distributed by the end of the calendar year following the year of death (administrative practice is to register shares within 60 days after receipt of required documentation).
- Employee obligations tied to the award include non-solicitation, confidentiality, non-disparagement, cooperation, compliance with the Award Agreement, and a notice period.
- Non-solicitation: during employment and for the longer of one year post-termination or three years from grant date (if award not canceled), prohibits (i) soliciting current employees to leave (with exceptions for job eliminations), (ii) hiring recent former employees within six months unless their job was eliminated, and (iii) soliciting or diverting then-current customers/suppliers known or serviced through employment, to the fullest extent allowed by law. Excludes publicly known institutional customers serviced post-employment without using confidential information and authorized actions in the normal course of employment.
- Confidential information: prohibits using or disclosing firm confidential information and communicating with the media about firm matters during and after employment, except as permitted by the Code of Conduct, policy, law, or legal process.

nodes.title: Non-Solicitation of Employees and Customers
nodes.heading: 39.13.1 Non-Solicitation of Employees and Customers
nodes.start_phrase: During your employment by the Firm and for the longer of the (i) one year period following the termination of your employment or, (ii) if your award is not cancelled as of your termination date, the three year period from Grant Date, you will not directly or indirectly, whether on your own behalf or on behalf of any other party, without the prior written consent of the Director of Human Resources: (i) solicit, induce or encourage any of the Firm’s then current employees to leave the Firm or to apply for employment elsewhere, unless such current employee has received official, written notice that his or her employment will be terminated due to job elimination (ii) hire any employee or former employee who was employed by the Firm at the date your employment terminated, unless the individual’s employment terminated because his or her job was eliminated, or the individual’s employment with the Firm has been terminated for more than six months, (iii) to the fullest extent enforceable under applicable law, solicit or induce or attempt to induce to leave the Firm, or divert or attempt to divert from doing business with the Firm, any then current customers, suppliers or other persons or entities that were serviced by you or whose names became known to you by virtue of your employment with the Firm, or otherwise interfere with the relationship between the Firm and such customers, suppliers or other persons or entities.
nodes.summary:
- Release/Certification requirements for continued vesting after employment ends: execute a Firm-specified release of claims; for Full Career Eligibility, confirm eligibility, give at least 180 days’ written notice, and obtain written consent; for Full Career Eligibility and Government Office, certify ongoing compliance with employment restrictions before each vesting date; for Disability, provide required notice/documentation and obtain written consent; comply with all Award Agreement terms.
- Death provisions: beneficiary or estate may receive shares based on the “Number to Vest on the Vesting Date” using average performance for completed years and 100% payout for remaining years; additional Reinvested Dividend Equivalent Share Units through the date of death; distribution no later than the end of the year following death (administratively targeted within 60 days after required documentation).
- Participant obligations in exchange for the award:
  - Non-solicitation of employees and customers during employment and for the longer of one year post-termination or three years from grant (if award not canceled), with specified exceptions (e.g., job eliminations, former employees after six months, publicly known institutional customers without use of confidential information) and allowance for authorized on-the-job actions.
  - Confidentiality: no use/disclosure of Firm confidential information or media communications about Firm matters; no post-termination access to internal systems without authorization; whistleblower and legal-response carve-outs; “Confidential Information” as defined in the Code of Conduct.
  - Non-disparagement: no public statements disparaging the Firm or its stakeholders, with whistleblower/legal-response carve-outs.
  - Cooperation: full cooperation and accurate information in audits, litigation, investigations, and governmental proceedings, with reimbursement of reasonable out-of-pocket expenses.
  - Compliance: provide information to verify Award Agreement compliance; authorize Firm to disclose agreement terms to affected third parties, including prospective employers.
  - Notice Period: if contract/policy requires advance notice of resignation, provide it; Firm may require work or place on paid leave during notice; maintain loyalty, refrain from other employment, and receive base pay/benefits until termination; parties may modify by mutual agreement; separate 180-day advance notice applies for Full Career Eligibility resignations.
- Remedies (cancellation/recapture): up to 100% of outstanding PSUs (including Reinvested Dividend Equivalent Share Units and Calculated PSUs) may be canceled for detrimental or risk-related conduct, including material financial/reputational harm, awards based on materially inaccurate metrics (regardless of fault), material misrepresentation, or failure (improperly or with gross negligence) to timely identify/raise/assess material risks; in addition to other cancellation/recoupment provisions (Protection-Based Vesting, Bonus Recoupment, Termination of Employment).

nodes.title: Confidential Information
nodes.heading: 39.13.2 Confidential Information
nodes.start_phrase: You will not, either during your employment with the Firm or thereafter, directly or indirectly (i) use or disclose to anyone any confidential information related to the Firm’s business, or (ii) communicate with the press or other media about matters related to the Firm, its customers or employees, including matters and activities relating to your employment, or the employment of others, by the Firm, in the case of either (i) or (ii), except as explicitly permitted by the JPMorgan Chase Code of Conduct and applicable policies or law or legal process.
nodes.summary:
- Confidential information: Defined as in the JPMorgan Chase Code of Conduct; access to the Firm’s private/internal information via phone, intranet, or internet requires written authorization.
- Whistleblower and legal cooperation carve-outs: Nothing in the award restricts reporting suspected legal or Code of Conduct violations to management, directors, government, regulators, self-regulatory bodies, attorneys, or courts, or responding truthfully to official inquiries.
- Non-disparagement: During and after employment, you must not make public statements that disparage the Firm or its people as a group, with exceptions for lawful reporting and truthful participation in investigations or proceedings.
- Cooperation duty: You must fully cooperate with the Firm and its counsel in audits, tax matters, litigation, investigations, or governmental proceedings; reasonable out-of-pocket expenses will be reimbursed.
- Compliance with the Award Agreement: You must provide information needed to assess compliance and authorize the Firm to disclose award terms to affected third parties, including prospective employers.
- Notice Period obligations: If subject to a contractual/policy notice period, you must give the required written advance notice. The Firm may require continued services or place you on paid leave during the notice period. You must devote full time and loyalty to the Firm, not work for others, and will receive base salary and certain benefits until termination; the notice length can be mutually modified or waived. Separately, a 180-day advance notice applies for “Full Career Eligibility” terminations.
- Remedies—cancellation/recapture: In addition to other cancellation provisions (Protection-Based Vesting, Bonus Recoupment, Termination of Employment), up to 100% of outstanding PSUs (including Reinvested Dividend Equivalent Share Units and Calculated PSUs) may be canceled if the Firm determines:
  - You engaged in conduct causing material financial or reputational harm to the Firm;
  - The award was based on materially inaccurate performance metrics (regardless of your responsibility);
  - The award was based on your material misrepresentation; or
  - You improperly or with gross negligence failed to timely identify, raise, or assess material risks as reasonably expected.

nodes.title: Non-Disparagement
nodes.heading: 39.13.3 Non-Disparagement
nodes.start_phrase: You will not, either during your employment with the Firm or thereafter, make or encourage others to make any public statement or release any information in verbal, written, electronic or any other form, that is intended to, or reasonably could be foreseen to, disparage, embarrass or criticize the Firm or its employees, officers, directors or shareholders as a group.
nodes.summary:
- Confidentiality and access controls: Confidential information is as defined in the JPMorgan Chase Code of Conduct; access to the Firm’s private/internal information (via phone, intranet, internet) requires written authorization and protection of such information.
- Whistleblower and truth-telling protections: Nothing prohibits reporting suspected legal or Code of Conduct violations to management, directors, government, regulators, self-regulatory agencies, attorneys, or courts, or responding truthfully to official inquiries.
- Non-disparagement: No public statements that disparage, embarrass, or criticize the Firm or its people, with exceptions for lawful reporting and cooperation with legal/regulatory processes.
- Cooperation obligation: Full cooperation with the Firm and its counsel in audits, tax matters, litigation, investigations, and governmental proceedings; reimbursement for reasonable out-of-pocket expenses.
- Compliance with Award Agreement: Provide information to confirm compliance; authorize the Firm to disclose award terms to affected third parties, including prospective employers.
- Notice Period: If subject to a contractual/policy notice period, provide required advance written notice of resignation; Firm may require continued service or place employee on paid leave during notice; employee must devote full time to the Firm, not work elsewhere, and will receive base salary and certain benefits; parties may mutually adjust the notice length; separate 180-day advance notice applies under “Full Career Eligibility.”
- Remedies—cancellation/recapture: Up to 100% of outstanding PSUs (including reinvested dividend equivalents and calculated PSUs) may be cancelled for detrimental or risk-related conduct, including material financial/reputational harm, awards based on materially inaccurate metrics (regardless of fault), material misrepresentation, or improper/grossly negligent failure to timely identify/escalate/assess material risks; references to additional cancellation under Protection-Based Vesting, Bonus Recoupment, and Termination of Employment.

nodes.title: Cooperation
nodes.heading: 39.13.4 Cooperation
nodes.start_phrase: You will cooperate fully with and provide full and accurate information to the Firm and its counsel with respect to any matter (including any audit, tax proceeding, litigation, investigation or governmental proceeding) with respect to which you may have knowledge or information, subject to reimbursement for actual, appropriate and reasonable out-of-pocket expenses incurred by you.
nodes.summary:
- Confidentiality and authorized access: Access to the Firm’s private/internal information via phone, intranet, or internet requires written authorization. “Confidential information” has the meaning in the JPMorgan Chase Code of Conduct. The agreement does not restrict lawful reporting to management, directors, government, regulators, self-regulatory bodies, attorneys, or courts, nor truthful responses to legal/regulatory inquiries.
- Non-disparagement: You may not make or encourage public statements that disparage, embarrass, or criticize the Firm or its stakeholders during or after employment, with carve-outs for lawful reporting and truthful participation in investigations or proceedings.
- Cooperation: You must fully cooperate with the Firm and its counsel in audits, tax matters, litigation, investigations, and governmental proceedings, with reimbursement of reasonable out-of-pocket expenses.
- Compliance and disclosure: You must provide information needed to confirm compliance with the Award Agreement and authorize the Firm to disclose its terms to affected third parties, including prospective employers.
- Notice period: If subject to a contractual/policy notice period, you must give the required written notice before resigning. The Firm may require continued service or place you on paid leave during the notice period. You must devote full time and loyalty to the Firm, refrain from working for other employers, and will receive base salary and certain benefits until termination. The notice period may be mutually modified/waived. A separate 180-day advance notice applies for terminations under “Full Career Eligibility.”
- Remedies—cancellation/recapture: In addition to other vesting/recoupment/termination provisions, up to 100% of outstanding PSUs (including reinvested dividend equivalents and Calculated PSUs) may be cancelled if the Firm determines detrimental or risk-related conduct occurred, including: conduct causing material financial or reputational harm; awards based on materially inaccurate performance metrics (regardless of fault); material misrepresentation; or improper/grossly negligent failure to timely identify, raise, or assess material risks.

nodes.title: Compliance with Award Agreement
nodes.heading: 39.13.5 Compliance with Award Agreement
nodes.start_phrase: You will provide the Firm with any information reasonably requested to determine compliance with the Award Agreement, and you authorize the Firm to disclose the terms of the Award Agreement to any third party who might be affected thereby, including your prospective employer.
nodes.summary:

- Requires full cooperation with the Firm and its counsel in audits, tax matters, litigation, investigations, and governmental proceedings, with reimbursement of reasonable out-of-pocket expenses.
- Requires providing information to verify compliance with the Award Agreement and authorizes the Firm to disclose its terms to third parties, including prospective employers.
- Establishes notice period obligations: if subject to a contractual/policy notice requirement, the employee must give the required advance written notice; the Firm may have the employee work or place them on paid leave during the notice period; during this time the employee must devote full time/loyalty to the Firm, perform no services for others, and will receive base salary and certain benefits; the period can be mutually modified; separately, a 180-day advance notice applies for “Full Career Eligibility.”
- Sets remedies allowing cancellation/recapture of up to 100% of outstanding PSUs (including reinvested dividend equivalents and calculated PSUs) if the Firm determines detrimental or risk-related conduct, including: conduct causing material financial or reputational harm; awards based on materially inaccurate performance metrics (regardless of fault); material misrepresentation; or improper/grossly negligent failure to timely identify, raise, or assess material risks. References additional cancellation under Protection-Based Vesting, Bonus Recoupment, and Termination of Employment sections.

nodes.title: Notice Period
nodes.heading: 39.13.6 Notice Period
nodes.start_phrase: If you are subject to a notice period or become subject to a notice period after the Grant Date, whether by contract or by policy, that requires you to provide advance written notice of your intention to terminate your employment (“Notice Period”), then as consideration for this award and continued employment, you will provide the Firm with the necessary advance written n o t i c e t h a t a p p l i e s t o y o u , a s s p e c i f i e d b y s u c h c o n t r a c t o r p o l i c y .
nodes.summary:
- Confidential information: Reaffirms that “Confidential Information” is defined by the JPMorgan Chase Code of Conduct; restricts accessing or sharing the Firm’s private/internal information without written authorization (including via phone, intranet, or internet); clarifies that nothing prevents reporting suspected legal or Code of Conduct violations to management, directors, regulators, government, self-regulatory bodies, attorneys, or courts, or from truthfully responding to official inquiries.
- Non-disparagement: Prohibits making or encouraging public statements that disparage the Firm or its stakeholders during or after employment, with carve-outs allowing lawful reporting and truthful cooperation with authorities and courts.
- Cooperation: Requires full cooperation and accurate information in audits, tax matters, litigation, investigations, and governmental proceedings; allows reimbursement of reasonable out-of-pocket expenses.
- Compliance with Award Agreement: Employee must provide information to verify compliance; Firm may disclose Award Agreement terms to affected third parties, including prospective employers.
- Notice Period: If subject to a contractual/policy notice requirement, the employee must give the required written advance notice of resignation. The Firm may require continued service or place the employee on paid leave during the notice period; the employee must devote full time to the Firm, not work elsewhere, and will receive base salary and certain benefits until termination. Parties may mutually modify/waive the period. Separately, a 180-day advance notice applies for terminations under the “Full Career Eligibility” provision.
- Remedies—cancellation/recapture: In addition to other cancellation/recoupment provisions (Protection-Based Vesting, Bonus Recoupment, Termination of Employment), the Firm may, in its sole discretion, cancel up to 100% of the award (including PSUs, Reinvested Dividend Equivalent Share Units, and Calculated PSUs) if:
  - The employee engages in conduct causing material financial or reputational harm to the Firm,
