nodes.title: Remedies
nodes.heading: 39.14 Remedies
nodes.start_phrase: In addition to the cancellation provisions described under the sections captioned “ Protection-Based Vesting ”, “Bonus Recoupment ” and “ Termination of Employment ”, up to 100% of your award (for the avoidance of doubt, including any associated Reinvested Dividend Equivalent Share Units as well as the Calculated PSUs) your outstanding PSUs under this award may be cancelled if the Firm in its sole discretion determines that:
nodes.summary:
- Confidentiality and access: Confidential information defined per JPMorgan Chase Code of Conduct; restrictions on accessing the Firm’s private/internal information without written authorization; carve-out permitting lawful reporting to management, directors, regulators, government, attorneys, or courts and truthful responses to official inquiries.
- Non-disparagement: No public disparagement of the Firm or its people during or after employment; does not restrict lawful reporting or truthful participation in legal/regulatory matters.
- Cooperation: Obligation to fully cooperate and provide accurate information in audits, tax matters, litigation, investigations, or governmental proceedings; reimbursement for reasonable out-of-pocket expenses.
- Compliance with Award Agreement: Provide information requested to verify compliance; authorize the Firm to disclose Award terms to affected third parties, including prospective employers.
- Notice Period: If subject to a contractual/policy notice period, provide the required written advance notice of resignation; the Firm may have you work or place you on paid leave during the period; you must devote full time to the Firm, not work elsewhere, and will receive base salary and certain benefits; the period may be mutually modified; separate 180-day advance notice under “Full Career Eligibility” still applies.
- Remedies—cancellation/suspension: Up to 100% of outstanding PSUs (including reinvested dividend equivalents and calculated PSUs) may be canceled for detrimental conduct causing material financial/reputational harm, awards based on materially inaccurate metrics or your misrepresentation, failure to identify/raise material risks, termination for Cause (or could-have-been Cause), failure to meet notice/cooperation/employment restrictions, failure to return required Release/Certification forms, or violations of “Your Obligations.” The Firm may suspend vesting/distributions during evaluation and is not responsible for market fluctuations; suspended units may be reinstated per plan procedures.
- Recovery/clawback: Repayment up to the fair market value of previously distributed shares may be required for distributions within three years before notice-of-recovery in cases of fraud, knowing/willful misconduct, violations of “Your Obligations,” or post-termination employment restrictions (Full Career Eligibility or Government Office). Additional one-year lookback may apply per “Recapture Provisions.” Notice-of-recovery may be electronic/written to last known address and preserves recovery rights. Shares include those withheld for taxes, but repayment is not required for irrevocable tax withholdings/payments that cannot be recovered; repayment may be in shares or cash; not a penalty; separate “Bonus Recoupment” obligations still apply.
- Injunctive relief: The Firm may seek an injunction for immediate/irreparable harm from violations, in addition to other legal remedies.
- Administrative provisions—tax withholding: The Firm may retain shares from distributions or take other steps to satisfy applicable withholding and tax obligations.

nodes.title: Administrative Provisions
nodes.heading: 39.15 Administrative Provisions
nodes.start_phrase: Withholding Taxes: As a result of legal and/or tax obligations the Firm, in its sole discretion, may (i) retain from each distribution the number of shares of Common Stock required to satisfy applicable tax obligations or (ii) implement any other desirable or necessary procedures, so that appropriate withholding and other taxes are paid to the competent authorities with respect to the vested shares and the award.
nodes.summary:
- Grounds for cancellation and/or recovery of the award: termination for Cause (including post-termination determinations that Cause existed); failure to meet advance notice/cooperation requirements or employment restrictions tied to termination; failure to return required Release/Certification forms by the deadline; or violation of “Your Obligations.”
- Right to suspend vesting and/or share distributions while the Firm evaluates cancellation/recovery or conditions for distribution; the Firm is not liable for price fluctuations during suspension; suspended units may be reinstated per plan procedures (see Administrative Provisions—No Ownership Rights/Other Limitations).
- Clawback/repayment obligation: you may be required to repay up to the Fair Market Value (as of vest/acceleration) of the gross number of previously distributed shares (including those subject to holding requirements):
  - Within three years prior to a notice-of-recovery if the Firm determines you committed fraud, engaged in knowing and willful misconduct, violated “Your Obligations,” or violated post-termination employment restrictions (Full Career Eligibility or Government Office).
  - Within one year prior to a notice-of-recovery if the Firm deems appropriate under the “Recapture Provisions.”
- Notice-of-recovery: written/electronic notice requiring or indicating the Firm is evaluating repayment; good-faith delivery to your last known address suffices; an evaluation notice preserves the Firm’s rights with no obligation to complete the evaluation.
- Treatment of tax-withheld shares: “shares distributed” includes shares withheld for taxes; intent is to require repayment only for shares you retain after tax liabilities; no repayment required for amounts representing irrevocable withholdings or unrecoverable tax payments as determined by the Firm or its nominee.
- Repayment may be made in shares or cash; any repayment is a lawful recovery under the Award Agreement, not a penalty; does not limit obligations under “Bonus Recoupment.”
- Right to an injunction: the Firm may obtain injunctive relief for violations or attempted violations of obligations, in addition to other legal or equitable remedies.
- Administrative tax withholding: the Firm may retain shares from distributions or implement other procedures to satisfy applicable tax obligations to authorities.

nodes.title: Withholding Taxes
nodes.heading: 39.15.1 Withholding Taxes
nodes.start_phrase: As a result of legal and/or tax obligations the Firm, in its sole discretion, may (i) retain from each distribution the number of shares of Common Stock required to satisfy applicable tax obligations or (ii) implement any other desirable or necessary procedures, so that appropriate withholding and other taxes are paid to the competent authorities with respect to the vested shares and the award.
nodes.summary:
- Sets out cancellation and recoupment triggers for a JPMorgan Chase PSU award, including termination for Cause (or if Cause could have been determined post-termination), failure to meet advance notice/cooperation or post-employment restrictions, failure to return required Release/Certification forms by deadline, and violations of “Your Obligations.”
- Allows the Firm to suspend vesting and/or distribution of shares while it evaluates cancellation, recovery, or distribution conditions; the Firm is not liable for market price changes during suspension, and suspended units may be reinstated per plan procedures.
- Describes clawback/repayment: the Firm may require you to repay up to the Fair Market Value of shares previously distributed (including those subject to holding requirements) if, within three years before a notice-of-recovery, you committed fraud/knowing willful misconduct, violated “Your Obligations,” or breached post-employment restrictions (Full Career Eligibility or Government Office). The Firm may also require repayment for shares distributed within one year before notice under “Recapture Provisions.”
- Defines “notice-of-recovery” (written/electronic notice sent to last known address) and clarifies that a notice of evaluation preserves the Firm’s rights without obligating it to complete the evaluation.
- Clarifies that “shares distributed” include shares withheld for taxes, but the Firm intends to seek repayment only for shares you could retain after taxes; amounts representing irrevocable tax withholdings/payments not recoverable by you will not be required to be repaid.
- Permits repayment in cash or shares and states such recovery is lawful and not a penalty; does not limit separate “Bonus Recoupment” rights.
- Provides for injunctive relief: the Firm can seek an immediate court injunction for any breach or attempted breach of obligations, in addition to other legal/equitable remedies.
- Administrative tax provisions: the Firm may satisfy withholding via share retention, market sale of shares, withholding from cash compensation (if required), or by retaining vested shares until you pay taxes directly.
- Right to set-off: to the extent permitted by law (including Section 409A), the Firm may retain funds or shares from vesting to satisfy your debts to the Firm, but will not recoup from your funds or unrestricted securities held in your personal Firm accounts without consent; certain designated accounts remain subject to plan limits.
- No ownership rights: PSUs confer no stock ownership or voting rights until shares are determined and vested. By accepting, you authorize the Firm to open a brokerage or book-entry account to deliver vested shares. During any suspension, PSUs may be canceled if cancellation provisions apply. The Firm may impose post-vesting restrictions (e.g., on sale, transfer, pledge, hedging) without affecting voting/dividend rights; if recovery applies during such restrictions, you may be required to repay up to the FMV of the restricted shares.
- Confirms the Award Agreement binds any JPMorgan Chase successor.
- States the award is not an employment contract; employment remains at-will, there is no right to future awards, and the award’s value is not used to calculate severance.
- Section 409A compliance: intended to comply with Section 409A; if you are a “specified employee” who separates from service and any portion is deferred compensation payable within six months as a result of separation, delivery is delayed until the first month after six full months post-separation; provides timing rules for payments when no substantial risk of forfeiture remains.
- Change in capital structure: the Committee may make equitable substitutions/adjustments to outstanding PSUs and share reserves for stock splits, dividends, recapitalizations, mergers, spin-offs, exchanges, or similar corporate events.

nodes.title: Right to Set Off
nodes.heading: 39.15.2 Right to Set Off
nodes.start_phrase: Although the Firm expects to settle this award in share(s) of Common Stock as of the applicable vesting date, as set forth in your Award Agreement, the Firm may, to the maximum extent permitted by applicable law (including Section 409A of the Code to the extent it is applicable to you), retain for itself funds or the Common Stock resulting from any vesting of this award to satisfy any obligation or debt that you owe to the Firm.
nodes.summary:
- Tax withholding and settlement: The firm may satisfy tax obligations arising from vesting by selling a portion of shares, withholding from cash compensation as required, or retaining vested shares until taxes are paid directly to authorities.
- Right to set off: Subject to law (including Section 409A), the firm may retain funds or vested shares to satisfy debts you owe the firm. It will not recover from your other funds or unrestricted securities held at the firm without your consent, except for accounts established for this award.
- No ownership rights prior to vesting: PSUs confer no ownership or voting rights. Shares are issued only after PSUs are determined and vest, following the firm’s issuance procedures. The firm may open a brokerage/book-entry account in your name to deliver vested shares.
- Suspension/cancellation and recoupment: PSUs can be suspended or canceled under provisions such as Protection-Based Vesting, Bonus Recoupment, Termination of Employment, Remedies, and via amendments permitting suspension. After vesting, the firm may impose restrictions (e.g., on sale, transfer, pledge, hedging) for a specified period; voting and dividend rights on issued shares remain during this period. If recovery provisions apply during the restriction period, you may owe up to the fair market value of the gross restricted shares as of vesting, despite set-off limits.
- Binding effect: The Award Agreement binds any successor to JPMorgan Chase.
- Employment status: The agreement is not an employment contract; employment is at-will. The award does not guarantee future awards and is not counted as compensation for severance purposes.
- Section 409A compliance: The award is intended to comply with Section 409A. For specified employees who separate from service, any deferred compensation shares distributable within six months will be delivered in the first month after six full months. If no substantial risk of forfeiture remains, the remainder of each calendar year after the vesting date is a permissible payment date for distributing vested portions.
- Corporate changes: In the event of stock splits, dividends (other than regular cash), recapitalizations, mergers, spin-offs, exchanges, or similar events, equitable adjustments will be made to shares reserved/issued under the plan and to outstanding PSUs.

nodes.title: No Ownership Rights/Other Limitations
nodes.heading: 39.15.3 No Ownership Rights/Other Limitations
nodes.start_phrase: PSUs do not convey the rights of ownership of Common Stock and do not carry voting rights.
nodes.summary:
- Tax withholding: The firm may satisfy withholding and related tax obligations by selling vested shares, withholding from cash compensation as required by law, or retaining vested shares until you pay taxes to the authorities.
- Right to set off: Subject to applicable law (including Section 409A), the firm may retain funds or shares from vesting to satisfy debts you owe the firm. It will not recoup from funds or unrestricted securities held in your name at the firm without your consent, except for accounts established under the stock plan as described below.
- No ownership rights: PSUs do not confer ownership or voting rights. No shares are issued until PSUs are determined and vest. You authorize the firm to open a brokerage or book-entry account to deliver vested shares. PSUs may be canceled in whole or part if cancellation provisions apply during a vesting suspension.
- Post-vesting share restrictions: As of any vesting date, the firm may restrict sale, transfer, pledging, assignment, hedging, or encumbrance of issued shares for a specified period. These restrictions do not affect voting or dividend rights. If recovery provisions apply during such period, you may be required to repay up to the fair market value of the gross restricted shares, despite the set-off limitation.
- Binding agreement: The Award Agreement binds JPMorgan Chase’s successors.
- No employment contract: Employment remains at-will. The award does not guarantee continued employment, similar future awards, or severance treatment.
- Section 409A compliance: The award is intended to comply with Section 409A. For specified employees who separate from service, deliveries that would occur within six months are delayed until the first month after six full months. Additional payment timing rules apply when amounts are no longer subject to a substantial risk of forfeiture.
- Corporate adjustments: In the event of stock splits/dividends (other than regular cash dividends), recapitalizations, new classes of stock, mergers, spin-offs, combinations, exchanges, or similar events, equitable adjustments will be made to outstanding PSUs and shares reserved/issued under the plan.

nodes.title: Binding Agreement
nodes.heading: 39.15.4 Binding Agreement
nodes.start_phrase: The Award Agreement will be binding upon any successor in interest to JPMorgan Chase, by merger or otherwise.
nodes.summary:
- Tax withholding and settlement: The firm may satisfy tax obligations from vested shares via market sale of shares, required cash compensation withholding, or by retaining vested shares until you pay taxes directly to authorities.
- Right to set off: Subject to law (including Section 409A), the firm may retain funds or shares resulting from vesting to satisfy debts you owe to the firm. It will not recover from your unrestricted funds or securities held at the firm without your consent, except for certain accounts referenced under “No Ownership Rights/Other Limitations.”
- No ownership rights before vesting: PSUs do not confer ownership or voting rights. Shares of Common Stock are issued only after PSUs are determined and vest. The firm may establish a brokerage or book-entry account in your name to deliver vested shares.
- Suspension and cancellation: Vesting may be suspended and PSUs may be canceled under provisions related to protection-based vesting, bonus recoupment, termination of employment, remedies, and amendments permitting suspension.
- Post-vesting restrictions: On any vesting date, the firm may restrict sale, transfer, pledging, assignment, hedging, or encumbrance of issued shares for a specified period. Voting and dividend rights on such restricted shares remain. You may be required to repay up to the fair market value of restricted shares if recovery provisions apply, notwithstanding general set-off limits.
- Binding effect: The Award Agreement binds successors to JPMorgan Chase.
- Employment at will: The award does not create a contract of employment, does not guarantee future awards, and is not considered compensation for severance purposes.
- Section 409A compliance: The award intends to comply with Section 409A. For specified employees who separate from service, delivery of deferred-compensation shares triggered within six months post-separation will be delayed until the first calendar month after six full months. If no substantial risk of forfeiture remains, the remainder of each calendar year after the vesting date is a payment date for distributing vested portions.
- Corporate adjustments: In the event of stock splits, dividends, recapitalizations, mergers, spin-offs, or similar events, equitable adjustments may be made to outstanding PSUs and shares reserved under the plan.

nodes.title: Not a Contract of Employment
nodes.heading: 39.15.5 Not a Contract of Employment
nodes.start_phrase: Nothing contained in the Award Agreement constitutes a contract of employment or continued employment.
nodes.summary:
- Tax withholding and settlement: The firm may satisfy tax obligations from vested shares by selling a portion of shares, withholding from cash compensation, or retaining shares until you directly pay taxes to authorities.
- Right to set off: Subject to applicable law (including Section 409A), the firm may retain funds or shares from vesting to satisfy debts you owe to the firm. It will not recoup from your funds or unrestricted securities held at the firm without your consent, except for certain stock-plan-related accounts described below.
- No ownership rights before vesting: PSUs do not convey ownership or voting rights until they vest and shares are issued. Shares will be issued via a firm-established brokerage or book-entry account in your name. PSUs may be cancelled if specified cancellation provisions apply during any suspension of vesting.
- Post-vesting share restrictions: On any vesting date, the firm may restrict transfer, sale, pledge, assignment, hedging, or encumbrance of issued shares for a period it specifies; voting and dividend rights during this period are unaffected. If recovery provisions apply, you may have to repay up to the fair market value of the gross restricted shares, notwithstanding certain set-off limits.

- Binding on successors: The Award Agreement binds any successor to JPMorgan Chase.

- Section 409A compliance: The award is intended to comply with Section 409A and will be interpreted accordingly. If you are a “specified employee” who separates from service and the award constitutes deferred compensation, share delivery triggered within six months post-separation will be delayed until after six full months. If no substantial risk of forfeiture applies, the remainder of each calendar year following the vesting date is a payment window for distribution of vested portions.
- Adjustments for corporate actions: In the event of stock splits, dividends (other than regular cash), recapitalizations, mergers, spin-offs, new classes of stock, combinations, exchanges, or similar events, equitable adjustments will be made to plan share reserves and outstanding PSUs.

nodes.title: Section 409A Compliance
nodes.heading: 39.15.6 Section 409A Compliance
nodes.start_phrase: To the extent that Section 409A of the Code is applicable to this award, distributions of shares hereunder are intended to comply with Section 409A of the Code, and the Award Agreement, including these terms and conditions, shall be interpreted in a manner consistent with such intent.

- Right to set off: Subject to applicable law (including Section 409A), the firm may retain funds or shares from vesting to cover debts you owe the firm; it will not recover amounts from your funds or unrestricted securities held at the firm without your consent, except for certain accounts referenced under “No Ownership Rights/Other Limitations.”
- No ownership rights before vesting: PSUs do not confer stock ownership or voting rights. Shares are issued only after PSUs are determined and vest, following JPMorgan Chase’s issuance procedures.

PSUs may be canceled if cancellation provisions apply during any suspension of vesting (as referenced in Protection-Based Vesting, Bonus Recoupment, Termination of Employment, Remedies, and Amendment).

If recovery provisions apply during that period, you may owe the firm up to the fair market value of the gross restricted shares, notwithstanding set-off limits.

- No employment contract: Employment remains at-will; the award does not guarantee continued employment, future awards, or count as compensation for severance.
- Section 409A compliance: The award is intended to comply with Section 409A. - Employment at will; no entitlement: The award does not create an employment contract; employment remains at-will. There is no right to future awards, and the award’s value is not included for severance purposes.
- Section 409A compliance: The award is intended to comply with Section 409A. If you are a specified employee who separates from service and the award constitutes deferred compensation payable within six months due to separation, delivery is delayed until the first month after six full months post-separation.   - Cause: Termination for specified misconduct or performance failures, including legal/regulatory violations, felony indictment/conviction, fraud, policy/Code of Conduct violations (other than immaterial/inadvertent), grossly inadequate performance or refusal to follow directives, or acts harmful to the Firm or its relationships.
  - Financial Services Company: A business engaging in specified financial services directly or via affiliates/subsidiaries (definition continues beyond the excerpt).

nodes.title: Definitions
nodes.heading: 39.27 Definitions
nodes.start_phrase: “Average Tangible Common Equity” means annual average common stockholders’ equity less annual average goodwill and annual average identifiable intangible assets.
nodes.summary:
- Authorization revocation: You may terminate the prior authorization at any time (except for tax/regulatory reporting and the Firm’s legal/regulatory obligations); doing so cancels the award.
- Governing law and forum: New York law governs. The Firm may elect American Arbitration Association arbitration for disputes; if not arbitrated, exclusive venue is the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York. You waive objections to personal jurisdiction/venue and agree not to file elsewhere.
- Waivers: You waive the right to a jury trial and to bring or participate in class, collective, or representative actions; claims must be pursued individually.
- Litigation costs: In Firm-initiated actions to enforce award terms where the Firm prevails, it may recover reasonable attorneys’ fees and expenses; you waive advancement of fees and indemnification under Firm By-Laws in such suits.
- Non-transferability: Awards and related rights cannot be assigned, pledged, transferred, hedged, hypothecated, or liened; transfer allowed only upon death via will, descent, or valid beneficiary designation.
- Key definitions and payout mechanics:
  - Average Tangible Common Equity; Firm Reported ROTCE; ROTCE methodology and restatement adjustments.
  - Target Award Number; Award Payout Percentage; Calculated PSUs determined by Target Award Number times Award Payout Percentage based on the Firm’s relative Performance Ranking and subject to absolute ROTCE floors/caps (placeholders to be specified).
  - Performance Period of three specified calendar years; Performance Companies peer set with Committee authority to make prospective adjustments for mergers, spin-offs, or failures.
  - Performance Ranking and Performance Table mapping average ROTCE and relative rank to payout percentages, including tie-breaking rules.
  - Firmwide Financial Threshold (cumulative ROTCE over the three-year period; placeholder percentages/years).
  - Calculation Agent: independent third party.
  - Cause: detailed grounds including legal/regulatory violations, felony indictment/conviction, fraud, policy/code violations, grossly inadequate performance or disobedience, and injurious acts.
  - Financial Services Company: broad definition covering banking, insurance, advisory, trading/market-making, fintech, private equity/real estate activities, and similar services.
  - Line of Business definitions and Line of Business Financial Thresholds: triggers tied to annual negative pre-tax pre-provision income or pre-loan loss reserve income for specified units; Corporate Functions treated as one line; certain CIB product-level revenue thresholds (excluding XVA).
  - Not-for-Profit Organization (U.S. 501(c)(3) or foreign equivalents) and Recognized Service.
- Government Office Requirements:
  - Potential continued vesting if you resign to accept or campaign full-time for a Government Office; inapplicable if you already meet Full Career Eligibility at termination.
  - Conditions include at least 60 days’ advance written notice, cooperation during the notice period, and no services for another employer during that time; the Firm may shorten the notice period at its discretion.

nodes.title: Government Office Requirements
nodes.heading: 39.28 Government Office Requirements
nodes.start_phrase: You may be eligible to continue vesting in all or part of your award if you voluntarily resign to accept a Government Office (as defined above) or to become a candidate for an elective Government Office.
nodes.summary:
- Defines key terms for a performance share unit (PSU) award program tied to relative ROTCE performance.
- Performance Companies: peer institutions with business activities overlapping the Firm’s revenue mix; the Committee may prospectively adjust the peer list for mergers, spin‑offs, business mix changes, bankruptcies, sales, or similar events, including adding acquirers or new companies.
- Performance Period: three specified calendar years.
- ROTCE: calculated annually as earnings from continuing operations minus preferred dividends divided by Average Tangible Common Equity; subject to recalculation if financial statements are restated; used solely for Performance Ranking.
- Performance Ranking: Firm’s average ROTCE ranked against the average ROTCE of the Performance Companies per a footnote to the Performance Table.
- Performance Table: sets Award Payout Percentages based on Firm-reported average ROTCE and relative ranking; includes a detailed schedule assigning specific payout percentages to each ranking position; tie-handling rules specify ties are disregarded for payout determination, with examples for ties involving the Firm and among Performance Companies.
- Recognized Service: follows the Firm’s service-related policies.
- Target Award Number: the number of PSUs specified in the Award Agreement.
- Government Office Requirements: potential eligibility to continue vesting if voluntarily resigning to accept or run for an elective Government Office, contingent on:
  - Not qualifying for Full Career Eligibility (if you do, this section does not apply).
  - Providing at least 60 days’ advance written notice and performing requested services cooperatively and professionally during the notice period without working for another employer; the Firm may shorten the notice period at its discretion.

nodes.title: Full Career Eligibility
nodes.heading: 39.28.1 Full Career Eligibility
nodes.start_phrase: “Government Office Requirements ” does not apply to you if you satisfy the subsection captioned “--Full Career Eligibility” as of the date that you voluntarily terminate your employment with the Firm.
nodes.summary:
- Defines “Performance Companies” as peer institutions with revenue mixes overlapping the firm’s, and allows the committee to adjust the peer list prospectively for mergers, spin‑offs, bankruptcies, sales, or other material business changes (including adding acquirers).
- Sets the “Performance Period” as three specified calendar years.
- Establishes “Performance Ranking” based on the firm’s average ROTCE versus the peers’ average ROTCE, tied to a “Performance Table” that maps relative rankings/ROTCE to Award Payout Percentages.
- Provides tie‑breaking rules for rankings, stating that ties are disregarded in determining payout, with examples for how ties between the firm and peers, and among peers, are treated.
- Defines “Recognized Service” per the firm’s service‑related policies.
- Defines “ROTCE” (earnings from continuing operations less preferred dividends divided by Average Tangible Common Equity for each year) and requires recalculation and adjusted rankings if the firm or a peer restates financials within the vesting period; this calculation is solely for determining Performance Ranking.
- Defines “Target Award Number” for PSUs as specified in the Award Agreement.
- Outlines Government Office Requirements: potential eligibility to continue vesting if voluntarily resigning to accept or run for elective Government Office, unless the individual already meets Full Career Eligibility.
- States eligibility conditions for continued vesting upon Government Office resignation, including at least 60 days’ advance written notice, performing requested services cooperatively during the notice period, refraining from working for another employer during that time, and the firm’s discretion to shorten the notice period.

nodes.title: Eligibility
nodes.heading: 39.28.2 Eligibility
nodes.start_phrase: Eligibility for continued vesting is conditioned on your providing the Firm:
nodes.summary:
- Defines key terms for a PSU (Performance Share Unit) award tied to relative ROTCE performance: Performance Companies, Performance Period, Performance Ranking, Performance Table, Recognized Service, ROTCE, and Target Award Number.
- Performance Companies: peer institutions with materially similar revenue mix; Committee may prospectively remove, replace, or adjust peers after mergers, spin‑offs, bankruptcies, sales, or material business changes (including adding acquirers/new companies).
- Performance Period: three specified calendar years.
- ROTCE: calculated annually as earnings from continuing operations minus preferred dividends divided by Average Tangible Common Equity; if financials are restated, ROTCE and rankings are recalculated solely for award purposes.
- Performance Ranking and Performance Table: award payouts are determined by the Firm’s average ROTCE ranking versus peers according to a predefined payout scale; a detailed rank-to-payout mapping applies; tie-handling rules favor treating tied rankings as satisfied without penalizing the Firm and adjust peer rankings accordingly.
- Target Award Number: the number of PSUs designated in the Award Agreement.
- Recognized Service: employee service period per Firm policy, used in vesting determinations.
- Government Office Requirements: outlines eligibility for continued vesting if an employee resigns to accept or run for a Government Office, unless the employee already meets Full Career Eligibility.
- Eligibility conditions for continued vesting: at least 60 days’ advance written notice while continuing to serve the Firm and not another employer (Firm may shorten notice), confirmation of legal compliance, and documentation of government service/candidacy purpose.
- Portion eligible for continued vesting (CV Award) based on continuous service at termination: 50% (3–<4 years), 75% (4–<5 years), 100% (≥5 years); the remainder is canceled at termination.
- Conditions to receive CV Award: hold a non‑elective Government Office for ≥2 years (or have a vesting date occur during a shorter government service), or for elective office, have name on the primary or final ballot; performance and protection‑based vesting conditions continue to apply.
- Satisfaction of conditions: upon meeting them (including unsuccessful election after appearing on a ballot), outstanding and previously accelerated awards resume standard vesting terms and employment restrictions as if Full Career Eligibility had been met.
- Failure to satisfy conditions: CV Award PSUs are canceled; the participant must repay the Fair Market Value of shares previously accelerated that would otherwise have remained outstanding PSUs, valued as of distribution date.
- References an accelerated distribution mechanism for ethics/conflict reasons arising from government employment, with specifics cross‑referenced elsewhere in the agreement.

nodes.title: Portion of Your Award Subject to Continued Vesting
nodes.heading: 39.28.3 Portion of Your Award Subject to Continued Vesting
nodes.start_phrase: Subject to the conditions below, the percentage of this award that will continue to vest in accordance with this award’s original schedule will be based on your years of continuous service completed with the Firm immediately preceding your termination date, as follows:
nodes.summary:
Summary of main points:
- Purpose: Outlines when a portion of a performance share unit (PSU) award will continue to vest if an employee resigns to accept or campaign for a Government Office.
- Required documentation: (1) Confirmation that continued vesting complies with applicable laws/regulations; (2) Proof the resignation is to accept or run for a Government Office.
- Portion eligible for continued vesting (CV Award): Based on continuous service at termination—50% (≥3 to <4 years), 75% (≥4 to <5 years), 100% (≥5 years); the remainder is cancelled at termination.
- Conditions to receive CV Award: (a) Serve in a non-elective Government Office for at least two years after termination (or have a vesting date occur during a shorter non-elective term), or (b) for elective roles, have your name on the primary or final public ballot.
- Ongoing requirements: Original performance and protection-based vesting criteria still apply to the CV Award.
- If conditions are satisfied: Outstanding CV Awards (and those previously accelerated for ethics/conflict reasons) continue under the Award Agreement for the remaining vesting period as if the employee met Full Career Eligibility, including employment restrictions.
- If conditions are not met: Outstanding CV Award PSUs are cancelled, and the employee must repay the fair market value of any shares previously distributed early due to ethics/conflict-related accelerated distribution.

nodes.title: Conditions for Continued Vesting of Award
nodes.heading: 39.28.4 Conditions for Continued Vesting of Award
nodes.start_phrase: You must remain in a non-elective Government Office for two or more years after your employment with the Firm terminates to be eligible to receive the CV Award; provided that if your non-elective Government Office is for a period less than two years, you will be eligible to receive the CV Award if it has a vesting date during your period of Government Service; or
nodes.summary:
- Sets documentation requirements: confirmation that continued vesting complies with applicable laws and proof that resignation is to accept or run for a Government Office.
- Defines portion of award eligible for continued vesting (CV Award) based on continuous service at termination: 50% (3–<4 years), 75% (4–<5 years), 100% (5+ years); non-eligible portion is cancelled at termination.
- Conditions for CV Award:
  - Non-elective Government Office: must serve at least two years post-termination; if the office term is under two years, eligibility applies only to tranches vesting during the government service.
  - Elective office candidacy: name must appear on the primary or final public ballot; if not elected, employment restrictions apply.
- Confirms that performance and protection-based vesting criteria continue to apply to the CV Award.
- Upon satisfying conditions (including unsuccessful election after appearing on a ballot), any then-outstanding CV Awards and awards that would have been outstanding but for accelerated distribution remain subject to the Award Agreement terms and employment restrictions as if the employee had Full Career Eligibility.
- Failure to satisfy conditions results in cancellation of outstanding PSUs under the CV Award and a clawback: repayment of the fair market value of shares previously distributed via accelerated distribution that would have remained outstanding PSUs, valued as of the distribution date.
- References accelerated distribution mechanisms for ethics or conflict reasons arising from government employment and reiterates ongoing employment restrictions during the remaining vesting period.

nodes.title: Satisfaction of Conditions
nodes.heading: 39.28.5 Satisfaction of Conditions
nodes.start_phrase: If your service in a Government Office ends two years or more after your employment with the Firm terminates, or in the case of resignation from the Firm to campaign for a Government Office,
nodes.summary:
- Scope: Explains how a performance share/unit award may continue to vest when an employee resigns to accept or campaign for a Government Office.
- Required documentation: (1) Confirmation acceptable to the Firm that continued vesting would not violate any law, regulation, or rule; and (2) proof acceptable to the Firm that the resignation is to accept a Government Office or to become a candidate.
- Portion eligible for continued vesting (the “CV Award”): Based on continuous service at termination—50% (3 to <4 years), 75% (4 to <5 years), 100% (5+ years). The non-eligible portion is canceled at termination.
- Conditions to receive the CV Award:
  - Service in a non-elective Government Office for at least two years after termination; if the office term is under two years, eligibility applies if a vesting date occurs during the government service; or
  - For elective office, the individual’s name must appear on the primary or final public ballot.
  - Performance and protection-based vesting criteria continue to apply to the CV Award.
- Satisfaction of conditions: If government service ends at or after two years, or the individual runs, appears on a ballot, and is not elected, then any then-outstanding CV Awards and any awards otherwise outstanding but for an accelerated distribution due to ethics/conflict from government employment will continue for the remaining vesting period under the same terms as a resignation with Full Career Eligibility, including employment restrictions.
- Failure to satisfy conditions: All outstanding PSUs under the CV Award are canceled. The individual must repay the fair market value (pre-withholding) of any shares previously distributed via accelerated distribution that would otherwise have remained outstanding as PSUs on the failure date, with fair market value measured as of the distribution date.

nodes.title: Failure to Satisfy Conditions
nodes.heading: 39.28.6 Failure to Satisfy Conditions
nodes.start_phrase: If you do not satisfy the above “Conditions for Continued Vesting of Awards”, any outstanding PSUs under the CV Award will be cancelled.
nodes.summary:
- Purpose: Outlines when and how equity awards (PSUs) may continue to vest if an employee resigns to accept or run for a Government Office.
- Required documentation: Confirmation acceptable to the Firm that continued vesting is lawful; proof that resignation is to accept a Government Office or to become a candidate (per Definitions).
- Portion eligible for continued vesting (CV Award): Based on continuous service with the Firm immediately before termination—50% (3–<4 years), 75% (4–<5 years), 100% (≥5 years). The remainder is cancelled at termination.
- Conditions to receive CV Award:
  - Non-elective office: Must serve 2+ years after leaving the Firm; if the term is under 2 years, eligibility applies if a vesting date occurs during the government service.
  - Elective office (campaign): Name must appear on the primary or final ballot. Notes that employment restrictions apply if not elected.
- Ongoing requirements: Performance and protection-based vesting conditions continue to apply to the CV Award.
- If conditions are satisfied: Any outstanding CV Awards (and awards that would have been outstanding but for an accelerated distribution due to ethics/conflict rules) remain subject to the Award Agreement’s terms for the rest of the vesting period, including employment restrictions, as if the employee had Full Career Eligibility.
- If conditions are not satisfied: Outstanding PSUs under the CV Award are cancelled; the employee must repay the fair market value of previously distributed shares that would have remained outstanding PSUs but for accelerated distribution tied to government ethics/conflict reasons.
