nodes.title: Calculation of Performance Ranking
nodes.heading: 40.5 Calculation of Performance Ranking
nodes.start_phrase: For purposes of the Performance Ranking, the ranking of the Firm and of each Performance Company for the Performance Period shall be determined and calculated by the Calculation Agent, using the definitions of “Average Tangible Common Equity” (if otherwise applicable), “Calculated PSUs”, “Firm Reported ROTCE”, “Performance Table” (including its footnote) and “ROTCE” as set forth in the “Definitions ” section of these terms and conditions.
nodes.summary:
- Outlines how Performance Ranking is determined by a Calculation Agent using defined terms (Average Tangible Common Equity, Calculated PSUs, Firm Reported ROTCE, Performance Table and footnote, ROTCE). Results (except Firm Reported ROTCE) are rounded to the nearest hundredth and are binding; tie rules per the Performance Table.
- Establishes a Capital Ratio Performance Threshold: if the Firm’s CET1 ratio falls below a set percentage at any year-end during the Performance Period, up to one-third of the Target Award PSUs may be reduced by the CMDC for each such year.
- Details a Qualitative Performance assessment conducted annually across four dimensions (Client/Customer Focus; Risk, Controls & Conduct; Teamwork & Leadership; Business Results). “Meets” yields a 100% factor (no reduction for that year); “Not Meet” may lead to a reduction between 0% and 99%. A 0% factor for each year would cancel the award. The Committee may also assess performance over the full three-year period and apply a single factor to all PSUs; 0% cancels the award. Feedback from the Chair of the UK Remuneration Committee is considered for UK Senior Manager responsibilities. The factor applies only for periods of employment or as soon as administratively practical.
- Describes Protection-Based Vesting: awards are intended to vest if continuously employed or eligible under job elimination, full career, government office, or disability provisions, but remain subject to all terms (including PSU determination, capital ratio threshold, recapture, and remedies). Up to 50% of otherwise distributable PSUs (“At Risk PSUs”) may be cancelled at the CEO’s discretion based on: sustained underperformance by the individual or Firm (considering net income, revenue, EPS, capital ratios, and peer comparisons); negative Firm-level annual pre-tax pre-provision income; cancellation of RSUs in a Line of Business under the individual’s responsibility due to missing its financial threshold; or failure to meet the Firmwide Financial Threshold.

nodes.title: Capital Ratio Performance Threshold
nodes.heading: 40.6 Capital Ratio Performance Threshold
nodes.start_phrase: Unvested PSUs are subject to reduction if the Firm’s Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) capital ratio at any year end falls below a predetermined threshold of ________%.
nodes.summary:
- Performance Ranking methodology: A Calculation Agent determines firm and peer rankings for the Performance Period using defined terms (Average Tangible Common Equity, Calculated PSUs, Firm Reported ROTCE, Performance Table and footnote, ROTCE). Results (except Firm Reported ROTCE) are rounded to the nearest hundredth (xx.yy%). Tie-breaking follows the Performance Table. All calculations are final and binding.
- Capital Ratio Performance Threshold: If the firm’s CET1 ratio is below a preset threshold at any year-end, up to one-third of the Target Award PSUs can be reduced by the CMDC for each such year.
- Qualitative Performance Factor: Annually, the Committee assesses performance across four categories—Client/Customer Focus; Risk, Controls & Conduct; Teamwork & Leadership; Business Results. “Meets” expectations yields a 100% factor (no reduction for that year’s one-third of Target PSUs). “Not Meet” can trigger a 0–99% factor and corresponding reduction; a 0% factor each year cancels the award. The Committee may alternatively assess performance over the full three-year period and apply one factor to all PSUs; a 0% factor cancels the award. Input is sought from the UK Remuneration Committee Chair regarding UK Senior Manager regulatory responsibilities. The factor is applied only for periods of employment or as soon as administratively practical.
- Protection-based vesting: Awards are intended to vest on scheduled dates if the employee remains employed or qualifies under Job Elimination, Full Career Eligibility, Government Office, or Disability, but are subject to all terms (including PSU determination at period end, Capital Ratio Threshold, Recapture, Remedies, and the protection-based provision). Up to 50% of otherwise distributable PSUs at any vesting date (“At Risk PSUs”) may be cancelled at the CEO’s discretion based on: sustained underperformance versus role or Firm/Operating Committee priorities (considering metrics such as net income, total net revenue, EPS, and capital ratios, absolute and relative to peers); negative Firm-level annual pre-tax pre-provision income; cancellation of RSUs in a Line of Business under the employee’s responsibility for missing its LOB Financial Threshold; or failure to meet the Firmwide Financial Threshold.

nodes.title: Qualitative Performance
nodes.heading: 40.7 Qualitative Performance
nodes.start_phrase: Determination of Qualitative Performance Factor.
nodes.summary:
- Performance Ranking methodology: A Calculation Agent determines the Firm and each Performance Company’s ranking for the Performance Period using defined terms (Average Tangible Common Equity, Calculated PSUs, Firm Reported ROTCE, Performance Table and footnote, ROTCE) from the Definitions section. Calculations (except Firm Reported ROTCE) are shown to two decimal places (xx.yy%), rounded to the nearest hundredth. Tie-breaking follows the “Definitions—Performance Table.” All performance calculations are binding and conclusive.
- Capital Ratio Performance Threshold: Unvested PSUs may be reduced if the Firm’s CET1 ratio falls below a preset year-end threshold. For each year below the threshold during the Performance Period, up to one-third of the Target Award PSUs may be reduced by the CMDC.
- Qualitative Performance Factor: Annually assessed across four categories—Client/Customer Focus; Risk, Controls & Conduct; Teamwork & Leadership; Business Results. “Meets” expectations = 100% factor (no downward adjustment) for that year; “Not Meet” may trigger a downward adjustment to 0–99%. A 0% factor for each year would cancel the award (no shares vest). The Committee may alternatively assess qualitative performance over the entire three-year Performance Period and apply one factor to the total PSUs determined under “Number of Performance Share Units at End of the Performance Period”; a 0% factor cancels the award. Assessment incorporates feedback from the Chair of the UK Remuneration Committee for Senior Manager responsibilities in CIB UK-regulated entities. The factor applies only for periods of employment (or as soon as administratively practical).
- Protection-based vesting and potential cancellation: Awards are intended to vest on scheduled dates if continuously employed or if eligible under Job Elimination, Full Career Eligibility, Government Office, or Disability. Vesting and PSU amounts remain subject to these terms, including “Number of PSUs at End of Performance Period,” “Capital Ratio Performance Threshold,” “Recapture Provisions,” and “Remedies.” Up to 50% of otherwise distributable PSUs at a vesting date (“At Risk PSUs”) may be cancelled at the CEO’s sole discretion based on: (1) sustained unsatisfactory performance by you or the Firm against stated priorities (considering metrics such as net income, total net revenue, EPS, and capital ratios, absolute and relative to peers); (2) negative Firm-level annual pre-tax pre-provision income; (3) cancellation of RSUs in a Line of Business you oversee due to failure to meet its LOB Financial Threshold; or (4) failure to meet the Firmwide Financial Threshold.

nodes.title: Protection-Based Vesting
nodes.heading: 40.8 Protection-Based Vesting
nodes.start_phrase: This award is intended and expected to vest on each vesting date set forth in your Award Agreement, provided that you are continuously employed by the Firm through such vesting date, or you meet the requirements for continued vesting described under the subsections “--Job Elimination”, “--Full Career Eligibility”, “--Government Office” or “--Disability”.
nodes.summary:
- Establishes how Performance Ranking is calculated by the Calculation Agent using defined terms (Average Tangible Common Equity, Calculated PSUs, Firm Reported ROTCE, Performance Table, ROTCE); results (other than Firm Reported ROTCE) rounded to two decimal places; tie-breaking per the Performance Table; calculations are binding and conclusive.
- Capital Ratio Performance Threshold: If the Firm’s CET1 ratio falls below a preset threshold at any year-end during the Performance Period, up to one‑third of the Target Award PSUs may be reduced by the CMDC for each such year.
- Qualitative Performance Factor: Annual Committee assessment across four categories (Client/Customer Focus; Risk, Controls & Conduct; Teamwork & Leadership; Business Results). “Meets” = 100% (no reduction) for that year’s one‑third tranche; “Not Meet” may reduce that tranche to 0–99%. A 0% each year cancels the award. Committee may alternatively assess performance over the full three‑year period and apply one factor to all PSUs determined at period end; a 0% cancels the award. Assessment includes UK Senior Manager responsibilities feedback; factor applies only for periods of employment (or as soon as administratively practical).
- Protection-Based Vesting: Up to 50% of PSUs otherwise distributable at any vest date (At Risk PSUs) may be cancelled at the CEO’s discretion based on factors including: sustained underperformance versus priorities (e.g., net income, revenue, EPS, capital ratios), negative Firm-level pre‑tax pre‑provision income, Line of Business failing its Financial Threshold (triggering RSU cancellations), or failure to meet the Firmwide Financial Threshold. Cancellations can occur before the Performance Period ends, up to 50% of Target PSUs. These cancellation conditions continue to apply after certain qualifying terminations. Determinations require CMDC ratification; for any CEO award, CMDC decides and the Board ratifies.
- Bonus Recoupment: Award and related cash incentive are subject to the JPMorgan Chase Bonus Recoupment Policy as amended from time to time; Firm’s rights under the policy are unaffected by these terms.
- EMEA Malus and Clawback Policy (Identified Staff): Award and related cash incentive are subject to this policy (and any supplements), enabling malus/clawback to meet regulatory obligations, including in cases of material Firm performance downturn or increased capital requirements; these circumstances align with broader Firm terms such as Bonus Recoupment and Protection-Based Vesting.
- Termination of Employment: Award cancels upon termination unless specific exceptions apply (Job Elimination, Full Career Eligibility, Government Office, Disability, or Death). Continued vesting eligibility after termination is subject to all terms (including Protection-Based Vesting, Recoupment, Malus/Clawback, obligations, remedies). For Job Elimination, continued vesting requires HR determination that the job was eliminated, cooperative/professional transition services, and satisfaction of release/certification requirements. The Full Career Eligibility section begins but is not fully included in this excerpt.

nodes.title: Bonus Recoupment
nodes.heading: 40.9 Bonus Recoupment
nodes.start_phrase: In consideration of the grant of this award, you agree that you are subject to the JPMorgan Chase Bonus Recoupment Policy (or successor policy) as in effect from time to time as it applies both to the cash incentive compensation awarded to you for performance year 20____ and to this award.
nodes.summary:
- At Risk PSUs may be canceled, in whole or part, before the end of the Performance Period based on specified factors, with a pre-period cancellation cap of up to 50% of the Target Award Number.
- If employment ends due to Job Elimination, Full Career Eligibility, Government Office, or Disability (including potential acceleration for Government Office), the same cancellation rules continue to apply during post-termination vesting.
- Any protection-based vesting determinations require ratification by JPMorgan Chase’s Compensation and Management Development Committee; for current or former CEOs, determinations are made by the Committee and ratified by the Board.
- The award and the related cash incentive are subject to the JPMorgan Chase Bonus Recoupment Policy; nothing in the terms limits the Firm’s rights under that policy.
- Identified Staff are also subject to the JPMorgan Chase EMEA Malus and Clawback Policy (and any supplements), allowing reduction or recovery of awards in circumstances such as a material downturn in Firm performance or increased capital requirements; these circumstances align with the Firm’s broader Bonus Recoupment and Protection-Based Vesting provisions.
- Upon termination of employment, the award is generally canceled unless the termination qualifies under Job Elimination, Full Career Eligibility, Government Office, Disability, or Death, in which case continued vesting may apply subject to all terms (including Protection-Based Vesting, Recoupment, EMEA Malus/Clawback, Your Obligations, and Remedies).
- For continued vesting under Job Elimination: HR (or nominee) must determine the job was eliminated, the employee cooperated and provided requested services professionally after notice, and the employee met specified Release/Certification requirements.
- The Full Career Eligibility section begins but is not fully included in this excerpt.

nodes.title: EMEA Malus and Clawback Policy - Identified Staff
nodes.heading: 40.10 EMEA Malus and Clawback Policy - Identified Staff
nodes.start_phrase: In consideration of grant of this award, and without prejudice to any other provision of this Award Agreement, you agree that you are subject to the JPMorgan Chase EMEA Malus and Clawback Policy - Identified Staff (and any applicable supplement(s) to that policy) or successor policy as in effect from time to time as it applies both to the cash incentive compensation awarded to you for performance year ______ and to this award.
nodes.summary:
- Up to 50% of At Risk PSUs may be canceled before the end of the Performance Period based on specified factors; these cancellation conditions continue to apply even if the participant becomes entitled to continued vesting or potential acceleration due to Job Elimination, Full Career Eligibility, Government Office, or Disability.
- Any determinations related to protection-based vesting require ratification by JPMorgan Chase’s Compensation and Management Development Committee; for current or former CEOs, the Committee makes determinations which are then ratified by the Board.
- The award and the cash incentive for the relevant performance year are subject to the JPMorgan Chase Bonus Recoupment Policy, and nothing in the award terms limits the Firm’s rights under that policy.
- Identified Staff are also subject to the JPMorgan Chase EMEA Malus and Clawback Policy (and any supplements), which allows reduction or recovery of awards in circumstances such as material downturn in Firm performance or increased capital requirements; these circumstances align with existing Firmwide terms like the Bonus Recoupment Policy and Protection-Based Vesting.
- Upon termination of employment, the award is generally canceled effective on the termination date, except under specified cases (Job Elimination, Full Career Eligibility, Government Office, Disability, or Death), in which continued vesting may occur subject to all applicable terms (including Protection-Based Vesting, Bonus Recoupment, EMEA Malus and Clawback, Your Obligations, and Remedies).
- For continued vesting due to Job Elimination, the HR Director (or nominee) must determine that the job was eliminated, the participant cooperated professionally after notice as requested, and the Release/Certification Requirements were satisfied.

nodes.title: Termination of Employment
nodes.heading: 40.11 Termination of Employment
nodes.start_phrase: Except as explicitly set forth below under the subsections captioned “--Job Elimination”, “--Full Career Eligibility”, “--Government Office” or “--Disability” or under the section captioned “ Death ”, this award will be cancelled in full effective on the date your employment with the Firm terminates for any reason.
nodes.summary:
- Clarifies that up to 50% of At Risk PSUs (relative to the Target Award Number) may be cancelled before the end of the Performance Period based on specified factors, and such cancellation rules continue to apply even if vesting continues after certain qualifying terminations.
- States that protection-based vesting determinations are subject to ratification by JPMorgan Chase’s Compensation and Management Development Committee; for current or former CEOs, the Committee makes determinations subject to Board ratification.
- Confirms the award and related cash incentive compensation are subject to the JPMorgan Chase Bonus Recoupment Policy, without limiting the Firm’s rights under that policy; provides a link to the governance page.
- Extends the JPMorgan Chase EMEA Malus and Clawback Policy – Identified Staff to the award and related cash incentives, enabling malus/clawback in circumstances such as material financial downturns or increased capital requirements; notes alignment with Firmwide Bonus Recoupment and Protection-Based Vesting provisions; provides access via My Rewards.
- Provides that, unless specified otherwise, the award is cancelled upon employment termination; outlines exceptions allowing continued vesting if conditions are met:
  - Job Elimination: Requires HR determination of role elimination, cooperative/professional services after notice, and satisfaction of release/certification requirements.
  - Full Career Eligibility: Requires voluntary termination; at least 5 years of continuous service; 15 years Recognized Service or 30 years combined Recognized Service plus external experience; 180 days advance written notice with cooperative service and no outside work; a pre-termination determination that continued vesting is appropriate; a 36-month post-grant restriction on working for a Financial Services Company or in the same profession (with exceptions for government, education, or not-for-profit); and satisfaction of release/certification requirements. The Firm may require service during the notice period or shorten it (not earlier than meeting service requirements). Additional local notice policies may apply.
  - Government Office: Voluntary termination to accept or run for a Government Office, subject to Government Office Requirements and definitions.
  - Disability: Termination due to qualifying LTD status (or equivalent/qualifying long-term disability as determined by the Firm or its designee), with written request for continued vesting within 30 days, supporting documentation, Firm’s written consent, and satisfaction of release/certification requirements.
- Details Release/Certification requirements: execution of a Firm-specified release of claims; for Full Career Eligibility, pre-termination confirmation of eligibility and written consent; for Full Career Eligibility and Government Office, ongoing certifications before each vesting date confirming compliance with employment restrictions; for Disability, required notices/documentation and consent; and compliance with all Award Agreement terms.
- Provides death provisions: if the participant dies while eligible to vest, the designated beneficiary (or estate if none/invalid) may receive the associated shares.

nodes.title: Release/Certification
nodes.heading: 40.12 Release/Certification
nodes.start_phrase: To qualify for continued vesting after termination of your employment under any of the foregoing circumstances:
nodes.summary:
- Outlines conditions for continued vesting after voluntary termination under “Full Career Eligibility,” including:
  - At least 5 years of continuous service immediately before termination.
  - Recognized Service of 15+ years, or combined Firm Recognized Service and external professional experience totaling 30+ years.
  - At least 180 days’ advance written notice, during which the employee must perform requested services cooperatively, refrain from working for any other employer, and comply with Firm direction; Firm may require service during the notice or shorten it (not earlier than meeting service requirements).
  - Firm’s prior determination that continued vesting is appropriate based on performance and conduct.
  - For 36 months from grant, no services in any capacity for a Financial Services Company or in the employee’s profession; work allowed for government, education, or Not-for-Profit organizations.
  - Satisfaction of Release/Certification requirements.
  - Additional notice period policies may apply.
- Provides a separate path for continued vesting upon voluntary termination to accept or run for a Government Office, subject to “Government Office Requirements” and defined terms.
- Details disability-related continued vesting if employment ends due to qualifying long-term disability under the Firm’s LTD Plan (or equivalent), or a disability that would qualify:
  - Employee must request continued vesting within 30 days of termination, provide documentation, and obtain the Firm’s written consent.
  - Must also satisfy Release/Certification requirements.
- Specifies Release/Certification Requirements:
  - Execute a Firm-specified release of claims.
  - For Full Career Eligibility: confirm eligibility with management in advance (including 180-day notice) and obtain written consent.
  - For Full Career Eligibility and Government Office: certify compliance with post-employment restrictions before each vesting date while restrictions apply.
  - For Disability: meet notice/documentation requirements and obtain written consent.
  - Comply with all other Award Agreement obligations (“Your Obligations”).
- Provides death provisions: if the employee dies while eligible to vest, the designated beneficiary (or estate, as applicable) may receive shares associated with the award.
- References definitions (e.g., Recognized Service, Financial Services Company, Not-for-Profit, Government Office) and related sections (Notice Period, Government Office Requirements, Your Obligations).

nodes.title: Death
nodes.heading: 40.13 Death
nodes.start_phrase: If you die while you are eligible to vest in this award, your designated beneficiary on file with the Firm’s Stock Administration Department (or your estate or if no beneficiary has been designated or survives you or if beneficiary designation is not recognized locally) may be entitled to receive a distribution of a number of shares of Common Stock associated with your award.
nodes.summary:
- Conditions for continued vesting after employment ends
  - Full Career Eligibility: requires at least 5 years of continuous service; 15+ years of Recognized Service or 30+ years combined Recognized Service and attested external professional experience; at least 180 days’ advance written notice; provision of services during the notice period without working for another employer; Firm’s prior determination that continued vesting is appropriate based on performance and conduct; and a 36‑month post‑grant restriction on working in financial services or in your profession (with exceptions for government, education, or not‑for‑profit roles). Release/Certification requirements apply. The Firm may require service during the notice period or shorten it (not earlier than meeting service requirements). Additional notice rules may apply under the Notice Period policy.
  - Government Office: eligibility to continue vesting if you resign to accept or run for an elective government office, subject to specific Government Office Requirements and definitions.
  - Disability: eligibility if employment ends due to long‑term disability qualifying under the LTD Plan or equivalent; must request continued vesting within 30 days, provide documentation, and receive the Firm’s written consent; Release/Certification requirements apply.

- Release/Certification requirements to qualify for continued vesting
  - Execute a Firm‑specified release of claims.
  - For Full Career Eligibility: confirm eligibility with management before termination (including 180‑day notice) and obtain written consent.
  - For Full Career Eligibility and Government Office: certify compliance with post‑employment restrictions prior to each vest date while restrictions apply.
  - For Disability: meet notice/documentation requirements and obtain written consent.
  - Comply with all other terms of the Award Agreement.

- Death provisions
  - If death occurs after the Performance Period, the beneficiary/estate receives shares equal to any outstanding PSUs.
  - If death occurs during the Performance Period, payout is based on average performance of completed calendar years, one‑third of target PSUs for each completed year, and 100% Award Payout Percentage for remaining years.
  - Distribution no later than the end of the calendar year following death (administrative practice targets registration within 60 days of receiving required documentation).

- Participant obligations tied to the award
  - Non‑Solicitation of Employees and Customers: for the longer of one year post‑termination or three years from grant date (if the award is not canceled), restrictions on soliciting/hiring Firm employees and soliciting/diverting Firm customers, with specified exceptions and alignment to applicable law.
  - Confidential Information: prohibition on using/disclosing Firm confidential information or communicating with media; no access to Firm systems post‑termination without authorization; whistleblower and legal/regulatory response carve‑outs per Code of Conduct and law.
  - Non‑Disparagement: prohibition on public statements that disparage the Firm or its stakeholders, with carve‑outs for lawful reporting and truthful regulatory/legal responses.
  - Cooperation: obligation to cooperate with the Firm and its counsel on matters such as audits, litigation, investigations, or governmental proceedings.

- Cross‑references and definitions noted
  - References to “Recognized Service,” “Financial Services Company,” “Not‑for‑Profit Organization,” “Government Office,” “Performance Period,” “Award Payout Percentage,” and the “Notice Period” policy, which are defined or detailed elsewhere in the full document.

nodes.title: Your Obligations
nodes.heading: 40.14 Your Obligations
nodes.start_phrase: In consideration of the grant of this award, you agree to comply with and be bound by the obligations set forth below next to the subsections captioned “--Non-Solicitation of Employees and Customers”, “--Confidential Information”, “--Non-Disparagement”, ”-- Cooperation”, “--Compliance with Award Agreement”, and “--Notice Period”.
nodes.summary:
- Death and PSU payout: If the participant dies after the Performance Period, the beneficiary receives shares equal to any outstanding PSUs. If death occurs during the Performance Period, payout is based on the average performance of completed calendar years, multiplied by one-third of the target PSUs for each completed year, and 100% payout is used for any remaining calendar years. Shares are distributed no later than the end of the calendar year following death; administratively, shares are typically registered to the beneficiary or estate within 60 days after required documentation is received.
- Acceptance obligations tied to the award include: Non-Solicitation, Confidentiality, Non-Disparagement, Cooperation, Compliance with Award Agreement, and Notice Period (the latter two referenced but not detailed here).
- Non-Solicitation: For the longer of (i) one year post-termination or (ii) three years from grant date if the award is not canceled at termination, the participant may not (without HR’s written consent) solicit or induce Firm employees to leave; hire Firm employees except in specified circumstances (job elimination or more than six months post-Firm employment); or, to the fullest extent enforceable, solicit or divert customers, suppliers, or other business contacts known through employment. Exceptions include publicly known institutional customers serviced without using Firm confidential information and authorized actions in the normal course of employment.
- Confidential Information: During and after employment, no use or disclosure of Firm confidential information and no media communications about Firm matters, except as permitted by the Code of Conduct, law, or legal process; no unauthorized post-termination access to internal systems. “Confidential information” is as defined in the Firm’s Code of Conduct. Whistleblowing and truthful responses to regulators/courts are expressly protected.
- Non-Disparagement: During and after employment, no public statements intended or reasonably foreseeable to disparage the Firm or its stakeholders, with carve-outs for lawful reporting and truthful cooperation with regulators or courts.
- Cooperation: Ongoing duty to cooperate fully and provide accurate information to the Firm and its counsel in audits, tax matters, litigation, investigations, or governmental proceedings (clause text is partially truncated).

nodes.title: Non-Solicitation of Employees and Customers
nodes.heading: 40.14.1 Non-Solicitation of Employees and Customers
nodes.start_phrase: During your employment by the Firm and for the longer of the (i) one year period following the termination of your employment or, (ii) if your award is not cancelled as of your termination date, the three year period from Grant Date, you will not directly or indirectly, whether on your own behalf or on behalf of any other party, without the prior written consent of the Director of Human Resources: (i) solicit, induce or encourage any of the Firm’s then current employees to leave the Firm or to apply for employment elsewhere, unless such current employee has received official, written notice that his or her employment will be terminated due to job elimination (ii) hire any employee or former employee who was employed by the Firm at the date your employment terminated, unless the individual’s employment terminated because his or her job was eliminated, or the individual’s employment with the Firm has been terminated for more than six months, (iii) to the fullest extent enforceable under applicable law, solicit or induce or attempt to induce to leave the Firm, or divert or attempt to divert from doing business with the Firm, any then current customers, suppliers or other persons or entities that were serviced by you or whose names became known to you by virtue of your employment with the Firm, or otherwise interfere with the relationship between the Firm and such customers, suppliers or other persons or entities.
nodes.summary:
- Death benefits for PSUs:
  - If death occurs after the Performance Period ends, the beneficiary receives shares equal to any outstanding PSUs.
  - If death occurs during the Performance Period, the beneficiary receives shares based on the average performance of completed calendar years, calculated as one-third of the Target Award per completed year, and assumes a 100% Award Payout Percentage for any remaining years.
  - Distribution timing: no later than the end of the calendar year following the year of death; administratively, shares are typically registered to the beneficiary or estate within 60 days after required documentation is received.

- Employee obligations tied to the award:
  - Non-solicitation of employees and customers:
    - Applies during employment and for the longer of one year post-termination or three years from Grant Date if the award isn’t cancelled at termination.
    - Prohibits soliciting or encouraging Firm employees to leave; hiring certain current/former employees (with exceptions for job eliminations or if more than six months have passed since termination); and, to the extent enforceable, soliciting or diverting customers/suppliers known or serviced through employment. Publicly known institutional customers may be serviced post-employment without using Firm confidential information.
    - Excludes authorized actions taken in the normal scope of employment.
  - Confidential information:
    - Prohibits using or disclosing Firm confidential information and communicating with media about Firm matters during and after employment, except as permitted by the Code of Conduct, policies, law, or legal process.
    - Post-termination, prohibits unauthorized access to internal Firm systems.
    - Allows reporting suspected legal or Code of Conduct violations to management, regulators, government, attorneys, or courts, and truthful responses to lawful inquiries.
  - Non-disparagement:
    - Prohibits making or encouraging public statements that disparage the Firm or its stakeholders during and after employment, with carve-outs for lawful reporting and truthful cooperation with authorities or legal processes.
  - Cooperation:
    - Requires full cooperation and accurate information provision to the Firm and its counsel in audits, tax matters, litigation, investigations, or governmental proceedings related to matters within the employee’s knowledge.

- The section also references obligations to comply with the Award Agreement and a Notice Period requirement (details not included in the excerpt).

nodes.title: Confidential Information
nodes.heading: 40.14.2 Confidential Information
nodes.start_phrase: You will not, either during your employment with the Firm or thereafter, directly or indirectly (i) use or disclose to anyone any confidential information related to the Firm’s business, or (ii) communicate with the press or other media about matters related to the Firm, its customers or employees, including matters and activities relating to your employment, or the employment of others, by the Firm, in the case of either (i) or (ii), except as explicitly permitted by the JPMorgan Chase Code of Conduct and applicable policies or law or legal process.
nodes.summary:
- Treatment of PSUs upon death:
  - If death occurs after the Performance Period, the beneficiary receives shares equal to all outstanding PSUs.
  - If death occurs during the Performance Period, the beneficiary receives shares based on:
    - Average performance for all completed calendar years,
    - Multiplied by one-third of the Target Award for each completed year,
    - Using a 100% Award Payout Percentage for any remaining, uncompleted calendar years.
  - Distribution timing: no later than the end of the calendar year following the year of death; administratively, shares are typically registered to the beneficiary or estate within 60 days after required documentation is received.

- Employee obligations in exchange for the award:
  - Non-solicitation of employees and customers:
    - Applies during employment and for the longer of (i) one year post-termination or (ii) three years from Grant Date if the award is not canceled at termination.
    - Prohibits soliciting or inducing Firm employees to leave, hiring recent Firm employees (with limited exceptions), and, to the extent enforceable, soliciting or diverting Firm customers, suppliers, or relationships known through employment. Excludes publicly known institutional customers serviced without using the Firm’s confidential information and authorized actions in the normal course of duties.
  - Confidentiality:
    - No use or disclosure of the Firm’s confidential information during or after employment; no media communications about Firm matters except as permitted by policy, law, or legal process.
    - No unauthorized post-termination access to the Firm’s internal systems.
    - “Confidential information” aligns with the JPMorgan Chase Code of Conduct.
    - Safe-harbor for reporting concerns to management, directors, government, regulators, self-regulatory bodies, attorneys, or courts, and for truthful legal/regulatory responses.
  - Non-disparagement:
    - No public statements intended or reasonably expected to disparage the Firm or its stakeholders, with carve-outs for lawful reporting and truthful cooperation with legal/regulatory inquiries.
  - Cooperation:
    - Obligation to cooperate fully and provide accurate information to the Firm and its counsel regarding audits, tax matters, litigation, investigations, or governmental proceedings.

- Additional referenced obligations (content not fully shown here): Compliance with Award Agreement and Notice Period.

nodes.title: Non-Disparagement
nodes.heading: 40.14.3 Non-Disparagement
nodes.start_phrase: You will not, either during your employment with the Firm or thereafter, make or encourage others to make any public statement or release any information in verbal, written, electronic or any other form, that is intended to, or reasonably could be foreseen to, disparage, embarrass or criticize the Firm or its employees, officers, directors or shareholders as a group.
nodes.summary:
- Describes PSU death benefits and payout timing:
  - If death occurs after the Performance Period, the beneficiary receives shares equal to all outstanding PSUs.
  - If death occurs during the Performance Period, payout is based on the average performance of completed calendar years, multiplied by one-third of the target PSUs for each completed year; remaining years are paid at 100% of target.
  - Shares are distributed no later than the end of the calendar year following the year of death; administratively, the firm aims to register shares to the beneficiary or estate within 60 days after receiving required documentation.

- Sets employee obligations tied to the award:
  - Non-solicitation of employees and customers:
    - Applies during employment and for the longer of (i) one year post-termination or (ii) three years from Grant Date if the award is not canceled at termination.
    - Prohibits soliciting or inducing firm employees to leave; hiring recent employees (with exceptions for job eliminations or if separated >6 months); and, to the fullest extent enforceable, soliciting or diverting current customers, suppliers, or other relationships known through employment. Exception for publicly known institutional customers served without using the firm’s confidential information.
    - Normal, authorized actions in the course of employment are not restricted.
  - Confidential information:
    - Prohibits using or disclosing the firm’s confidential information and communicating with the media about firm-related matters during and after employment, except as allowed by the Code of Conduct, law, or legal process.
    - Bars unauthorized post-termination access to internal systems; “confidential information” aligns with the Code of Conduct.
    - Carve-outs permit reporting suspected legal or Code violations to management, directors, regulators, government, self-regulatory agencies, attorneys, or courts, and truthful responses to lawful requests.
  - Non-disparagement:
    - Prohibits public statements intended or reasonably likely to disparage the firm or its stakeholders during or after employment, with the same legal/reporting carve-outs as above.
  - Cooperation:
    - Requires full cooperation and accurate information to the firm and its counsel in audits, tax matters, litigation, investigations, or governmental proceedings (section text is truncated).

- Notes that obligations regarding “Compliance with Award Agreement” and “Notice Period” are referenced but not detailed in this excerpt.

nodes.title: Cooperation
nodes.heading: 40.14.4 Cooperation
nodes.start_phrase: You will cooperate fully with and provide full and accurate information to the Firm and its counsel with respect to any matter (including any audit, tax proceeding, litigation, investigation or governmental proceeding) with respect to which you may have knowledge or information, subject to reimbursement for actual, appropriate and reasonable out-of-pocket expenses incurred by you.
nodes.summary:
- Death benefits for PSUs:
  - If death occurs after the Performance Period, the beneficiary receives shares equal to all outstanding PSUs.
  - If death occurs during the Performance Period, payout is based on the average performance of completed calendar years, multiplied by one-third of target PSUs for each completed year; remaining years assume a 100% Award Payout Percentage.
  - Shares are distributed no later than the end of the calendar year following the year of death; administratively, shares are typically registered to the beneficiary/estate within 60 days of receiving required documentation.

- Employee obligations tied to the award:
  - Non-solicitation of employees and customers:
    - Applies during employment and for the longer of (i) 1 year post-termination or (ii) 3 years from grant date if the award is not canceled at termination.
    - Prohibits soliciting or hiring certain current/former employees (with limited exceptions) and, to the fullest extent permitted by law, soliciting or diverting customers/suppliers you serviced or learned of through employment (excluding publicly known institutional customers serviced without using the Firm’s confidential information).
    - Does not restrict authorized, job-related actions per Firm policy.
  - Confidential information:
    - No use/disclosure of Firm confidential information or media communications about Firm matters during or after employment, except as allowed by policy, law, or legal process; no post-termination access to internal systems without authorization.
    - Preserves rights to report suspected legal or Code of Conduct violations and to cooperate truthfully with authorities.
  - Non-disparagement:
    - No public statements intended or reasonably expected to disparage the Firm or its people; exceptions for lawful reporting/cooperation.
  - Cooperation:
    - Ongoing duty to cooperate and provide accurate information in audits, litigation, investigations, and related matters, with reimbursement of reasonable out-of-pocket expenses.
  - Compliance with award agreement:
    - Provide requested compliance information; authorize the Firm to disclose award terms to affected third parties, including prospective employers.
  - Notice period:
    - If subject to a contractual/policy notice period, must give advance written notice; the Firm may require work or place you on paid leave during the period.
    - During the notice period, you must devote full time to the Firm, not work elsewhere, and will receive base salary and certain benefits; parties may agree to modify the notice length.
    - Regardless, a separate 180-day advance notice applies if invoking Full Career Eligibility.

- Remedies and enforcement:
  - Cancellation/recapture (up to 100% of outstanding PSUs and related dividend equivalents/calculated PSUs) may occur if the Firm determines:
    - Detrimental conduct causing material financial or reputational harm; award based on materially inaccurate metrics; material misrepresentation; improper/grossly negligent failure to identify/raise/assess material risks; termination for Cause or post-termination determination that Cause existed.
    - Failure to meet advance notice, cooperation, or employment restrictions tied to termination; failure to submit required Release/Certification forms on time; violation of “Your Obligations.”
  - Suspension rights:

nodes.title: Recovery
nodes.heading: 40.15.1 Recovery
nodes.start_phrase: In addition , you may be required to pay the Firm up to an amount equal to the Fair Market Value (determined as of the applicable vesting date or acceleration date) of the gross number of shares of Common Stock previously distributed, including vested shares subject to the Holding Requirements, under this award as follows:
nodes.summary:
- Compliance and disclosure: Employee must provide information to confirm compliance with the Award Agreement and authorizes the firm to disclose the agreement’s terms to affected third parties, including prospective employers. Reasonable out-of-pocket expenses for cooperation may be reimbursed.
- Notice Period obligations: If subject to a contractual or policy-based notice period, the employee must give the required advance written notice as consideration for the award and continued employment. The firm may require continued service or place the employee on paid leave during the notice period. During this period, the employee must devote full time and loyalty to the firm, not work for another employer, and will receive base salary and certain benefits. The notice period may be mutually waived/modified. A separate 180-day advance notice applies for “Full Career Eligibility” terminations.
- Remedies—cancellation/recapture: Up to 100% of outstanding PSUs (including reinvested dividend equivalent units and calculated PSUs) may be canceled at the firm’s discretion for:
  - Detrimental or risk-related conduct causing material financial or reputational harm;
  - Awards based on materially inaccurate performance metrics (regardless of responsibility) or employee misrepresentation;
  - Failure to identify/raise/assess material risks as expected;
  - Termination for Cause or post-termination determination that Cause existed;
  - Failure to meet advance notice/cooperation or employment restrictions;
  - Failure to return required Release/Certification forms by the deadline;
  - Violations of “Your Obligations.”
- Suspension rights: The firm may suspend vesting and/or share distributions while evaluating cancellation, recovery, or distribution conditions; it is not responsible for price fluctuations during suspension. Suspended units, if applicable, are reinstated per plan procedures.
- Remedies—recovery/clawback: The firm may require repayment up to the fair market value of gross shares previously distributed (including those subject to holding requirements):
  - For shares distributed within three years prior to notice-of-recovery if there was fraud, knowing and willful misconduct, violations of “Your Obligations,” or post-termination violations of “Full Career Eligibility” or “Government Office” restrictions.
  - For shares distributed within one year prior to notice-of-recovery for specified detrimental/risk-related conduct.
  - Notice-of-recovery may be electronic and sent to the last known address and preserves the firm’s rights during evaluation.
  - Recovery applies to shares distributed, including shares withheld for taxes, but the firm intends not to seek amounts tied to irrevocable, non-recoverable tax withholdings/payments. Repayment may be in shares or cash and is not a penalty. Other recoupment policies (e.g., Bonus Recoupment; EMEA Malus and Clawback for Identified Staff) remain unaffected.
- Injunctive relief: The firm may obtain an injunction to prevent or stop violations of these obligations, in addition to other legal or equitable remedies.
- Administrative provisions:
  - Withholding taxes: The firm may withhold shares, sell shares to cover taxes, withhold from cash compensation, or retain vested shares until taxes are paid to authorities.
  - Right to set off: Subject to law (including Section 409A), the firm may retain funds or shares from vesting to satisfy debts owed to the firm. It will not recover from funds or unrestricted securities in the employee’s individual firm accounts without consent, except as permitted under accounts referenced in “No Ownership Rights/Other Limitations.”
  - No ownership rights/other limitations: PSUs do not confer ownership or voting rights. Shares are issued only after PSUs are determined and vested, following firm procedures. The employee authorizes the firm to open a brokerage/book-entry account to deliver vested shares. The section notes implications if cancellation provisions apply (text truncated).

nodes.title: Right to an Injunction
nodes.heading: 40.15.2 Right to an Injunction
nodes.start_phrase: You acknowledge that a violation or attempted violation of the obligations set forth herein will cause immediate and irreparable damage to the Firm, and therefore agree that the Firm shall be entitled as a matter of right to an injunction, from any court of competent jurisdiction, restraining any violation or further violation of such obligations; such right to an injunction, however, shall be cumulative and in addition to whatever other remedies the Firm may have under law or equity.
nodes.summary:
- Clawback/recapture: The firm may require repayment of award value if you commit fraud, willful misconduct, violate “Your Obligations,” or breach post-termination restrictions (“Full Career Eligibility” or “Government Office”). It may also seek repayment for shares distributed within one year prior to a notice-of-recovery for detrimental or risk-related conduct referenced elsewhere.
- Notice-of-recovery: Defined as written (including electronic) notice to your last known address; notice that the firm is evaluating recovery preserves its rights and does not obligate the firm to complete the evaluation.
- Tax treatment in recovery: “Shares distributed” include shares withheld for taxes, but the intent is to seek repayment only for shares/value you retain; amounts representing irrevocable tax withholdings/payments that cannot be reclaimed will not be required to be repaid, as determined by the firm or its nominee.
- Repayment form and characterization: Repayment may be made in cash or shares and is deemed a lawful recovery, not a penalty. Obligations under “Bonus Recoupment” and “EMEA Malus and Clawback Policy - Identified Staff” remain unaffected.
- Injunctive relief: The firm can seek an injunction for violations, in addition to other legal or equitable remedies.
- Administrative provisions:
  - Withholding taxes: The firm may retain shares, sell shares, withhold from cash compensation, or hold vested shares until taxes are paid to satisfy tax obligations.
  - Right to set-off: Subject to law (including Section 409A), the firm may retain funds or stock from vesting to satisfy debts you owe, but will not use funds or unrestricted securities in your name held at the firm without your consent, except for certain accounts referenced in “No Ownership Rights/Other Limitations.”
  - No ownership rights: PSUs confer no ownership or voting rights until determined and vested; shares are issued per firm procedures. By accepting the award, you authorize the firm to open a brokerage or book-entry account to deliver vested shares. The section ends noting potential application of cancellation provisions.

nodes.title: Administrative Provisions
nodes.heading: 40.16 Administrative Provisions
nodes.start_phrase: Withholding Taxes: As a result of legal and/or tax obligations the Firm, in its sole discretion, may (i) retain from each distribution the number of shares of Common Stock required to satisfy applicable tax obligations or (ii) implement any other desirable or necessary procedures, so that appropriate withholding and other taxes are paid to the competent authorities with respect to the vested shares and the award.
nodes.summary:
- Clawback/recapture triggers: repayment or cancellation may be required if you commit fraud, willful misconduct, violate “Your Obligations,” or breach post-employment restrictions (“Full Career Eligibility” or “Government Office”), including detrimental or risk-related conduct.
- One-year lookback: the Firm may require repayment for shares distributed within the year prior to a notice-of-recovery tied to such conduct.
- Notice-of-recovery: written (including electronic) notice to your last known address; notice that the Firm is evaluating recovery preserves its full rights without any obligation to complete the evaluation.
- Tax treatment in recovery: “shares distributed” includes shares withheld for taxes, but the Firm intends not to seek repayment for irrevocable tax withholdings/payments you cannot recover; the Firm/its nominee determines the amount represented by such taxes.
- Repayment form and characterization: repayment may be made in shares or cash and is deemed a lawful recovery, not a penalty; obligations under “Bonus Recoupment” and “EMEA Malus & Clawback Policy – Identified Staff” remain unaffected.
- Injunctive relief: the Firm can obtain an injunction for violations or attempted violations of obligations, in addition to other legal or equitable remedies.
- Tax withholding mechanics: the Firm may satisfy tax obligations by retaining vested shares, selling shares to cover taxes, withholding from cash compensation, or holding vested shares until you pay required taxes.
- Right to set-off: subject to law (including Section 409A), the Firm may retain funds or shares from vesting to satisfy debts you owe; it will not recover amounts from your funds or unrestricted securities held at the Firm without your consent, except for certain award-related accounts referenced below.
- No ownership rights until issuance: PSUs don’t convey stock ownership or voting rights until PSUs are determined and vest; the Firm may open a brokerage/book-entry account to deliver vested shares; PSUs can be canceled if cancellation provisions apply during suspended vesting.
- Post-vesting share restrictions: the Firm may temporarily restrict sale, transfer, pledging, assignment, hedging, or encumbrance of issued shares; these restrictions do not affect voting or dividend rights; if recovery applies during a restriction period, you may owe up to the fair market value of the gross restricted shares.
- Successors: the Award Agreement binds JPMorgan Chase’s successors.
- Employment status: the award is not an employment contract; employment is at-will; no right to future awards; award value does not count for severance.
- Section 409A compliance: the award is intended to comply with 409A; for specified employees, distributions triggered by separation may be delayed six months; payment timing rules for vested portions are defined.
- Corporate actions: equitable adjustments to PSUs/shares may be made for stock splits, dividends, recapitalizations, mergers, spin-offs, or similar events.
- Other equitable adjustments: excluding the “Qualitative Performance Factor,” the Committee may adjust the award up or down to preserve intended economics given unusual events, accounting changes, regulatory capital changes, or similar circumstances.
- Interpretation and administration: the Committee has sole authority to interpret the Plan/Award, determine employment termination reasons, apply post-employment, cancellation, and recovery provisions, decide claims, and delegate authority; determinations need not be uniform and may be selective.

nodes.title: Interpretation/Administration
nodes.heading: 40.17 Interpretation/Administration
nodes.start_phrase: The Committee has sole and complete authority to interpret and administer this Award Agreement, including, without limitation, the power to (i) interpret the Plan and the terms of this Award Agreement; (ii) determine the reason for termination of employment; (iii) determine application of the post-employment obligations and cancellation and recovery provisions; (iv) decide all claims arising with respect to this award; and (v) delegate such authority as it deems appropriate.
nodes.summary:
- PSU cancellation: If vesting is suspended, outstanding PSUs may be cancelled in whole or part, with references to protection-based vesting, qualitative performance factor, bonus recoupment, EMEA malus and clawback, termination, remedies, and amendment provisions.
- Post-vesting stock restrictions: On any vesting date, the firm may impose discretionary restrictions on issued common stock (e.g., sale, transfer, pledge, assignment, hedging, encumbrance) without affecting voting or dividend rights.
- Recovery/recoupment: If recovery provisions apply during a restriction period, the recipient may be required to repay up to the fair market value (at vest date) of the gross restricted shares, notwithstanding right-to-set-off limits; references to bonus recoupment and remedies.
- Binding effect: The Award Agreement binds successors to JPMorgan Chase.
- Employment status: The Award Agreement is not an employment contract; employment is at-will; no right to future or similar awards; award value is excluded from severance calculations.
- Section 409A compliance: Intended to comply with Section 409A; if a “specified employee” separates from service and the award is deferred compensation, delivery is delayed until the first month after six full months post-separation; if no substantial risk of forfeiture remains, the remainder of each calendar year after each vesting date is a payment date for distributing vested portions.
- Corporate actions: Equitable substitutions/adjustments for changes in outstanding shares (e.g., stock splits, mergers, spin-offs, recapitalizations, special distributions).
- Other equitable adjustments: Committee may adjust awards (up or down), excluding the Qualitative Performance Factor, to preserve intended economics for unusual/non-recurring events, accounting changes, regulatory capital structure changes, or other appropriate circumstances.
- Interpretation and administration: The Committee has sole authority to interpret the Plan/Award Agreement, determine termination reasons, apply post-employment, cancellation, and recovery provisions, decide claims, and delegate authority; determinations are binding.
- Non-uniform treatment: Determinations and modifications under the Plan/Award Agreements may be non-uniform and selective across participants.

nodes.title: Amendment

The accelerated share count is determined using the “Death” methodology. The Firm may also waive holding periods for already vested shares if required. Despite acceleration or waiver, all repayment obligations and employment restrictions (e.g., “Protection-Based Vesting,” “Government Office Requirements,” “Full Career Eligibility”) continue as if vesting occurred on the original schedule.

Where allowed, the recipient may revoke this authorization (excluding required legal/tax reporting), but doing so cancels the award.
- Governing law: New York law applies.
- Choice of forum/arbitration: Disputes related to the award or Plan may be required to go to arbitration under AAA rules if the Firm elects; otherwise, exclusive jurisdiction and venue lie with the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York. The recipient waives objections to personal jurisdiction/venue and agrees not to file elsewhere.

Where allowed by law, authorization may be terminated (not for tax/regulatory reporting or other legal obligations), but doing so will result in award cancellation.

nodes.title: Choice of Forum
nodes.heading: 40.23 Choice of Forum

- Amendment: The Committee may amend the Award Agreement at any time for any reason, provided no material adverse effect on the participant’s rights occurs without consent, except as needed to comply with laws/regulatory/accounting changes, adjust vesting schedules, or impose specified restrictions, subject to Section 409A. Any amendment must be in writing signed by JPMorgan Chase’s Director of Human Resources.

Recovery periods remain tied to original vesting or distribution dates.
- Scope of Acceleration After Termination: 
  - If voluntarily terminated and the “Government Office Requirements” are met, acceleration applies only to the portion that would have continued to vest.
  - For terminations where awards remain outstanding due to “Job Elimination” or “Full Career Eligibility,” acceleration may apply to the full outstanding award.
  - The number of shares upon acceleration is calculated as under the “Death” section.
  - The Firm may waive the holding period for vested shares if divestiture is required.
  - Despite acceleration or waiver, all Award Agreement obligations continue as if vesting occurred on schedule, including repayment (“Remedies”) and restrictions under “Protection-Based Vesting,” “Government Office Requirements,” and “Full Career Eligibility.”
- Use of Personal Data: Acceptance authorizes the Firm to process and share personal data (including with service providers and tax/regulatory authorities) and to transfer data cross-border even to jurisdictions with lesser protections. Where allowed, participants may revoke authorization (not for tax/regulatory obligations); revocation results in award cancellation.
- Governing Law: New York law governs.

If not arbitrable, the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York has exclusive jurisdiction and venue; participants waive objections to personal jurisdiction and venue and agree not to file elsewhere.
- Waiver of Jury Trial/Class Claims: Participants waive the right to a jury trial and (as indicated by the heading) class claims; the provision is partially excerpted in the text provided.

nodes.title: Waiver of Jury Trial/Class Claims
nodes.heading: 40.24 Waiver of Jury Trial/Class Claims

nodes.summary:
- Amendment: The Committee (or nominee) can amend the Award Agreement at any time for any reason, but not in a way that materially adversely affects the participant without consent, except to comply with laws/regulations/accounting changes or to adjust vesting dates/impose stated restrictions, subject to Section 409A. Amendments must be in writing signed by JPMorgan Chase’s Director of Human Resources.
- Severability: Unenforceable provisions may be reformed by the Firm, a court/arbitrator, or the Director of HR (e.g., duration, geography, scope) to make them enforceable under applicable law.
- Accelerated Distribution for ethics/conflict due to government employment: The Firm may accelerate distribution and waive the holding requirement when required by applicable ethics or conflict-of-interest laws, provided no Section 409A violation. Recovery periods are based on original vesting/distribution dates. Applies proportionally after voluntary termination meeting “Government Office Requirements,” or fully if outstanding due to “Job Elimination” or “Full Career Eligibility.” Shares on acceleration are determined using the “Death” methodology. Holding requirements on already vested shares may be waived if required. Despite acceleration/waiver, all award obligations remain, including Remedies, Protection-Based Vesting, Government Office Requirements, and Full Career Eligibility.
- Use of Personal Data: Acceptance authorizes the Firm to process and transfer personal data (including to third parties and across borders with potentially lower protections) for award administration and regulatory/tax purposes. Authorization can be terminated (except for legal/regulatory obligations), but termination cancels the award.
- Governing Law: New York law applies, without regard to conflicts principles.
- Choice of Forum: Disputes may be compelled to AAA arbitration at the Firm’s discretion; otherwise, exclusive jurisdiction/venue is the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York. Participant waives objections to jurisdiction/venue and agrees not to sue elsewhere.
- Waiver of Jury Trial/Class Claims: Participant waives jury trial and agrees all claims will be pursued individually (no class, collective, or representative actions).
- Litigation: If the Firm prevails in enforcing the Award Agreement, it may recover reasonable attorneys’ fees/expenses. Participant waives advancement of fees and indemnification under the Firm’s by-laws for such suits.
- Non-transferability: Awards and related rights cannot be assigned, pledged, transferred, hedged, hypothecated, or subjected to liens; transfer is permitted after death by will, descent, or designated beneficiary.
- Key definitions:
  - Average Tangible Common Equity: Annual average common equity less goodwill and identifiable intangibles, calculated using quarterly (or year-end if unavailable) balances; used solely for Performance Ranking.
  - Award Payout Percentage: The percentage tied to the Performance Table.
  - Calculated PSUs: Target Award Number (after any cancellation) multiplied by the Award Payout Percentage based on three-year average performance; subject to override if average Firm Reported ROTCE is at/above or below specified thresholds; cancellations reduce the target; rounding for public reporting is not applied.
  - Calculation Agent: An independent third party (e.g., accounting/consulting firm) retained by the HR Director or delegate.
  - Cause: Includes legal/regulatory violations, felony indictment/conviction, fraud, material policy/Code of Conduct violations or misconduct, grossly inadequate performance or failure to follow directives, and acts/omissions injurious to the Firm or its relationships.
  - Financial Services Company: Broadly defined to include banking, insurance, financial/investment/economic advisory (e.g., investment banking, brokerage, asset management, FX, hedge funds), securitization/derivatives, fintech (e.g., blockchain, financial products/services), private equity/real estate advising/investing, and other similar activities as determined by HR.
  - Firm Reported ROTCE: The Firm’s annual return on tangible common equity as reported in public year-end disclosures, without rounding conventions.

nodes.title: Non-transferability

nodes.title: Definitions
nodes.heading: 40.27 Definitions
nodes.start_phrase: “Average Tangible Common Equity” means annual average common stockholders’ equity less annual average goodwill and annual average identifiable intangible assets.
nodes.summary:
- Dispute and litigation terms:
  - All claims must be brought on an individual basis; you waive participation in class, collective, or other representative actions.
  - In Firm-initiated actions to enforce the Award Agreement where the Firm prevails, the Firm may recover its reasonable attorneys’ fees and expenses.
  - You agree not to seek advancement of fees or indemnification under the Firm’s by-laws in such suits.

- Transfer restrictions:
  - Awards (including RSUs and PSUs) and related rights may not be assigned, pledged, transferred, hedged, or otherwise encumbered.
  - Transfer is allowed only upon death via will, laws of descent, or a beneficiary designation on file.

- Core performance share unit (PSU) framework and calculations:
  - Target Award Number: the baseline number of PSUs designated in the Award Agreement; reduced by any cancellations.
  - Performance Period: a specified three-calendar-year span.
  - Firm Reported ROTCE and Average Tangible Common Equity (ATCE) defined and used solely for Performance Ranking; ROTCE recalculated if financials are restated.
  - Calculated PSUs: Target Award Number multiplied by an Award Payout Percentage tied to the Firm’s three-year average ROTCE ranking versus a defined peer set (“Performance Companies”).
  - Award Payout mechanics:
    - Performance Table maps absolute ROTCE levels and relative ROTCE rankings to specific payout percentages.
    - Substitution rules apply if the Firm’s average ROTCE meets/exceeds an upper threshold or falls below a lower threshold.
    - Tie-handling rules clarify how equal rankings affect payout determinations.
  - Independent Calculation Agent (not owned/controlled by the Firm) may be retained to perform calculations.

- Financial thresholds:
  - Firmwide Financial Threshold: a minimum cumulative ROTCE over the three-year period (formula specified).
  - Line of Business (LOB) Financial Thresholds:
    - Thresholds defined primarily as annual negative pre-tax pre-provision income or pre-tax pre-loan loss reserve income, depending on LOB.
    - Applies to AWM, Card & Auto, Commercial Banking, CIB (overall or specified products excluding XVA), Consumer/Wealth/Business Banking, Corporate Functions (including CIO), and Home Lending.
    - Clarifies definitions of pre-tax pre-provision income and pre-tax pre-loan loss reserve income.
  - Corporate Functions (including CIO) treated as a single LOB.

- Peer group governance:
  - “Performance Companies” are peers with business mixes overlapping the Firm’s; the Committee may adjust the list prospectively for mergers, spin-offs, business mix changes, or cessation.

- Employment and eligibility definitions:
  - Cause: includes legal/regulatory violations, felony indictment/conviction, fraud, Code of Conduct/policy violations, grossly inadequate performance or refusal to follow directives, and acts injurious to the Firm’s interests.
  - Recognized Service: as defined in Firm policies.

- Sector and role definitions:
  - Financial Services Company: broadly defined to include banking, insurance, advisory, brokerage, asset management, FX, payment processing, securitization, fintech (including blockchain/financial products), private equity/real estate, and similar activities per HR discretion.
  - Not-for-Profit Organization: 501(c)(3) entities or foreign equivalents with identical purposes.
  - Government Office: full-time elected/appointed roles not expected to be full career, or bona fide full-time campaigns after formal filing.

- Administrative notes:
  - Many percentages, years, firms, and rankings are placeholders to be filled in the Award Agreement.
  - Calculations and definitions are expressly for determining PSU payouts and Performance Ranking.

nodes.title: Government Office Requirements
nodes.heading: 40.28 Government Office Requirements
nodes.start_phrase: You may be eligible to continue vesting in all or part of your award if you voluntarily resign to accept a Government Office (as defined above) or to become a candidate for an elective Government Office.
nodes.summary:
- Purpose: Outlines conditions under which an employee who resigns to accept or run for a Government Office may continue vesting in all or part of an equity award.
- Full Career Eligibility carve‑out: The section does not apply if the employee qualifies for “Full Career Eligibility” at the time of resignation.
- Eligibility requirements:
  - Provide at least 60 days’ advance written notice of intent to accept/pursue a Government Office; remain cooperative, perform requested services, and do not work for another employer during the notice period (Firm may shorten the period).
  - Provide confirmation that continued vesting complies with applicable laws, regulations, and rules.
  - Provide satisfactory documentation that the resignation is to accept or run for a Government Office.
- Portion eligible for continued vesting (CV Award), based on continuous service immediately before termination:
  - 50% with ≥3 and <4 years,
  - 75% with ≥4 and <5 years,
  - 100% with ≥5 years.
  - The non‑eligible portion is cancelled at termination.
- Conditions for continued vesting:
  - Non‑elective office: Must remain in that office for 2+ years after termination; if the office term is under 2 years, eligibility applies if a vesting date occurs during the government service.
  - Elective office: The employee’s name must appear on the primary or final public ballot. If not elected, employment restrictions apply as referenced.
  - All original performance and protection‑based vesting conditions continue to apply to the CV Award.
- Satisfaction of conditions:
  - If government service ends 2+ years post‑termination, or if the employee appears on the ballot but is not elected, any then‑outstanding CV Awards (and those that would have been outstanding but for an ethics/conflict‑driven accelerated distribution) continue for the remainder of the vesting period under the same terms as if the employee resigned with Full Career Eligibility, including employment restrictions.
- Failure to satisfy conditions:
  - Outstanding PSUs under the CV Award are cancelled.
  - Clawback: The employee must repay the Fair Market Value of shares previously distributed early (due to ethics/conflict reasons tied to government employment) that would otherwise have been outstanding PSUs on the failure date; FMV measured on the original distribution date.
- Cross‑references:
  - Definitions of Government Office and related terms.
  - Accelerated distribution rules for ethics or conflict reasons from government employment.
  - Employment restrictions applicable during the vesting period.

nodes.start_phrase: While there are a number of subsidiaries that are required to be reported for various purposes to bank regulators, the following is a list of JPMorgan Chase & Co.’s significant legal entity subsidiaries as of D e c e m b e r 3 1 , 2 0 2 2, as defined by SEC rules.
nodes.summary: The partial document presents Exhibit 21, outlining JPMorgan Chase & Co.’s significant legal entity subsidiaries as of December 31, 2022, as defined by SEC rules. It explains inclusion criteria (parent entities of significant subsidiaries and certain material legal entities designated for Dodd-Frank resolution planning) and exclusions (subsidiaries that are not significant in aggregate). It then lists selected major subsidiaries and their jurisdictions across the United States, United Kingdom, Germany, Japan, India, and Luxembourg, including JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A.; J.P. Morgan Securities entities; asset management entities; Paymentech; and various holding and services companies. Exhibit 22.2 discloses that JPMorgan Chase Financial Company LLC issues Global Medium-Term Notes, Series A, under a 2016 indenture, which are fully and unconditionally guaranteed by JPMorgan Chase & Co., and are offered under an effective Form S-3 registration (Nos. 333-236659 and 333-236659-01) declared effective on April 8, 2020.

James Dimon certifies the Form 10-K was reviewed; contains no material misstatements or omissions; fairly presents financial condition, results, and cash flows; and that management designed, maintained, and evaluated disclosure controls and procedures and internal control over financial reporting. nodes.title: CERTIFICATION
nodes.heading: Exhibit 31.1 JPMorgan Chase & Co. CERTIFICATION
nodes.start_phrase: 1. I have reviewed this Annual Report on Form 10-K of JPMorgan Chase & Co.;
nodes.summary:
- Exhibits 31.1 and 31.2 of JPMorgan Chase & Co.’s Form 10-K contain Sarbanes-Oxley Section 302 certifications by CEO James Dimon and CFO Jeremy Barnum, dated February 21, 2023.
- Both officers certify they have reviewed the 10-K; it contains no untrue statements or material omissions; and the financial statements fairly present, in all material respects, the company’s financial condition, results of operations, and cash flows for the periods presented.
- They state responsibility for establishing and maintaining disclosure controls and procedures and internal control over financial reporting (ICFR); that such controls were designed under their supervision; that the effectiveness of disclosure controls was evaluated as of period-end; and that any changes in ICFR during the most recent fiscal quarter that materially affected or are likely to materially affect ICFR were disclosed.
- They confirm disclosure to the auditors and audit committee of all significant deficiencies and material weaknesses in ICFR, and any fraud (whether or not material) involving management or employees with significant ICFR roles.
- Signatures and titles: James Dimon, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer; Jeremy Barnum, Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer.

nodes.title: CERTIFICATION
nodes.heading: Exhibit 31.2 JPMorgan Chase & Co. CERTIFICATION
nodes.start_phrase: 1. I have reviewed this Annual Report on Form 10-K of JPMorgan Chase & Co.;
nodes.summary:
- The excerpt contains Exhibits 31.2 and 32 to JPMorgan Chase & Co.’s Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2022.
- Exhibit 31.2: Section 302 certification by CFO Jeremy Barnum (dated February 21, 2023) stating:
  - He reviewed the 10-K.
  - The report contains no material misstatements or omissions.
  - The financial statements and other financial information fairly present the company’s financial condition, results of operations, and cash flows.
  - He and the other certifying officer are responsible for disclosure controls and procedures and internal control over financial reporting, including:
    - Designing and supervising these controls to ensure material information is known to management.
    - Providing reasonable assurance over reliability of financial reporting and GAAP compliance.
    - Evaluating effectiveness of disclosure controls and reporting conclusions.
    - Disclosing any material changes in internal control over financial reporting in the most recent quarter.
  - They have disclosed to auditors and the audit committee:
    - All significant deficiencies and material weaknesses in internal control over financial reporting.
    - Any fraud involving management or key employees related to financial reporting.
- Exhibit 32: Section 906 certification under 18 U.S.C. §1350 by CEO James Dimon and CFO Jeremy Barnum (dated February 21, 2023) affirming:
  - The 10-K complies with Section 13(a) or 15(d) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934.
  - The report fairly presents, in all material respects, JPMorgan Chase & Co.’s financial condition and results of operations.
  - The certification is furnished (not filed) for Exchange Act Section 18 purposes, and original signed statements are retained by the company and will be provided to the SEC upon request.

nodes.title: CERTIFICATION PURSUANT TO 18 U.S.C. SECTION 1350, AS ADOPTED PURSUANT TO SECTION 906 OF THE SARBANES-OXLEY ACT OF 2002
nodes.heading: Exhibit 32 JPMorgan Chase & Co. CERTIFICATION PURSUANT TO 18 U.S.C. SECTION 1350, AS ADOPTED PURSUANT TO SECTION 906 OF THE SARBANES-OXLEY ACT OF 2002
nodes.start_phrase: 1. The Report fully complies with the requirements of Section 13(a) or 15(d) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934; and
nodes.summary: Exhibit 32 is a Sarbanes-Oxley Section 906 (18 U.S.C. §1350) certification for JPMorgan Chase & Co.’s Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2022. CEO James Dimon and CFO Jeremy Barnum, both dated February 21, 2023, certify that the 10-K complies with Exchange Act Sections 13(a) or 15(d) and that it fairly presents, in all material respects, the company’s financial condition and results of operations. The certification accompanies the Annual Report, is not deemed “filed” under Section 18 of the Exchange Act, and the signed original is retained by the company and available to the SEC upon request.
